Collections :

Collections pour tags :

  • epic superlourds TYRANIDES Tyranides-dominatrix NONDL NONSUP

Description :

1

Unlike the Hive Tyrant, which functions as a battlefield general, the Regina Monstrum is a living extension of the Hive Mind’s cold, starving ego. Where it treads, the ground does not merely shake; it curdles, responding to the overwhelming psychic pressure radiating from the creature’s pulsating, semi-exposed brain-vault. It is a biological paradox—a siege engine of impossible mass that moves with the sickening grace of a predatory insect. Its primary dorsal cannon is not a weapon in the traditional sense, but a specialized birthing canal for hyper-accelerated, corrosive spores that dissolve ferro-crete and bone alike in a matter of seconds. To look upon the Regina Monstrum is to see the inevitable end of the evolutionary ladder: a queen that does not rule through loyalty or fear, but through a synaptic tether so absolute that every creature in its shadow becomes merely a finger on its many-clawed hand. When a world falls, it is often the last thing the survivors see—a towering, chitinous monument to the fact that the universe does not care for their gods, only for their biomass.

These are a 40x20mm base for troops and 25mm round base for characters, both with indents to accomodate strip bases. They have sloped edges on their lower halve, so you can pick them up more easily.

Intended for resin printing or FDM printing with water-soluble supports.

You can fit up to two Ø 3x1mm neodym magnets on the underside. The holes should be pretty tight and only need glue to hold the magnets. They still have a bit of wiggle room though, in case your material shrinks during printing.

Well, I thought I will just check how a cannon crew would look like, and then I got carried away. It was so satisfying to do these little dwarfs, that I neglected my other hobbie. I might focus on those on the weekend then instead of modeling.

So this kit includes two different carriages (different wheel variants), seven barrel alternatives (though number four is actually the original empire one), and nine crewmen. I only planned six of those, without the imperial looking ones, but - as mentioned above - I got carried away. And they already had some very nice miniatures to work with. Also most of my Warhammer cannons have those crewmen.

I also added the siege bombard accessories here as well, they fit the model perfectly, I think.

Three dragon miniatures inspired by Blue Dragon, Forest Dragon and Baby Dragon styles. One huge adult dragon, one medium forest dragon and one smaller young drake, plus a scenic egg cluster.

Models included

Blue Dragon – large dragon on a 75–100mm round base. Body slightly coiled, wings half-spread, long neck arched with head lowered in a threatening pose. Horns swept back, scales sharp and angular. Base with rocky outcrop and cracked ground.

Forest Dragon – medium dragon perched on a fallen tree trunk crossing the base. Wings partially folded, tail curving around the log. Head turned to the side, antler-like horns and leafy frills along the neck. Roots and mushrooms on the base.

Young Dragon – small, compact dragon standing on a 40mm base. Wings folded close to the body, head slightly raised as if curious. Shorter horns, smoother scales. Simple rocky base.

Dragon Egg Cluster – scenic piece with three large dragon eggs partially embedded in rock, sized for a 30–40mm base; can be used as an objective or terrain.

They can easily represent the base variant of the 10 Ton [Flatbed Truck](https://www.sarna.net/wiki/Flatbed_Truck). Great for convoy escort missions or just as scatter terrain!

This was a fun little model - the Doomguard Rot Blade. It's a CR6 with a very nasty ability that, on kill, turns a creature and their non-magic items to ash. This is pretty brutal. Now I'm not sure on the ruling if that negates death saving throws as well but regardless it's nasty.

👍 Don't forget to Like and Collect this, so you can easily find it later! ⭐
If you like my models and what I do then come follow me on Patreon https://www.patreon.com/c/Adamnant for updates on my quests and access to exclusive minis.

This started as an AI model that I posed and sculpted, added spears, sword and helmet to. The helmet was something I had to kinda make from scratch. I think it looks pretty good. Here is a full video of my work on this model: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=xc8zzAErLSc

There are 3x variants of this mini. One with a pointing pose, one two-handed sword attack pose and one javelin throwing pose.

For printing I think the large version will be fine on FDM but like my previous model you'll want to be mindful of the spear. There are a few small surfaces and horns so it could be a bit of pain when removing supports on FDM but I believe in you! Just make sure to rotate the model so that supports aren't wrapped around the spear and you should be good. For resin I think auto-supports will work completely fine - just tilt it back 45 degrees.

I've completed my quest for 1000 models in 2025 so now I'm trying to decide whats next. Technically changelings can take any shape or form so maybe this one works too. Aside from that there doesn't seem to be much for what changelings should look like in their unchanged form.

This is the Basic Raptor, a free demonstration build of mine in 28mm/1-56th scale that I have shrunk to a quarter of its regular size for games of New Epic, AT-18, and other similar games.

These are tiny pieces. Some weapon barrels are as thin as support structures. Turn back. Down this road, madness awaits.

Take great care in post-processing. Print multiples, in case you snap something. Use heat to loosen supports before you try and free the objects. Use a soft toothbrush and light strokes when cleaning.

Otherwise, these take about 14 or 15 grams of material. You can make a few mistakes, since a kilogram bottle of resin contains potentially 66 or more Tiny Terrors.

Join my Discord to show off your little guys.
 https://discord.gg/7PyEqpkARb

Of join my Patreon at www.patreon.com/johnbearross to get discounts on my paid files, and support my caffeine habit.

Enjoy!

Best,
John Bear Ross

The Ruzisa Pattern Void Yacht is a luxurious, heavily customized reinterpretation of the Imperial Light Cruiser – Geonus II Pattern, repurposed not for war, but for status, prestige, and interstellar presence. Designed for use by planetary governors, noble dynasties, and high-ranking Rogue Traders, these ships are symbols of wealth, power, and refined taste within the Imperium.

While it retains elements of the original cruiser’s silhouette, the Ruzisa Pattern strips away most of its military infrastructure in favor of ornate architecture, custom superstructures, and ceremonial void chapels. The hull is reworked with lavish interiors, towering galleries, personal spires, arboretums, and frescoed observation domes—each vessel becoming a unique, spacefaring masterpiece.

Defensive capabilities remain: void shields and automated turrets provide a respectable level of protection, though the Ruzisa is not designed to endure the rigors of frontline conflict. Its most defining feature, however, is its colossal sub-light propulsion ring, a rare and fragile system that encircles its primary engine. This allows the yacht to achieve extraordinary cruising speeds, gliding through voidspace with unmatched smoothness. The cost and delicacy of this propulsion method prevent its use in most military contexts, but for a civilian vessel built to stay clear of danger and move with grace, it is ideal.

Each Ruzisa is custom-built, and no two are alike. Their baroque hulls may carry heraldry, relic vaults, or entire entourages of retainers, artists, or private militias. They are palaces with engines, and they serve their masters not only as ships—but as thrones among the stars.

Miniature Specs:
Length: 9,9 cm
Mounting: 3 mm

📡 Follow @j.p.m.designs for more elite voidcraft, Rogue Trader assets, and one-of-a-kind ships worthy of the God-Emperor’s most favored children.

Collectable figure from Lilo & Stitch. Figure 07: rap.

On planet Turo, Dr. Jumba Jookiba is convicted by the United Galactic Federation of illegal genetic experimentation, for creating an aggressive, near-indestructible creature with advanced learning capabilities called Experiment 626. Jumba is imprisoned, while 626 is exiled for his destructive behavior. However, 626 escapes by stealing a police cruiser and using its hyperdrive to reach Earth, crashing on Kauaʻi. The Grand Councilwoman offers Jumba freedom if he recaptures 626, pairing him with Earth expert, Agent Pleakley. 626 crashes near a wedding reception and is run over by a tourist trolley before being taken to an animal shelter.

A Hawaiian girl named Lilo Pelekai is expelled from hula school for pushing her bully Mertle off stage due to frustration over her sister Nani's absence. Their social worker, Mrs. Kekoa, visits and finds Nani unfit to care for Lilo, demanding she complete her tasks in a week.

The next day, having heard that Lilo wants a friend, their neighbor Tūtū takes Lilo to the animal shelter where 626 is kept. Realizing Jumba and Pleakley are after him, 626 impersonates as a dog and allows Lilo to adopt him for his protection. Nani takes them to her resort lūʻau job with her friend David Kawena. Lilo names 626 "Stitch" after Nani comments on having to stitch a car seat he tore. They enjoy the resort, but Stitch accidentally causes a table fire, leading to Nani's dismissal.

Nani is visited by Kekoa and Cobra Bubbles, a CIA agent posing as Kekoa's social director to investigate Stitch's arrival. Kekoa insists that Nani find new employment immediately. However, she is rejected after many interviews due to Lilo and Stitch's antics. Lilo helps Nani secure a job as a surfing instructor, and they enjoy surfing after her first shift. Meanwhile, Jumba and Pleakley fail to capture Stitch while jet skiing, causing the Pelekais and Stitch to wipe out, almost drowning Lilo when Stitch sinks.

After Lilo's recovery, Kekoa informs Nani that the Hawaiian government will cover her health insurance costs if she relinquishes her guardianship—a decision she reluctantly accepts. As the sisters share a final night together, Stitch reflects on his actions and forlornly returns to the animal shelter alone. Meanwhile, the Grand Councilwoman, frustrated with Jumba's failure to capture Stitch, cancels their deal and orders Pleakley to return Jumba to prison. However, Jumba escapes Pleakley and plans to capture Stitch instead.

Kekoa and Bubbles arrive the next morning to find that Lilo is missing, so they and Nani start searching for her. Lilo finds Stitch at the shelter, but Jumba arrives to recapture Stitch. They escape to the Pelekais' home and fight Jumba, destroying their house. During the battle, Jumba reveals that Stitch used Lilo for his protection, leading to guilt-ridden Stitch's surrender.

Jumba takes Stitch aboard his spaceship using a portal-generating gun, intending to erase Stitch's newfound empathy. However, Lilo sneaks aboard and frees Stitch, and they eject Jumba from the ship. The ship crashes into the ocean, trapping Lilo and Stitch underwater. Stitch rescues her, but as he cannot swim to the surface, he releases her to let her emerge and drowns.

Nani and David rescue Lilo, but she refuses to leave Stitch. David returns Lilo to shore while Nani swims back to get Stitch from the ocean floor. They reach shore, but Stitch remains unconscious. After Bubbles finds Pleakley and they rejoin the group, David revives Stitch by jump-starting his lungs. Shortly after, the Grand Councilwoman arrives and re-arrests Jumba. After seeing Stitch's change of heart, she decides to let Stitch exile on Earth with his newfound ʻohana. The Grand Councilwoman vows to keep in touch, with Pleakley living with the Pelekais to watch over Stitch.

As Pelekais, Stitch, and company return home, Kekoa tells Nani she can transfer Lilo's guardianship to David and Tūtū, letting her stay home. The ʻohana then repairs the house and lives happily.

This stalwart and sturdy Corgi is here to join you on your adventures!

These models are designed for use with tabletop roleplaying games, such as Dungeons and Dragons or Pathfinder, but it is detailed enough to scale up and print as you please.

As is, it is scaled to fit on a 25.4mm / 1 inch round base, not included. The 3-Headed version is scaled for both Medium and Large bases, so print him as large and terrifying as you want!

Two versions of the four standard Corgis are provided: Heroic, and Small. Small is scaled to be close to 28mm accurate, and Heroic is scaled to be larger and easier to print. If you have any doubts as to which to choose, go for Heroic!

This model was made possible thanks to the support of https://beldolorstudios.com/ ! They commissioned it and allowed it to be uploaded and printed by all!

Please note that they own the sole commercial right to print and sell all versions of this model, and as such no commercial use other than through them is allowed, and no remixes are allowed.

[If you liked this model and want to show your thanks, you can buy me a coffee!](https://ko-fi.com/clayrade)

[And follow me on Instagram!](https://www.instagram.com/clay.rade/)

Six years ago, I remixed the very first pieces of Fukai scatter terrain from the work of AxoloteGaming and onebitpixel.
They were a raw experiment in organic, alien-inspired structures—and to my surprise, they spread across the hobby world like wildfire.
Since then, they’ve been downloaded millions of times and used to build entire themed tables.

Today, I’m bringing them back—remastered.

🔧 What’s new?

Sharper, cleaner surface lines to make painting easier (washes and drybrushes pop much better now).

More consistent detailing across each piece for a stronger visual impact.

Optimized meshes for smoother printing results.

This is just the beginning—I plan to gradually rework the entire collection to bring it up to the same standard.

And if you want to go even further into the Fukai universe, don’t miss the ongoing Kickstarter campaign:
https://www.kickstarter.com/projects/alario/fukai

The campaign includes a complete playable biome with modular buildings, ruins, props, and tournament-ready layouts—all designed to expand and complement the free scatter terrain.

I was asked to make an all-archer goblin unit, and it instantly took me back to when I first started collecting goblins for Warhammer. Back then, my assistant lecturer’s salary didn’t leave much room for the hobby, so I was over the moon to find an eBay lot of a hundred goblin archers going for pennies. That bargain became my very first goblin archer unit — a proper horde of those classic monopose Kev Adams sculpts, all grinning the same grin, all ready to rain arrows (and probably trip over each other).

This little project was just for the sake of reliving those memories — don’t worry, I’ll be making a proper unit of goblin archers too.

Six years ago, I remixed the very first pieces of Fukai scatter terrain from the work of AxoloteGaming and onebitpixel.
They were a raw experiment in organic, alien-inspired structures—and to my surprise, they spread across the hobby world like wildfire.
Since then, they’ve been downloaded millions of times and used to build entire themed tables.

Today, I’m bringing them back—remastered.

🔧 What’s new?

Sharper, cleaner surface lines to make painting easier (washes and drybrushes pop much better now).

More consistent detailing across each piece for a stronger visual impact.

Optimized meshes for smoother printing results.

This is just the beginning—I plan to gradually rework the entire collection to bring it up to the same standard.

And if you want to go even further into the Fukai universe, don’t miss the ongoing Kickstarter campaign:
https://www.kickstarter.com/projects/alario/fukai

The campaign includes a complete playable biome with modular buildings, ruins, props, and tournament-ready layouts—all designed to expand and complement the free scatter terrain.

Having been dragged into another hobby, this time in 6/8mm scale, and missing models I wanted to field I decided to model my own. As I like my greenskin models a little bigger than usual, they are more like 10mm, but hey - they're supposed to be bigger than usual 'oomies ;)

In the collection you will find:

3. Two mobile flamethrowers - one 2-nd World War Willis style, the second a tankish ignition machine
4. A big boss on a bike with lots of dakka
5. A regular boss with an equal amount of dakka
6. A BIG WAGON with even more guns. This one has three turrets to choose from so you can customize them to your liking

Update!
7. Added three different leaders in heavy armour and some solid waponry

The battlefields of the grim-dark future are scattered will the everyday materiel of the industrial and military complex required to process war on a galactic scale.

This set offers a sample of a cargo crate, cargo hauler, blank trailer, and pallet of materiel.

These could be printed at 200% for 15mm gaming terrain, or, if you are ambitious, 400% for 28-32mm scale gaming. The models are sufficiently detailed to be printed at larger scale, yet simple and robust enough to print at their intended 6-8mm scale.

This set contains 4 STLs; a sample of the full set, available here:
https://cults3d.com/en/3d-model/game/epic-cargo-road-train-scatter-terrain-6mm-8mm-scale

The full set allows you to customise your selection. It can be used to create cargo 'road trains', linking multiple trailers and cargo containers to create thematic barriers for your miniatures to take cover behind, or individual pieces to add character to the bases of larger miniatures.

They would also make suitable 'toys' what could be added to 28-32mm scale models, adding a layer of horror and inhumanity to the devastation surrounding your grim-dark characters.

The crane and defence trailer is compatible with my other Epic tank turrets, so can be replaced with any of the turrets in this collection:
https://cults3d.com/en/3d-model/game/8mm-scale-grim-dark-tank-turrets-of-russ-nedius

So you want a large Sector Mechanicus tile, and you don't want greebly detail? And, maybe, you have a fairly small resin printer, so printing it in one piece isn't really possible? OK, or maybe you have a big enough printer?

Here's a few options for 122mm octagonal or square tiles. They match the dimensions you would expect for Sector Mechanicus. They have all the join-y holes underneath.

Unlike [my other large tile offering](https://www.thingiverse.com/thing:6962622) these have no locators on top. The bolts are recessed and do not protrude at all (not even like regular SM tiles), so you can stack whatever you like on top.

Your choice whether you want a port in the middle (and what orientation) or not.

If you are printing tiny little parts on your tiny little printer, then you will want:
* 1x centre piece, whether that's a square or a port
* 4x outer section, suited to port or not as appropriate
 Technically you can mix the oct (non diag) and square sections, I guess, if you want an unusual shape
 (e.g. if you were making [a big platform](https://www.thingiverse.com/thing:7092618), say)

If you don't care about splitting up your tile, then just print one of the full ones, or a quarter/half. These are designed to stand alone as regular tiles. If you can fit it on your printer, it'll be easier than assembling 5 parts to make a single tile!

There's a zip file named "fdm" containing all the whole-tile pieces with no recesses (except the join-y holes) underneath. I have _not_ tested them on an FDM printer; I do not own one. It just seemed maybe useful.

A griffin (or griffon, depending on the English spelling) is a mythological creature with the body of a lion and the head and wings of an eagle. It is a common figure in the mythology and art of various cultures, often associated with vigilance and the protection of treasures.
Characteristics:
Body:
The lower body of the griffin is that of a lion, including its tail and hind legs.
Head and Wings:
The upper body is that of an eagle, with a sharp beak, piercing eyes, and feathers.
Additional Attributes:
In some depictions, it is also attributed with pointed ears and eagle-like foreclaws.
Symbolism and Meaning:
Guardian:
Griffons are known to be guardians of treasures and riches, especially gold.
Strength and Courage:
Combining the strength of the lion and the sharpness of the eagle, the griffin symbolizes power, courage, and vigilance. Connection to the Sun:
In some cultures, the griffin is associated with the sun and light, due to the eagle's majestic nature.
Origin:
Griffins are believed to have ancient origins, possibly in the Middle East or Asia.
Depictions of griffins are found in the art and mythology of various civilizations, including Greek, Roman, and Persian.
There is speculation that the image of the griffin may have been inspired by dinosaur fossils.

I love the game SABLE by SHEDWORKS. It's probably my favorite game, and a really under-rated gem. This is my tribute to the game, and to the fans of game who, like me, have wanted a little physical model of Sable for their shelves or desks.

The Hakoa top and bottom are my favorite pieces of clothing in the game, so I created this version of Sable dressed in them. I've included two versions, one with the iconic Ibexii mask and one with the Scrapper mask, which is how Sable appears in my playthrough (screenshot attached.)

She's scaled for 28mm gaming, but you can also scale her up to any size that you like.

I really, really hope that we get to see more of SABLE's world in the future. It's really an amazing experience of a game.

My own take on a Super Heavy aerial transport for Space Marines dubbed the Storm Crane. Sized to be used in Epic/Legion Imperialis games.

Unique in its role, Storm Cranes are able to deliver a variety of assets to the front. From 10 fully embarked rhinos, or 4 kratos heavy battle tanks or any other armored detachment, Storm Cranes are able to bring full detachments of armor needed on the battle field. Protected by heavy plating and a pair of void shields this flyer can withstand any punishment short of anti-titan weapons. Ensuring its cargo successfully arrives where it is needed. Each Strom Crane is armed with two audax heavy bolter arrays and two titan sized havoc launchers making it a formidable assault craft that can break through enemy lines. A truly armored work horse, Space Marine legions relied heavily on these vehicles throughout the crusade and into the Heresy.


While I designed most of this using 3D Builder, I did borrow some choice parts from free kits.
Winglets/Audax Turrets from MKHand Industries
Thruster Turbine and Exhaust from IronMaster
Titan Hatch and Void Shields from Danny_Cyanide

Death From Below! The Imperious Republican Democratic Autocratic Pneumatic Psychotic Syphilitic Hegemony spans many worlds and encompasses many races of humans, demi-humans, and aliens. One such species are the Space Dwarves, who, because of some kind of sci-fi pseudo-babble, are half the size and twice the man as most of the IRDAPPSH's average citizens. Those same conditions also gave them Scottish accents, uncomfortably thick beards, and a strange obsession with art deco, but whatever.

It could be said that the Space Dwarves are compensating for something by deploying their massive and rather phallic Mega-Cannon. However, it better be said quietly or far away from the ears of said Space Dwarves, else the speaker may find themselves learning to live without any legs, so be warned. The Mega-Cannon fires a shell the size of a cargo van at targets the Imperious Leader has determined to be "bothersome".

This product includes both 6mm and 8mm versions!

Eerie in the contrast of their lethal size and silent movement, ScorpionMechs are deployed on the orbital and planetside battlefield when no quarter is to be given to the enemy, and none expected.

They're colony killers.

You send them in when you want the enemy base and any feeble defenders protecting it razed to the ground.

These scuttling terrors can chop enemy armors in half in close quarters or pound them to pieces from a distance. Using a variety of modular payloads, the ScorpionMech can tailor its weapons suite to the mission, whether it be cold, quiet up-close killing, napalm and gatling cascades at ballistic distances, or missiles beyond the horizon.

This 6/8mm scale ScorpionMech can be utilized as an attack drone against 15mm or 28mm figures with ease, or utilized in any miniatures-agnostic rule set. Or just as a keychain.

This is a fused, quarter-scale version of the 28mm version. It will be at home going into combat against tiny warmachines in the 3025 era or 40000 years from now.

Saws, claws, gatlings, flamethrowers, and gun clusters are all included in this package of STL files.

Details and links are in the included PDF instructions. If you want, you can preview them here at this WeTransfer link...
https://we.tl/t-OFCeq2Rnp7

I also offer 28mm and 15mm versions of this devastating battle construct. Check my other files for those offerings.

Enjoy!

JBR

These menacing multi-legged minions come in a variety of scales, as originally sculpted, but their universal nature and lack of scale cues enables them to be used as massed armies in nearly any setting, and can be exchanged easily between settings. A 28mm spiderdrone looks impressive next to a 15mm human, while the 6mm spiderbots look like they can crawl over and pull down a 28mm figure.

The 28mm, multi-part versions are crafted in separate legs and blasters set at multiple angles. The 15mm and 6mm versions are tiny and fused. You can fill entire print beds with the little creepy-crawlers!

Originally created as escort bots and onboard infantry for the ScorpionMech, which I also offer, these little bots come in deployed and stowed versions, with full and empty carrier racks that can be adapted to other builds.

ScorpionMechs and other figures are shown for reference, and are sold separately.

Enjoy!

A modular set of parts for dungeon crawling in the icy void of space.


These parts use OpenLOCK clips to assemble.


You'll find the clip in the 4-Others folder.


https://www.printablescenery.com/product/open-lock/





The pieces do not use the tile system per se.





This set allows you to play games such as Space Hulk, games in the Zone Mortalis environment, Necromunda and other Warhammer 40k SF dystopian universes.





For Space Hulk players, here you'll find everything you need to redo all the missions from V1 and its expansions.


Parts will be added as we go along, enabling you to play the game's 2 expansions.


This being done on my own time, thank you for understanding my pace of adding pieces.





The squares are 33x33 mm, which is a good compromise between the volume of filament required and good playability.


The whole thing can be scaled to suit your aspirations.

**Model Description:**
**"In the name of the Emperor, cleanse the filth of heresy!"**
This 3D printed model is inspired by the Adepta Sororitas in the Warhammer 40K universe, and reinterprets their sacredness and majesty in a cartoon style. The character is portrayed as the embodiment of the Empire's faith - wearing a finely crafted **Holy Power Armor**, with a burning Imperial double-headed eagle and scripture prayers engraved on the surface of the armor, symbolizing its dual mission as the **Sword of the State Religion** and the **Vanguard of the Inquisition**. The model is extremely dynamic. The nun is leaping and swinging a sword, with broken chaos symbols under her feet, as if she is tearing apart the darkness with her fervent faith.

Death From Below! The Imperious Republican Democratic Autocratic Pneumatic Psychotic Syphilitic Hegemony spans many worlds and encompasses many races of humans, demi-humans, and aliens. One such species are the Space Dwarves, who, because of some kind of sci-fi pseudo-babble, are half the size and twice the man as most of the IRDAPPSH's average citizens. Those same conditions also gave them Scottish accents, uncomfortably thick beards, and a strange obsession with art deco, but whatever.

Why fly into battle when you can drift gently? The Space Dwarf War-Zeppelin is less a flying machine and more a floating weapons platform. Six twin batteries of "Mobile Migraine" cannons and two Infinite Repeaters provide covering fire while the War-Zeppelin maneuvers into place to drop its huge payload of earth-shattering high-explosive extremely-rude gravity bombs. The floaty part of the airship isn't simply a giant balloon; it's a honeycomb of independent pockets permanently filled with helium and surrounded by a woven plasteel envelope that is highly puncture resistant.

Don't delay! Get yours today!

Built by da biggest Mek around, the Brawla Bot is the ultimate kombo of krumpin’ power and dakka mayhem. Armed with a mix of choppy gubbinz and shooty bitz, dis hulkin' heap of scrap don’t care how it smashes – just that it does.

Whether it’s tearin' through enemy lines wiv buzzin’ blades, or lightin’ up targets from afar wiv loud, rattly shootas, da Brawla Bot is ready for any scrap. It’s got armor thicker than a squig’s skull and enough attitude to make a Warboss jealous.

Designed for tabletop mayhem and hobby fun, dis multipart kit comes with options for both melee and ranged gear – so you can pose it just right before sendin' it into a proper Waaagh!

Note: Dis is a fan-made model, full of grimy character and orkiness, but not linked to any official game or company. It’s just for da ladz who like loud machines an’ big fights.


This model is compatible to the bitz of following models:
- Mosha Bot
- Shoota Bot


======= PRINTING =========

- Layer hight 0.05mm
- Use tree / organic supports.
- I printed my test prints with a 0.25mm nozzle (for best quality)
- Orientate the Exhausts01-04 vertical

======= Assembly =========

If you need instructions - just open all files in 3D Builder or e.g. Meshmixer at the same time (drag and drop). There you can have a look where they need to go in 3D.



---
Shame less beggin' for some coins for caffeine I need doin' stuff like that :-)

Please consider a tip ....this highly detailed model was a work of hundeds of hours of free time!
If you do so, I HIGHLY APPRECIATE YOUR GENEROSITY :-)

Kind regands,
Tersus

Sector Mechanicus style tiles.
Simpler - no details in the gratings. Sometimes you don't need all the detail. 
Many of them have pipe ports, which oddly don't exist in the originals outside a ruined one. 

Standard holes underneath for pillars and join-y connector-y things.

I needed a single rectangular tile with a port for myself. But, you know, with what I needed to make for that one, I could make multiple permutations. I'd done half the work already (It might seem like I'd done more than half, but making the permutations took way longer than I expected!).

1x1 square tiles, and 1x2 tiles, and a single strange 1x1.5 tile.
Two different gratings (plain and with a cog design), plus pipe ports in different positions and numbers, with hatches at various orientations.
Honestly, yeah, it's overkill. I do not know how many people care about getting hatches in the every possible orientation, but well, the person sitting in my chair really is that ridiculous.

The *FDM* zip file contains the exact same tiles, but without the recesses underneath. They still have holes for pegs; there's no other changes. I _have not_ printed these in FDM. I don't even have an FDM printer. It was a suggestion someone made to me, seeing as the simpler nature of the top detail might lend itself to FDM printing, and I figured, sure, why not. May as well, right? Perhaps this is useful to someone, perhaps not.

* What's with the 2-port tiles' letter-number designations? Why are some numbers missing?
 A/O/S = Aligned/Opposite/Symmetric. The numbers are missing because some would be equivalent (e.g. O1 == S1, A3 == S3), or creatable simply by rotating/mirroring an existing piece (e.g. A4 would be A2 mirrored)

#### You may also like
https://www.thingiverse.com/thing:7098595 - for larger and/or octagonal type tiles

"Immerse yourself in the atmosphere of the Middle Ages with our collection of 3D printed houses!"

These carefully designed models have been created specifically for 3D printing and are ideal for board games, dioramas and lovers of historical architecture. Each house is tested and ready to print on FDM and SLA printers, ensuring excellent quality and detail at all levels.

All models are made in 28 mm scale, which makes them ideal for most tabletop role-playing games such as Dungeons & Dragons, Pathfinder and others.

Features:

Easy to print: The models are designed with the features of 3D printers in mind, minimizing the need for support.

Detailing: Authentic medieval architecture, every detail worked out with love.

Versatility: Suitable for use both in games and as a decoration.

Tested: All models were printed and tested for compatibility with different types of 3D printers.

In this project, every small element of the village has been thought out to create an atmosphere of the Middle Ages and the feeling that you are in this era. You will be able to print and assemble each building together, creating a unique composition that will become a worthy decoration of your interior or playing field.

Do not miss the opportunity to purchase this unique project and plunge into the world of medieval architecture and atmosphere!

Victoria is a 3D artist, and Victoria lovingly creates unique models for 3D printing. This project is the result of her passion for the fantasy world and attention to detail.

Inspired by the excellent work of Mortalitis, with their Warhound weapon rack (found here: https://cults3d.com/en/3d-model/game/adeptus-titanicus-legions-imperialis-warhound-weapon-rack)

This rack works with Reaver or Warlord weapons. Intended to go into Really Useful Boxes fitted with rubberized/ferrous magnetic sheet. Or metal biscuit tins or whatever magnetic thing you're using.

Base magnets are 6x2mm per Mortalitis' design. However, there are 3x holes in my design; I felt that the bigger weapons needed more grip, though you can ignore the central magnet if you like.

The weapon mounting magnets are 5x1mm.
This is because the 'standard' magnet size for 8mm scale Reaver and Warlord titans is is 5x1mm (the plastic has holes in these sizes!). And also I have a lot of that size, so thats what I used.

There is a new terror stalking the arenas and battlefields of Junctionworld and its worldgate networks.

Eerie in the contrast of their lethal size and silent movement, ScorpionMechs are sent through hostile interdimensional portals as shock attack units, scything and slicing through any resistance on the other side.

In the Gatekeepers' colosseums of mechanized bloodsport, ScorpionMechs have quickly earned a reputation as close-quarter killers, their tail weapons well-placed to send a buzzsaw or energized claw into an opponent's cockpit, regardless of shielding.

In conventional fights, the scuttling nightmares are sometimes inserted on to the a planetside battlefield via the use of a-grav or chemical rocket packs bolted under their hulls.

They are utilized when no quarter is to be given to the enemy, and none expected.

They're colony killers. Merciless reapers. Harvesters of those foolish enough to try and face them.

Using a variety of modular payloads, the ScorpionMech pilot can tailor their unit's weapons suite to the mission, whether it be cold, quiet up-close killing, napalm and gatling cascades at ballistic distances, or missiles from beyond the horizon.

The base package for the 15mm (I use 1/100th scale) ScorpionMech includes pincers, saws, Asher claws (named for Neal Asher, whose books you should really check out), gatlings, flamethrowers, and gun clusters. Supplemental mounts are provided for heavy cannons and missile launchers.
As mentioned above, orbital assault belly packs are also included.

This is a pretty decent undertaking, not for the faint-hearted. Rest assured, though, the largest piece (the main hull) will fit in a Mars 2 or similar-sized printer.

These are remixes of the terminals by Jymacdougall, and all credit should go to him for the amazing designs. Keep in mind these are based on the Grand Master Terminals so are a bit bigger than the standard ones. For the warhound, I corrected errors in the text and modified the token slots to take 3x1mm magnets instead of pegs. The Reaver is pretty much made from scratch but printed out fine. Also included are 3 different custom tokens I made for the different tracking types.

-Resin Printers: I had some issues with warping on the edge towards the plate. To solve this, I added a break away wedge to one end. These are the STL's labelled with "R". If you angle the terminal with the wedge towards the plate, the wedge should warp instead of the terminal, then just break off the wedge when it's done.

-FDM Printers: If you want the smaller text to be legible, you're going to have to use a .2 nozzle so be prepared for a fairly long print time. Don't forget to change the settings in your slicer or risk a major clog.

I do plan on making a Warlord terminal when I get some time.

Use LOWKEY20 at checkout for a 20% discount!

The war for Renner’s World is not going well for the embattled forces defending their home from the invading Kaiju. The abominable walking mega-fauna are now manifesting new abilities and incorporating cybernetic systems and replacement limbs, hinting at a more sinister force behind the invasion through the world-gates.

To compensate for this growing threat, the members of the Renner Defense League command staff have dusted off old plans from the Project Gigante design competition, the JagdHund, or Hunting Hound. JagdHund was a concept once deemed too large and unwieldy for the battlefield, but it has been recalled to the forefront as the threat literally grows larger.

JagdHund’s paired heavy gatling weapons are capable of dealing with hordes or point targets with equal ease, while the dorsal-mounted main gun, a superheavy maser cannon, is dedicated to frying and boiling the larger monsters emerging through the dimensional breaches. The directed energy weapon is an experiment, and has not been properly developed to withstand the rigors of close-range combat with kaiju. Plans are in the works to add different weapons and countermeasures to the JagdHund arsenal.

The majority of the Hund crews are composed of Quads, or quadruple amputees, wounded veterans and civilian volunteers who have been maimed and disfigured by the invading megafauna. Body modifications are sometimes necessary for final adjustments, but replacement limbs are provided. Quads came about originally from the Assault Raptor program, but have proved to be an invaluable asset in the fight against the invading monsters.

I suggest joining my Patreon at www.patreon.com/johnbearross for a monthly rolling 50% discount on my entire inventory, including this one.

Enjoy!

Trays are designed to be used with 1.75L Really Useful Boxes (UK/EU) to maximise the space inside when carrying minis for smaller scale games like Legions Imperialis, From Ashes or Dropzone Commander. Simply apply some ferrous rubber sheet to the floor of the tray and then you can stack multiple layers of magnetised minis inside a single RUB.

Each 1.75L RUB has approx 60mm of inner height so the trays are used in the following combinations.

3x 20mm Trays
2x 30mm Trays
1x 40mm Tray + 1x 20mm Tray

20mm trays are good for Legions Imperialis infantry minis, rhinos/smaller vehicles
30mm trays are good for most other vehicles and From Ashes (15mm scale) infantry
40mm trays are good for the larger minis like Legions Imperialis automata

Based on the design by JTSWargaming (https://cults3d.com/en/3d-model/game/legions-imperialis-storage-tray-inserts-for-4l-really-useful-boxes). His designs are only good for the US version of 4L RUB, the UK/EU 4L is a bit wider so it is incompatible. I also found these to be a little too big to fit on my printer as I needed bed adhesion support to avoid lifting.

I made these as a resource for myself, as I want to start making up some themed bases, and need the basics in place to build on!

This is an extensive set of round and oval bases, that can be used as spares for existing minis for you to print and texture yourself, or to make life easier when designing your own scenic base STLs.

The set for magnets are also for those who wish to save a bit of resin - they have support structures underneath the base surface for added strength, with holes for 5mm x 2mm round magnets. This is my preferred magnets for magnetising bases. In case you prefer 1mm thick magnets, I've added a 'filler' that can be printed and inserted into the holes, in case it is any use. Alternatively, just use your preferred modeling putty to fill the hole, and press the magnet into it.

The Wastes are home to all manner of terrible creatures, mutated from what were once the humble creatures of the forests. Whether this was by design, genetic mutation, or simply through exposure to chaotic magics is unknown.

This is a collection of mutated beasts, designed for Fantasy and Post-Apocalyptic Wargaming and RPGs. They are truly massive beasts, and so are provided both whole, in kit form, and with hollowed out versions to allow you to chose the right set for your needs. These were made whilst making my toad-dragon (link below), as each time I looked at it, it made me think of a different animal! I saw a rat, molerat, and hippo, and here they are!

I love settings in post apocalyptic fallout shelters, where desert mole rats have mutated into massive beasts, so have a particular fondness for the mole-rat monster here - perfect for creating a monstrous mount for your post apocalyptic raiders or travelling merchants!

The Toad Dragon can be found here:
https://cults3d.com/en/3d-model/game/chaos-toad-dragon

These models come without rider or saddle, and are designed to be kit-bashed with your favourite fantasy range. These parts are also compatible with the bits from the Toad Dragon, and so would complement it nicely.

Please see my other designs for other wargaming STLS, including maggots, tics and flies suitable for adding even more detail to this model, or to decorate your army's bases.

I am an amateur enthusiast 3D designer, and appreciate all support and constructive feedback. Please check out my other designs for more wargame models, and please consider following me, post a make, and enjoy my models. If you would like to support my work, please leave a comment, like the design, or make a donation via my profile! Thanks!

Small and Mean, and you can crank them out by the bushel!

The Basic Raptor in 15mm Tabletop (1/100th scale) is a starter model, a free demonstration of both the scale and the detail of my files. It can also make an easy desktop display model, without taking up too much room.

Depending on pose, height on the included 50mm base is about 2 and 5/8th inch, or 66.6mm.

If you would like the free 28mm (1/56th scale) version, click here...
https://cults3d.com/en/3d-model/game/free-project-raptor-the-basic-raptor

Check out my other mech and knight parts, most of which are free, in the other collections in my store.

https://cults3d.com/en/users/johnbearross/3d-models

------------------------

Kushal Heavy Industries, based 214 jumps deep in the Fourth Gate Network of worlds, is a renowned manufacturer of arms, both for their economy of material usage and rock bottom pricing structures.

They recently have taken their surrounding upstream and downstream neighborhood of dimensions by storm with the release of the Basic Raptor, a clean-sheet refinement of the datacore salvaged long ago from an unknown, nuked-out world.

That datacore gave the Realms Project Raptor, a broad category of light mechs that serve as scouts and fast attack platforms, taking the fight to the enemy with speed and devastating firepower.

Kushal's version is a stark, bare-bones battle platform that is intended for the customer who needs to put warheads on foreheads, without any need for frivolity, pomp, or circumstance. Or cockpit padding, as many a bruised pilot can testify.

The Basic Raptor is sneered at by some, but admired by others for its uncompromising simplicity, ruggedness, and singularity of purpose.

Many smaller defense contractors and boutique armor shops are taking stock Basic Raptors and modifying them with fancier weapons and armor packages. Assassins from the Kushal Heavy Industries Legal Department have been dispatched through the world-gates to deliver enhanced cease-and-desist notifications, to some lethal effect.

------------------------

If you like what you see, I encourage you to join my Patreon.
http://www.patreon.com/johnbearross

I give a rolling monthly 50% discount code for my entire inventory, including new releases as I put them out.

I also have a Discord, The Madness of John Bear Ross. We're a collection of mecha-heads, painters, builders, and other artists who love giant walking nightmares. Here's the invite link...
https://discord.gg/7PyEqpkARb

Enjoy!

Other mechs are shown for size ref purposes, and are available separately.

This is a set for creating a city building as a terrain for any wargame in 1/285 (6mm) scale. The set allows you to assemble both an intact (undamaged) buildings and a destroyed ones (ruins). You can assemble a building of any height you want by printing the required number of intermediate floors.


There is one option with square windows (marked with number 1) and the second with rounded windows (marked with number 2).


To make it easier to paint the windows, I made it a separate piece that can be painted in advance (for example, with spray paint) and inserted inside the walls.


I also made a set of interior parts in case you don't use windows or want to make glass from transparent material.

In the heat of battle, it's sometimes necessary to salvage enemy equipment, even wreckage, and recondition it to make it usable again, and why not use your own damaged ships to reassemble everything into something usable.


That's what's on offer here. The Magos of the Dark Mechanicum always take great pleasure in corrupting and reusing imperial technology so that they can use it against the imperium.





The design isn't mine, it's a kitbash of several parts from Italianmoose for the hulls and Keiler for the turrets.





A 2.00mm slot is provided for fixing it to a base with a rod of any kind.





I haven't printed it yet, but a make will be posted as soon as possible.

This is a Painting Handle for epic-scaled miniatures!
The orange lever can be thrown to rotate the minis 90 degrees.
This allows you to have them in close rows, saving space, and allowing for efficient spraying, without sacrificing the ability to paint the side details!

This model is designed to be printed via FDM. If you don't have one, don't worry! I'll be printing them through my etsy, here:
https://etsy.me/3PB8q07

The handle is light, stable, and modular!

Use:
Basic Configuration: Put 5x Basic Gears in the handle and then a set of the two racks. You want to make sure one is at the top of it's travel, and the other is as far down as it can go. See the pictures for an example of how it should look.

The holder is designed that the gears are slightly taller than they ought to be. This means that the lid pushes down onto the gears to create enough friction and tension that the gears don't tilt around during painting. If you want to relieve a bit of tension to make the mechanism easier to operate, I've found that gently bending the lid outwards to relieve this tension helps.

Threaded Gears: The Threaded gears can be swapped in to allow the fitment of the Holder plates - these can be used for pinned minis using the central hole and a bit of superglue to hold it's rotation, or minis with a wider footprint.

Stackable Base and Lid: These are the regular base and lid but with a second hole so you can print a mirrored rack with handle, to allow for easier actuation of the mechanism.
This also means that you can line up the handles along your desk, nesting the switch nub into the hole of the painting handle in front, useful for keeping everything tidy and together when batchpainting or spraying!
For an example, check out the last two photos, for how the nesting works!

If you'd like to keep up with my current projects, and support the modelling work I do, please check out my patreon at: www.patreon.com/Daffmakes

If you like what I'm doing, please donate to my ko-fi!
www.ko-fi.com/daffmakes

Death From Below! The Imperious Republican Democratic Autocratic Pneumatic Psychotic Syphilitic Hegemony spans many worlds and encompasses many races of humans, demi-humans, and aliens. One such species are the Space Dwarves, who, because of some kind of sci-fi pseudo-babble, are half the size and twice the man as most of the IRDAPPSH's average citizens. Those same conditions also gave them Scottish accents, uncomfortably thick beards, and a strange obsession with art deco, but whatever.

Another of the Space Dwarf's strange obsessions is building things HUGE, much larger than necessary. It's possible they are overcompensating for something, but on the other hand, it's possible they are overcompensating for something. The Mjölnir Mobile Fortress is a huge armored crawler capable of carrying tanks, gyrocopters, and dozens of squat troops into battle. Armed with dozens of machine guns, antitank cannons, Gatling repeaters, anti-aircraft batteries, a siege mortar, and the patent-pending "Oh God Oh God We're All Gonna Die" siege cannon, which fires a slug the size of a Volkswagen, the Mjölnir can batter its way into any stronghold and wreak short, Scottish-accented havoc on the defenders within.

Note: This model is so big that I didn't bother making an 8mm version. It should work pretty well in both scales!

This is a set of 33 STLs that can act as a base for 2D+ RPG and boardgames set in space / industrial settings.

It's a base for further modelling and creative work. My plan is to use these as a base to add more detailed parts gathered from my bitz box and things I can print in resin. The FDM printed board tiles will provide a robust base to add the finer detailed parts onto. This is part of a personal modelling project to create a more generic space-corridor themed 2d+ tileset I can use with a range of models to play games like Space Hulk, Aliens, Necromunda, things like that. 

Each tile is based around a 32mmx32mm grid, so the larger bases common on 32mm miniatures will fit into the space. Square shaped floor tiles, cut or printed between 30mm - 32mm square will then fit the floor tiles to create a grid on which to play.

Compatible with my Atmosphere Processor Floor tiles set!
https://cults3d.com/en/3d-model/game/atmosphere-processor-rpg-tiles-for-gameboards-bases-and-dioramas


Each board tile features magnet holes for 5x2mm round magnets. However, also provided are two little exta bits - a 'peg' than can be used in place of magnets, and a 1x5mm disc for 'filling' the magnet holes so 5x1mm magnets can be used. When installing pegs, mount them in the lefthand hole only when facing you for each joint. You can do the right hand either, BUT the peg must be in the same side when facing you for every joint.

Included are two example 30x30mm floor tiles. These can be scaled to suit your preference, but will work at that size, or increased to 31mm or 32mm squared. Also included is an example greeble than can be added to the 'walls', to add a little visual interest.

There will be more complex versions of this set coming, with guide holes for floor tiles, mountings for wall decorations, a range of greebles. This will let me make a long time desired hobby project of an 'Aliens' themed Space Hulk board, so I can play a mix of those two games together!..

Please see my other designs for a variety of other sci-fi and fantasy models.

I am an amateur enthusiast 3D designer, and appreciate all support and constructive feedback. Please check out my other designs for more wargame models, and please consider following me, post a make, and enjoy my models. If you would like to support my work, please leave a comment, like the design, follow Nedius Designs via my socials links in my profile, or make a donation via my profile! Thanks!

Available for Deployment!

Our tiny archeologists have returned from their expedition to the tiny tank vaults and are proud to present you the ageless classic of tiny tank warfare - Sturmpanzer Mel! Named in honour of the ancient worthy, who for his skill in CAD was awarded the prestigious title of "CADor" - Mel the CADor is your number 1 choice for trench combat, prolonged sieges and general attritional warfare. The sturdy hull is provided with numerous options including:

- two different extra fuel tanks
- trench rails
- roof mounted searchlight

Furthermore our decoration team furnished optional imperial insignia to be affixed on prominent locations of your tank.

Autocannons, Laser Cannons, Heavy Gyrojets and a mighty Siege Howitzer are provided for sponson and hull mounts. The durable casemate can mount either a powerful cannon, long barreled tank killer cannon or a dual laser cannons.

In addition to that a specialized Protector variant is provided fully festooned with anti personnel weaponry for those hectic Mondays.

Furthermore all roof hatches are rendered fully operational so that you can always fulfil your urge to catch that fragrant smell of phosgene in the air.

Sturmpanzer Mel represents an exciting new chassis to be added to our tiny tank offering and is perfect for vehicular combat in 6 to 8mm scales!

Easy to print, FDM-friendly Pillbug (land isopods, roly-polys, etc) companions!

These are meant for tabletop roleplaying games such as D&D, Pathfinder, etc, but can be used for whatever you wish.

These giant fantasy isopods (don't at me about anatomy) are available in multiple flavors, including smooth, saddled, and cannoned.

The cannon prints separately (print the cannon oriented vertically with the mouth touching the build plate) and snaps into place, and includes a small prop crate of cannonballs.

They have been sized as Medium-sized (fits on a 1 inch / 25.4mm round base) creatures, but if you scale them up by about 150% they would work fine as Large creatures (Fits on a 2 inch / 50.8mm round base).

They print with minimal supports and should be quite sturdy, even with a 0.4mm nozzle.
They will look best printed in resin, or with a 0.2mm nozzle for fine details.
Example prints were printed at 0.16mm layer heights with a 0.4mm nozzle.

Simple supports will be needed on the cannon pivot points; be sure to cut or file down the contact point with supports.

item.description:

Id objet : 6772882

I recently got back into Warhammer after many years away, and after painting some marines I decided I wanted something different, so bought the Necromunda Hive War box with 2 gangs and some Zone Mortalis Terrain pieces. The terrain was interesting, but 4 things about it annoyed me.
1) It was hard to paint the panels on the walls and columns a contrasting colour without a lot of precise brush work
2) Placed on the game mat the walls and columns could too easily be knocked or slid around
3) The walls and columns were different lengths which limited the placement options on the mat if you wanted it to line up with the floor
4) I wanted more but it costs how much!

But I have a 3d printer, so I thought I’d print some so I looked around for some free STLs. The STLs I found weren’t 100% to liking though so I fired up Blender and got to work editing existing STLs and making new ones. I might have got a bit carried away…


This is a pack of 98 STLs for modular terrain that is designed for games like Necromunda, Killteam, Warhammer 40k and other 28mm scifi games that would suit small scale skirmish action in grimdark industrial terrain.

I started with Zone Mortalis Terrain Pieces (28mm scale) https://www.thingiverse.com/thing:2609090 by eberleg (this thing appears to have been deleted though) so this is technically a remix, though there’s not a lot left of the originals, and I added a whole lot more original stuff (There are 98 STLs in the pack).

The set includes the basic wall and column pieces, but these now have separate interior panels, with optional greebles on them. This way the panels can be painted/base coated separately and then glued to the wall or column, saving a lot of paint time. The basic walls and columns have also been edited (quite a lot) to look more like GWs ones (but not exactly the same) and have more details, they are also the same height as plastic GW ones, but are now 2 inches (50.8mm) long (this is different from the GW ones). You can place these on a terrain mat or game board as you like.

But just placing them on a table isn’t what I wanted, I wanted something more secure, so I designed a set of floor pieces with cross shaped slots in them. Then, with a small adaptor piece, you can slot the walls and columns into the floors. Also, with an adaptor you can stack them on top of each other. To work with these, there’s a set of 9 different platforms (1-7 are cosmetic designs, one has slots to fit into various supports and one is just left blank), which can either slot into the floor, or the tops of the walls/columns to make walkways and make the game board more 3 dimensional. To allow you miniatures to get up to these upper platforms there’s stairs and ladders, and frames with supports for catwalks and bridges between the upper walls and columns)

To add more flavour, there’s also a few designs of doors (door frame and door are separate so you can open or close them), railings, barricades (which can be slotted onto a platform, railing or free standing with an adaptor piece. Plus there’s a pipe system and a chemical tank for all your toxic sludge needs.

Everything is designed to fit into the 2” grid so you can place stuff wherever you like. I hope that makes sense, the pictures may help, but I hope it’s fairly logical which pieces slot into what.

As much as I would like the pieces to snap together like Lego, the tolerances required for that are outside of what a consumer 3d printer can do (well what mine can do anyway). I’ve put in some wiggle room into all the pieces so they should fit, but parts that are too tight may need adjustment with a file or sandpaper, and ones that are a bit loose can be held with blue tack, or a bit of superglue (let it dry thoroughly first) on the connector to make it wider. But for some pieces, like stairs and catwalks and the panels inside the walls and columns, I really recommend gluing them together, cheap superglue will work fine on PLA. You can leave all the parts modular or make tile pieces as you see fit

The basic walls and columns and there panels can be printed without support, but a lot of the other pieces will need some, for the platforms I used regular grid supports tuned to let them pull away fairly easily, and for most other parts I used tree/organic supports on the higher cross pieces, using paint on supports can help as most little details like bolts sticking out from parts don’t really need support. I recommend printing the pipe and tank parts vertically. For the floor pieces these really need to be flat, so don’t rip them off the print bed when the print finishes as they are still warm and can deform a little. Just remove the bed with them still on, place it on flat surfaces, put some weight on the parts and leave it to cool for 20-30 minutes. This way they should stay perfectly flat.

I printed all the parts on my Qidi X-Max3 mostly at .2 layer height with 2 or 3 walls and about 10-15% infill using JAYO PLA Meta. Almost all parts can be printed on a small printer apart from the ZML_floor_slots_6x3 and ZML_floor_slots_6x6, but if your printer can’t fit those on it, just print multiple copies of the 3x3 or 4x4 floors.

All the parts are designed for an FDM printer and have been test printed. Will they work on a resin printer? I don’t know, probably, but I can’t be certain as I don’t have one to test them on.

**Iota-HU, Pickup Truck**

This file is another remix/remaster of a file made by [TheDude21](https://www.thingiverse.com/thedude21/designs) (check him out and give him a tip, if you like). Much like the previous Glade-S, I very much liked the core Cyberpunk stylings of this vehicle concept and thought that it would make a nice adaption into a 'lower' tech level universe setting as a civilian hovercraft vehicle at the 6mm scale setting.

**About the Design.** Despite the superficial resemblance's to the original design, this project actually took quite a lot of time to remaster, because I wanted to remove as many of the 'hard-angle' edges as possible. This should make the model much better to orientate for supports and 3D print on a resin system. (zoom right in on the file to compare it with the original, if you like!)

**Other Designs.** This model set is intended to be compatible with the other 6mm (true-scale) and Hex(33) (hex scale) SciFi terrain sets that I have released on [Cults 3D](https://cults3d.com/en/users/Shiaic3D/creations) and other locations, [GumRoad](https://shiaic3d.gumroad.com/), [Printables](https://www.printables.com/@Shiaic3D/models) and [Thingiverse](https://www.thingiverse.com/shiaic1/designs).

Please search my other designs for more models of a similar type and theme.

****************
**Creativity Powered by Patreon.** This model is a remix of free files and parts available elsewhere. However, the time and effort to remix them into a model set like this were enabled with the support of my generous [Patreon](https://www.patreon.com/Shiaic3D) backers, who gain exclusive access to remixes like this for a temporary period well before it is released wider.

Please check out my [Patreon](https://www.patreon.com/Shiaic3D) if you want to support the creation of more remix projects like this, or gain access to my other remastered works and/or unique terrain creations for 6mm tabletop wargaming.

**Leave a Tip.** Alternatively, please feel free to leave a tip if you like this model and think it is merited (and don't forget to tip any original designers) - an occasional coffee helps fuel the creative effort and sustains morale :)

**Other Files.** Additionally, if you want to find more of my unique 6mm wargame terrain and building creations and other 3D designs, check out my [GumRoad](https://shiaic3d.gumroad.com/) shop or please also see my other unique designs on [Cults 3D](https://cults3d.com/en/users/Shiaic3D/creations). For a small cost (about half a coffee), I have a few re-detailed and remastered 6mm vehicle and FightMech models, such as:

* https://cults3d.com/en/3d-model/game/bt-asf-sparrowharwk-spr-h5
* https://cults3d.com/en/3d-model/architecture/bt-6mm-scifi-terrain-large-double-residential-habitation-enhanced

This file is a remix & remaster of a file originally made by [Pietia](https://www.thingiverse.com/Pietia). I had looked at this 28mm scale model Cyberpunk Sci-Fi car and thought that it would be a cool design to adapt and remix as a civilian-model Sci-Fi hover car for use at 6mm scale.

**About the Design.** I have taken the original 3D model by Pieta and remastered it slightly, adapting it more for the 6mm scale size where some of the detail at 28mm scale was either redundant or required some further adjusting to account for detail creep or dissolution (if printed). I then created the Hovercraft 'skirt' separately and melded these two main feature components together. Finally, I created some other new detail features as well as further adjusting some of the existing features to bring it all together more holistically as an integrated overall design that works on its own.

And voila! hopefully, it does.

**Other Designs.** This model set is intended to be compatible with the other 6mm (true-scale) and Hex(33) (hex scale) SciFi terrain sets that I have released on [Cults 3D](https://cults3d.com/en/users/Shiaic3D/creations) and other locations, [GumRoad](https://shiaic3d.gumroad.com/), [Printables](https://www.printables.com/@Shiaic3D/models) and [Thingiverse](https://www.thingiverse.com/shiaic1/designs).

Please search my other designs for more models of a similar type and theme.

****************
**Creativity Powered by Patreon.** This model is a remix of free files and parts available elsewhere. However, the time and effort to remix them into a model set like this were enabled with the support of my generous [Patreon](https://www.patreon.com/Shiaic3D) backers, who gain exclusive access to remixes like this for a temporary period well before it is released wider.

Please check out my [Patreon](https://www.patreon.com/Shiaic3D) if you want to support the creation of more remix projects like this, or gain access to my other remastered works and/or unique terrain creations for 6mm tabletop wargaming.

**Leave a Tip.** Alternatively, please feel free to leave a tip if you like this model and think it is merited (and don't forget to tip any original designers) - an occasional coffee helps fuel the creative effort and sustains morale :)

**Other Files.** Additionally, if you want to find more of my unique 6mm wargame terrain and building creations and other 3D designs, check out my [GumRoad](https://shiaic3d.gumroad.com/) shop or please also see my other unique designs on [Cults 3D](https://cults3d.com/en/users/Shiaic3D/creations). Our staff of dedicated tiny boffins had not sat idle and is proud to announce the latest and greatest in the tiny MBT scene - our new Apex MBT series. These high quality tanks are festooned with everything an enterprising tiny panzer general could ever desire. Elegant hull comes with two weapon option along with optional trench rails and engine filtration system for all your trench warfare needs! - Standard cannon

- Dual autocannon
- Dual laser cannon
- Siege howitzer

- Thermal ray emitter

I made these from scratch. The style is an attempt at homage to Kev Adams (GoblinMaster) HHG Heartbreaker Goblin sculpts.

I have enjoyed several free STL's from various creators. Freely I have received, so freely I give. This is a thank you to all of the people who make free STL's.

I hope to try to make some more variants.

These cannot be used for commercial purposes unless you buy the commercial license on my Gumroad site.


From the wikipedia page on Ronin
n feudal Japan (1185–1868), a rōnin (/ˈroʊnɪn/ ROH-nin; Japanese: 浪人, IPA: [ɾoːɲiɴ], 'drifter' or 'wanderer', lit. 'a person of the waves')[1] was a samurai who had no lord or master and in some cases, had also severed all links with his family or clan. A samurai becomes a rōnin upon the death of his master, or after the loss of his master's favor or legal privilege.[2][3]

In modern Japanese, the term is usually used to describe a salaryman who is unemployed or a secondary school graduate who has not yet been admitted to university.[4][5]
Etymology

The word rōnin is usually translated to 'drifter' or 'wanderer'; however, per kanji, rō (浪) means "wave" (as in body of water) or "unrestrained", while nin (人) means "man" or "person". It is an idiomatic expression for 'vagrant' or 'wandering man', someone who finds the way without belonging to one place. The term originated in the Nara and Heian periods, when it referred to a serf who had fled or deserted his master's land. In medieval times, the Ronin were depicted as the shadows of samurai, master-less and less honorable. It then came to be used for a samurai who had no master (hence the term 'wave man' illustrating one who is socially adrift).[3]
Status

According to the Bushido Shoshinshu (the "Code of the Warrior"), a samurai was supposed to commit seppuku (also harakiri, "belly cutting", a form of ritual suicide) upon the loss of his master.[6][7] One who chose not to honor the code was "on his own" and was meant to suffer great shame. The undesirability of rōnin status was mainly a discrimination imposed by other samurai and by daimyō, the feudal lords.[citation needed]

Like other samurai, rōnin wore two swords.[8] Rōnin used a variety of other weapons as well. Some rōnin—usually those who lacked money—would carry a bō (staff around 1.5 to 1.8 m (5 to 6 ft)) or jō (smaller staff or walking stick around 0.9 to 1.5 m (3 to 5 ft)) or a yumi (bow). Most weapons would reflect the ryū (martial arts school) from which they came if they were students.[citation needed]

During the Edo period, with the shogunate's rigid class system and laws, the number of rōnin greatly increased. Confiscation of fiefs during the rule of the third Tokugawa shōgun Iemitsu resulted in an especially large increase of rōnin.[2] During previous ages, samurai were able to move between masters and even between occupations. They could also marry between classes. However, during the Edo period, samurai were restricted, and were—above all—forbidden to become employed by another master without their previous master's permission.[citation needed]

Because the former samurai could not legally take up a new trade, or because of pride were loath to do so, many rōnin looked for other ways to make a living with their swords. Those rōnin who desired steady, legal employment became mercenaries that guarded trade caravans, or bodyguards for wealthy merchants. Many other rōnin became criminals, operating as bandits and highwaymen, or joining organized crime in towns and cities. Rōnin were known to operate or serve as hired muscle for gangs that ran gambling rings, brothels, protection rackets, and similar activities. Many were petty thieves and muggers. The criminal segment gave the rōnin of the Edo period a persistent reputation of disgrace, with an image of thugs, bullies, cutthroats, and wandering vagrants.[2] After the abolition of the Samurai, some of the ronin continued with their thuggery and their mercenary work and activities, such as participating in the infamous assassination of Korean Empress Myeongseong of the Joseon Dynasty in 1895, the Eulmi Incident.[citation needed]
History
Graves of the forty-seven rōnin at Sengaku-ji

Until the Sengoku period, peasants accounted for the majority of daimyō armies, so they accounted for the majority of ronin.[citation needed]

Especially in the Sengoku period, daimyō needed additional fighting men, and even if a master had perished, his rōnin was able to serve new lords. In contrast to the later Edo period, the bond between the lord and the vassal was loose, and some vassals who were dissatisfied with their treatment left their masters and sought new lords. Many warriors served a succession of masters, and some even became daimyō. As an example, Tōdō Takatora served ten lords. Additionally, the division of the population into classes had not yet taken place, so it was possible to change one's occupation from warrior to merchant or farmer, or the reverse. Saitō Dōsan was one merchant who rose through the warrior ranks to become a daimyō.[citation needed]

As Toyotomi Hideyoshi unified progressively more significant parts of the country, daimyō found it unnecessary to recruit new soldiers. The Battle of Sekigahara in 1600 resulted in the confiscation or reduction of the fiefs of large numbers of daimyō on the losing side; consequently, many samurai became rōnin. As many as a hundred thousand rōnin joined forces with Toyotomi Hideyori and fought at the Siege of Osaka. In the ensuing years of peace, there was less need to maintain expensive standing armies, and many surviving rōnin turned to farms or became townspeople. A few, such as Yamada Nagamasa, sought adventure overseas as mercenaries. Still, the majority lived in poverty as rōnin. Their number approached half a million under the third Tokugawa shōgun Iemitsu.[citation needed]

Initially, the shogunate viewed them as dangerous and banished them from the cities or restricted the quarters where they could live. They also prohibited serving new masters. As rōnin found fewer options, they joined in the Keian Uprising of 1651. This forced the shogunate to rethink its policy. It relaxed restrictions on daimyō inheritance, resulting in fewer confiscations of fiefs, and it permitted rōnin to join new masters.[citation needed]

Not having the status or power of employed samurai, rōnin were often disreputable and festive,[2] the group targeted humiliation or satire. It was undesirable to be a rōnin, as it meant being without a stipend or land. As an indication of the shame felt by samurai who became rōnin, Lord Redesdale recorded that a rōnin killed himself at the graves of the forty-seven rōnin. He left a note saying that he had tried to enter the service of the daimyō of Chōshū Domain but was refused. He killed himself, wanting to serve no other master and hating being a rōnin. On the other hand, the famous 18th-century writer Kyokutei Bakin renounced his allegiance to Matsudaira Nobunari, in whose service Bakin's samurai father had spent his life. Bakin voluntarily became a rōnin, and eventually spent his time writing books (many of them about samurai) and engaging in festivities.[citation needed]

In the 19th century, Emperor Meiji abolished the Samurai class and any status the ronin had died with them.[citation needed]

The ultimative tool for miniature painting! Clip in the base of your mini and you can paint without having to touch the mini at all, or getting paint on your hands. Especially useful when washing!

And for drybrushing, I included a structured 100x100mm plate to get to the perfect amount of paint on your brush, works much better than a paper towel.

There are two versions, one for bases between roughly 25mm and 50mm and one for bases between roughly 25 and 100mm ("PaintHolderFull").

Print:
1x Main Body
2x Clip
optional: 1x DistancePlate
1x Holder and Holder_Numbers
or 1x Full_Holder and Full_Holder_Numbers
or, for square bases, 2x Holder_Square or Full_Holder_Square

To assemble it, you need a rubber band, I usually use roughly 40mm diameter ones. Put it on one of the clips (for 40mm, I recommend doing two loops). You now need some kind of hook to pull your rubber loop through the whole assembly (check the images) and put it on the other clip. If you feel like the holders do not fit tight enough, you can add one distance plate on top of the main body. Since this highly depends on your print settings and tolerances, I'd recommend first testing it with and without distance plate and only then gluing it on top of the main body.

This tiny tank represents an older generation of imperial MBTs. Despite its seeming obsolescence many still soldier on. Perfect for games involving tiny robots or tanks in 8mm scale.

This set contains 2 hull weapon options along with numerous sponson gun variations. Uparmored engine compartment variant for siege tank is provided along with track guard option.

4 turret variants are provided:

- standard cannon
- 2 variants of a siege howitzer
- dual automatic cannon

Furthermore, this tank is compatible with other turrets made for similar pattern of mbt made before and hopefully after this one.

Turrets can be printed with a commander cupola opened (heroic tank officers will have to be sourced separately for the time being)

A complete collection of retro-themed Gothic Ruins for table top gaming. These are the full set of 20 ruins that make up the full set of the sample set released earlier, available here: https://cults3d.com/en/3d-model/game/retro-gothic-corner-ruins-set-1

Included in this set are 20 corner ruins, the floor piece for the raised platform on the two tallest corner ruins, plus two floor templates in case anyone wants to break them up a bit for some floor details on the ground level.

Inspired by the cardboard terrain I used in my youth, these turn those 2D flat terrain pieces into fully 3D models, to look more fitting on a modern gaming table!

Scaled to suit 28mm-32mm models, I actually designed them to be printed out at 50% scale for 15mm gaming. They even work well all the way down to 25% scale for 8mm gaming!

Perfect for reliving past wargaming experiences, or for giving your current games a bit of a Retro theme!

Please check out my other wargaming models including the first part of this set, and if you like this set, please consider liking the file, following me, or even making a donation! I love seeing what people do with my models, so please post a make once you've printed them out. I am an amateur, hobby-level designer, and any support helps keep me motivated and supports the hobby activities I can do! Thanks!

Rumbling forward on heavy tracks, the tanks of the Imperial Army are capable of decimating enemy forces with overwhelming firepower. The versatile main battle tank hull is capable of being adapted to feature a wide range of alternate patterns - including devastating artillery.

This set of 79 STLS, and features the heavy 'Bombardier' tank, the long range 'Basil' tank, and the medium 'Euryale' tank, each with variants with and without bulldozer blade, and variants with holes onto which plastic open hatches from comparable plastic tank kits are compatible. There are also additional hull variants, of each tank, including an Imperial Army Bombardier tank, and hulls with extra armour, plus some kit form Bombardiers. Also included are a range of an optional details, including rear-mounted mounted dozer blade (enabling the artillery to 'dig in' prior to firing), rear mounted trailers, support struts, and shells that can be used to add features to any bases you wish to mount the tanks on.

This set has been made to be compatible with 8mm scale main line battle tanks of the Imperial Army in a recently released 8mm grim-dark future wargame.

Please see my other items for a free sample of this set, and a range of other 8mm scale and other wargames and hobby models. I am an enthusiastic amateur designer, self and video-tutorial taught, so am always open to constructive feedback.

This sample hull has been made to be compatible with 8mm scale main line battle tanks of the Imperial Army in a recently released 8mm grim-dark future wargame. They feature a magnet hole, and a peg compatible with existing plastic model turrets.

This sample is free. For the full set, I've priced it cheaply, but priced it as a reflection of the time I took to create such an extensive set. I deeply appreciate all those who support and encourage my work by buying any of my paid designs.

Please see my other items for a free sample of this set, and a range of other 8mm scale and other wargames and hobby models, including a set of compatible turret options for these tanks. I am an enthusiastic amateur designer, self and video-tutorial taught, so am always open to constructive feedback.

I wanted to make a new Frostgrave warband/army for my brother. I came across the dwarf clan and netherforge constructs from dutchmogul (LINK: https://www.thingiverse.com/dutchmogul/designs) and decided to do some remixing. Hope others out there will enjoy these as well.

Each of these are made to be printed with little to no support and are printed best in resin.

If you enjoy this army please consider tipping dutchmogul as much of the files were remixed from his original files.
