Ok, so there are many ways to confiture the Malc, so here are a few of them. I did variants based on the combinations of the mainguns (Vanquisher, Battle Cannon, and Double LasCans with 3 different hull guns (lascanon, HvyBolter, Demolisher) and the 2 different sponsons of Autocannons and LasCans.

These STLs have been painstakingly repaired/ filled and then had the underneath scooped out to reduce suction.

Now, if the one you are seeking doesn't quite exist, just open them into 3D builder and cut/paste to your hearts desire. Its pretty easy - plenty of tutorials on the tube of YOU.

These models are all ultimately based on Danny_Cyanide's work. They were reduced in scale and assembled by Korgaan, but had a lot of internal hollow (especially around the sides/ tracks) that needed to be filled. I did a ton of repair work. Other creators have worked on these prior, but I noticed there were still internal hollows, so the ones here should be a better print with a lower chance of resin leakage - it is difficult to take multi-part STLs and assemble a single print model without some stuff missed - so this is not in any way a criticism of those fine works.

There are 8 tanks here:
BattleTurret with AutoCannonSpn and HvyBolterHull
BattleTurret with LasCannonSpn and HvyBolterHull
BattleTurret with LasCannonSpn and DemolisherHull
DblLasCaneTurret with LasCannonSpn and DemolisherHull
DblLasCaneTurret with LasCannonSpn and HvyBolterHull
DblLasCaneTurret with LasCannonSpn and LascanonHull
VanqTurret with LasCannonSpn and DemolisherHull
VanqTurret with LasCannonSpn and LascanonHull

You play role-playing games or maybe miniature games (the fun ones with the narrative as central), maybe you play both or some hybrid of the two. So you must find yourself occasionally needing some good guys or bad guys to add to the mayhem. Maybe they are unscrupulous gunmen sent by a local crime boss. Maybe they are stalwart citizens ready to defend their town/neighborhood. Maybe they are the latest member of your space faring crew of adventurers, though you just haven't gotten to know them yet. Maybe they are just hired muscle with guns that your gang hired for a bit of extra firepower in the upcoming battle. Maybe they are just random survivors of the Zombie Apocalypse who could be potential friends or foes. The possibilities are endless for a basic miniature with a firearm (call it a rifle, carbine, or lasgun in this case), some light 'flak' armor, and a combat knife. These NPCs might not be the heroes of the day, but they can't be completely ignored either.

(These parts and all my previous listings of Armoured Space Dwarves have been reworked and updated from what they originally were, with the whole model being scaled up by 1.1x, the hands and heads enlarged and the feet reduced in height slightly. The belt buckle detail has also changed; with the rune on the originals changed for a five sided twist release devise. This is the easiest way to check from which version any previously downloaded models are from and if they need to be replaced)

I present my fifth set of armoured space dwarf helmets. These are a few new designs that I felt were worth including.
First is an Astronaut style helmet; for sort of an old Squat and Votann middle-ground, inspired by this image: www.thecommguild.com/gallery/767558-Squats%20and%20Jokaero.html
Second is the Combat helmet, which is meant to look a little closer to a space marine helmet, at least the top half.
Third are a couple of helmets for some upcoming musician models, which will be this army's version of a Chaplain. I think their influence is fairly clear.
Last are the Fighter helmets, which initially were meant to be an expansion of the musician thing, but these should work with standard units.
There are 27 new helmets included here.
These are for use on my armoured space dwarves army, which (apart from the helmets) will look like very short space marines.

These helmets have a different body interface than my earlier versions and to fit them into my Armoured Space Dwarf models will require the V2 Helmet Neck Spacer part. The old design didn't allow the heads to look to the side properly, so this change corrects that.

These models are scaled to match in with the original metal Squat models. To match the scale of other currently available Space Dwarf STL files; these models will need to be scaled up by 1.1x.

Heads still to be made are any special character helmets, like a Medic, Living Ancestor or Guild Master.

I present my forth set of armoured space dwarf helmets. This is a collection of all my previous helmet designs, but expanded, with all my beard versions now available on every different helmet design.
I've also created alternatives for the Visor, Sergeant, Warlord and Hearthguard helmets. Hearthguards now have 4 completely different designs, with two variants of each.
There are now 256 unique helmets total.
These are for use on my armoured space dwarves army, which (apart from the helmets) will look like very short space marines.

These helmets have a different body interface than my earlier versions and to fit them into my Armoured Space Dwarf models will require the V2 Helmet Neck Spacer part. The old design didn't allow the heads to look to the side properly, so this change corrects that.

+++ Berserks units are made up from assault squads of the mos ferocious hand-to-hand fighters in the Stronghold. Armed with bolt pistols and power axes, theyre experts tunnel fighters and excel at clearing buildings and fortifications ahead of the Brotherhood´s advance. All squats are doughty fighters in close combat, but the Berserks units are renowed for their tneacity and courage against even the mightiest opponents without thought for their own looses.

By tradition, Berserkers often wear a striking crest dyed bright red, which is why they refuse to wear combat helmets. The origins of this practice have been lost in the mists of time, but what for many Imperial officers could be an absurd and tactically reprehensible risk, for the Squats is definitive proof of the courage of the Berserkers and their attitude of always spitting in death´s face.+++

I have had these models ready for quite some time, and in fact I also have them printed, but due to lack of time I have not been able to mount and paint them properly to take nice pics.

As I am currently focused on finishing my squat miners (among other lesser things such as graduating from university), I don't think I will resume my Epic Squats in the short term, so I have decided to upload these Berserkers models once and for all and thus finish the infantry forces at least.

Finally this guys come in two flavours: with a boltpistol/power axe combo, and the classic dual wield boltpistols. This is a simple aestetic choice to give variety to the squads.

"Every battlefield the Hostile Environment Troops find themselves on, is a hostile, bombarded and chemically saturated one. Taking trenches, cities and sectors require troops in the thousands, and waiting for weeks or months on end for the right moment to strike. To that end, Command uses Shock Assault Troops, Specialists in lightning warfare.

Other armies decorate these soldiers in honors, having them as elite regiments on their planets. The best of the best.
Not so for the Hostile Environment Troops, for in the hellish condition they find themselves in, a simple hole in their suits means they are living on borrowed time.
Most, but not all, Shock Assault are penal legionaires, promised freedom if they survive a single attack on an enemy position. Very few survive to see reinforcements, fewer still survive long enough for a commissar to excuse them of their sins and turn them free men and women.

The life of a Shock Assault Trooper is a short and deadly life, but their sacrifices turn the tide of battle, saving thousands.

Enlist Today!"

"Every battlefield the Hostile Environment Troops find themselves on, is a hostile, bombarded and chemically saturated one. Taking trenches, cities and sectors require troops in the thousands, and waiting for weeks or months on end for the right moment to strike. To that end, Command uses Shock Assault Troops, Specialists in lightning warfare.

Other armies decorate these soldiers in honors, having them as elite regiments on their planets. The best of the best.
Not so for the Hostile Environment Troops, for in the hellish condition they find themselves in, a simple hole in their suits means they are living on borrowed time.
Most, but not all, Shock Assault are penal legionaires, promised freedom if they survive a single attack on an enemy position. Very few survive to see reinforcements, fewer still survive long enough for a commissar to excuse them of their sins and turn them free men and women.

The life of a Shock Assault Trooper is a short and deadly life, but their sacrifices turn the tide of battle, saving thousands.

Enlist Today!"

This locally-produced heavy fighter, distantly related to the more commonly encountered Thunderbolt, featured heavily in the closing days of the imperial civil war. With poor maneuverability at low altitudes and a dangerously exposed propulsion system, the craft was poorly suited for ground attack work. However, its speed and performance at high altitudes, combined with a pair of lethally accurate long-barreled autocannons made the fighter especially dangerous when either escorting or intercepting bombers and reconnaissance aircraft. Fighting on both sides during the conflict, it was ultimately a shortage of pilots with combat experience that led to horrific casualty rates among its pilots.

Compatible with any 8mm scale wargame. Fits most standard flight stands. Comes in air and ground versions with a variety of ordnance.

+++ Traditionally the elite warriors known as the Hearthguards accompany the Warlord as his personal bodyguards, however their duties do not end there. Hearthguards who are not in the direct service of the Warlord take the position of platoon "captains", leading troops directly into battle. Only when a Hearthguard has proven to be a charismatic leader, a resourceful strategist, and a skilled warrior, he can be considered to be part of the Warlord's personal guard in the future.

+++ The individuals known as Grand Warlords are rarely seen, appearing only in the largest of battles where their great tactical skill and commanding presence are necessary to control a vast army of countless soldiers and monstrous war engines. The title itself is temporary, lasting for the duration of the campaign and generally being awarded to a warlord who stands out above the rest due to his martial achievements, although it is also possible that the Stronghold Lord himself is the one who wears the powerful Exo-armor distinctive of the Great Warlord. However, although it grants great honor and renown, it is a position that implies tremendous responsibility that not everyone is willing to assume or able to fulfill, and for a Great Warlord defeat in battle means ruin and contempt for his clan for generations.

The Living Ancestors are the oldest individuals in Squat society, who form the basis of their religion. For all intents and purposes, the Living Ancestors have abandoned their previous life and identity and are now regarded as vessels of the spirits of the deceased, who observe and judge all the actions of the Squats. In battle they provide wisdom and advice for leaders, and physical support for warriors, because their long life (or perhaps also due to the influence of spirits) has allowed them to develop psychic powers which focus on defense and healing, but they are not completely incapable of attacking if they are forced to do so, although with much disgust. +++


These are a Epic scale Squat Grand Warlord and a Living Ancestor for the Grindel Sronghold army list that you can find here: https://tacticalwargames.net/taccmd/viewtopic.php?f=134&t=33281&sid=422418b4bea515739e1aef8d862588e5

They are considered characters, which means that they do not form individual units but must join an existing one. As you can see in the photos, I attached them to a Warlord unit, because I think it makes sense, but they are not restricted to this unit only.

+++ Warlord is the title of Squat commanders. Warlords are close relatives of Stronghold Lords, and take command of a Stronghold's Brotherhood in battle. On the battlefield he is accompanied by a unit of elite warriors knows as Hearthguard, each one drawn from the Lord's loyal retainers, who formed an aristocratic class in Squat Strongholds. +++


This is a Squat Warlord unit designed for NetEpic Armageddon, in specific for the Grindel Sronghold army list that you can find here: https://tacticalwargames.net/taccmd/viewtopic.php?f=134&t=33281&sid=422418b4bea515739e1aef8d862588e5

The list does not consider the classic Squats exosuits, which gave me some creative freedom and I decided that both the warlord and his hearthguard would be equipped with power armor, for which I used (again) the fantastic models designed by Toftylicious. This also opens the possibility of creating an Epic scale army of squat marines in the distant (grimdark) future.

I have designed two warlord models, one with a thunder hammer and one with a power axe; two hearthguard models, although the difference is almost imperceptible; and a banner-bearing hearthguard.

About the very small supports, i placed each one by hand so probably many are redundant or totally unnecesary for the model size, but overall they gave good results on printing.

Lasers and cannon are interchangable with a range of weapons employed by ground forces, ensuring combat availability in the worst of field conditions.

Compatible with any 8mm wargame setting. Fits most standard flightstands. Options included for air and ground versions with a variety of ordnance included.

UPDATE: 2023-10-11
I didn't expect quite so many downloads so to I've done some extra bits last night that I was going to leave till Christmas. Essentially just some fiddling to create more variety (orks don't really do 'standardised', do they :) ?). More glyph options (the numbers correlate with those in JayMull420's pack for those wanting to fiddle more), some new turrets and, crucially, bolted versions of the dozer glyphs in addition to the welded. Thingiverse couldn't cope with one zip file so I've done three. Hope you enjoy them and any donations to the originators listed above, please, rather than me. Cheers.

Using the fantastic model made by FELIXTHECRAZY (along another Ridgerunner proxy that dissapeared time ago and i dont know who made it), i designed this vehicle mostly for my Squat miners, but i think is suitable for Genestealers Cults too.

I cant assure if is a proper Ridgerunner proxy, because i think this model is smaller, but i added all the weapons and accesories listed in GSC army book for the vehicle in case that someone want to use it in that way. Maybe re-escaling it a bit is enough, but i dont how much, i have never seen a real Ridgerunner model before.

The original model is a single piece, meant to be printed in resin, but my experience printing vehicles in resin is not the best, so i prefer print them on PLA. With that in mind, i separated some pieces of the model to make it suitable for FDM printers, specially small parts that will probably break when you try to remove supports, then the best is print them apart and glue them after. Refer the pics to look where each piece goes

Weapons and accesories are small and detailed, and were designed to be printed in resin. You can try to print them in FDM of course, but they will lost a lot of detail, specially with the mining laser.

About the Spotter, i choose a more "technological" option instead a guy with binoculars. It makes more sense i think, and it saved me a lot of work :P

I included the center hull as one piece and in halves. I printed it as one piece, but I think it's easier and faster to print two pieces. Your choice.

I dont discard make some aditional weapons and accesories in the future.

This cobbled-together flying piece of scrap metal looks as if it should fall apart under a gentle breeze. And yet, it barrels through the air with wild abandon; bullets, bombs and stranger projectiles flying from it in all directions. A mighty flying fortress, this super-scrap bomber all but ignores incoming fire as it passes harmlessly through open superstructure, or as it blasts away rusty plating that was all but falling off anyway, leaving critical structures safe below layers of bolted on scrap metal.

This 67 piece multi-part kit comes with a huge range of options. It can be built with two wing profiles, alternative hulls with differing tailfins, and a range of options for turrets and bombs, many of which can be mirrored for additional variety / symmetry. It includes monstrous 'bouncing bombs' for some truly 'wild' bombing runs!

The kit is designed to be scaled to 8mm scale model games, such as plane warfare games, or those featuring legions of models fighting. It could also be used in 6mm games where Epic Marines fight in Space, a real armageddon level battle. Compatable with ork style armies, it would be a great proxy for a mega bommber or landa. It is sufficiently detailed that an ambitious hobbyist could print it at 400% scale to create a huge center piece model or terrain for 32mm games set in grim dark universes. This would of course require additional cuts to the model!

I am a hobbyist 3D modeller - not a professional 3D designed. However, this project has taken many, many hours of development, test printing and correction. It is my first 'paid for' model, a reflection of the time it took to create. Almost all my other models are currently available for free, so please do look through those if you are interested in further supporting me and my hobby.

I also welcome feedback and will look to develop this model with improvments and additional options in future.

"'Ere We Go, 'Ere We Go, 'Ere We Go!"
— Common Ork chant heard during a Greenskin WAAAGH!
The Orks, also called Greenskins, are a savage, warlike, green-skinned race of humanoids who are spread all across the Milky Way Galaxy. They share many features with Warhammer Fantasy Orcs (and were initially called "Space Orcs" to distinguish them). They are seen by their enemies (pretty much everyone else in the universe) as savage, warlike, and crude, but they are the most successful species in the whole galaxy, outnumbering possibly every other intelligent race, even Mankind (with the very plausible exception of the Tyranids).

Greenskins are one of the most dangerous alien races to plague the galaxy. Numerous beyond belief and driven always to fight and conquer, the Orks threaten every single intelligent species of the galaxy. Orks are possibly the most warlike aliens in the 41st Millennium, and their number is beyond counting. Amid constant, seething tides of war and bloodshed, burgeoning Ork stellar empires rise and fall. Mercifully most are short-lived, soon destroying themselves in a maelstrom of violence and internecine conflict, but should the Orks ever truly unify, they would crush all opposition.

The Orks' unquenchable thirst for battle has always proved their downfall: historically, the Ork tribes have spent much of their time fighting amongst themselves, waging brutal wars with only the strongest surviving. On occasion, an Ork leader will emerge who is mighty enough to defeat his rivals and unite the warring tribes. His success draws other tribes to him, and soon a great WAAAGH! is underway -- partly a migration, partly a holy war that can exterminate the populations of entire star systems. When the Orks are on the rampage, the galaxy trembles, and in these dark days of the End Time, there are more WAAAGH!s rising than ever before recorded.

There have been woolly, tusked Squiggoths seen on battlefields, but the most common appears similar to a dinosaur. It commonly has a howdah on its back, where boyz ride into battle, shooting mounted guns, such as the Supa-lobba as they go. To protect their "ride", Orks usually add armour plating.

As with all Greenskin organisms, the Magos Biologis of the Adeptus Mechanicus have identified Squiggoth's as fungal lifeforms, though they are fairly rare and can only be grown by the specialist breeder Pigdok of the Snakebites Clan. The size of the Squiggoth is determined by the effectiveness of the feed-formula the breeder gives his creature. Less-effective formulas may result in puny Squiggoths while high-quality formulas will see them keep growing and growing.

Squiggoths themselves vary in size and shape, but there are two primary subspecies:

Big Squiggoths are the smaller but more common breed of Squiggoths, either young or whose breeding and feed were less effective and have stunted growth. They most often travel in packs.
Gargantuan Squiggoths are monsterous creatures the size of a small Imperial Titan, bred from the finest secret feed-formulas of the Snake Bites Clan. They are sometimes the favored steeds of powerful Ork Warbosses.

This is a 5 part Calibration tool.



This suite of tests does the following!
Burn in layer calibration
Z-offset calibration
Build Plate Leveling


There are 5 Build Plate Calibration(BPB) plates. Arrange 5 of them like a dice on your build plate. (Each plate has a symbol on it so you know where it goes, and where it came from during measuring.)

Burn in layer calibration
If all the parts print and hold to the build plate, and come off without much difficulty, you have a successful burn in exposure time. Add +4s for medium sized prints, add +8s for large size prints.

Build Plate Leveling
Use calipers to measure them or connect them side by side and do a fingernail check.

If they all print and are closest* to the same thickness, your Build Plate is level!
*0.15mm or less is acceptable for a difference in thickness.

Calibrate your Z-offset.
For this you NEED calipers, the (BPB) rafts should measure 1mm thick on the slot labeled 1mm. Measure them and find the average. Then simply adjust your Z-offset with the difference.
Example, if they measure 0.6mm, increase your z-offset by 0.4mm. Print again and they should now measure 1mm. You will no longer experience layer cruising!!!


For Normal layer calibration for both Dimensional accuracy AND Resin tensile strength! 
See my guide on how to use Boxes of Calibration!
https://docs.google.com/document/d/1Z8fkzOxEgI9sOTwDKI6CeblpnuP4V8ayYVwZrYGmo44/edit#bookmark=id.9ycniz31fm3g

They're now perfect to print with a 0,4mm nozzle and 0,2mm layer height.
I added all the earlier 1,5mm versions to a zip file, they still work perfectly fine.

Annoyed by having to fill the little gaps on hole bases for infantry models or by adding to much mass on top when adding more creative base designs?
Look no further! These bases have huge holes instead of small ones, so you can just fill the entire top of the base with Green Stuff/Milliput/Tamiya-Putty or whatever you like!

They're probably best printed with FDM but they should also work with SLA printers, I only tested them with FDM so far.

!MAKE SURE TO LET THEM COOL OFF INSTEAD OF PULLING THEM OFF THE BUILDPLATE WHILE THEY'RE STILL WARM OR THEY WILL END UP BEING BENT!

The core is printed as a single file but it moves even after printing. you can gently prise it apart if you want to make it easier to paint. When together you can rotate it around itself. When printed you load it into the hull from below into the channel .

Here's my set of modular building elements that allows you to build gothic-like structures for your wargaming terrain. I designed it for FDM printers.

The initial idea was to be able to create simple gothic-like walls in both undamaged and damaged form, so this is the reason why there are no floor tiles just yet.

There are no fancy connecting mechanism - use the glue, Luke! I prefer to use quick-drying basing glue.

**1.0v - Initial Release**

- Includes 27 wall and column modules.

**Updates**

- 18-07-2023: after some more printing, I can confirm that resizing the modules down to 80% still works great. I can also confirm that the modules print easily on a resin printer - with no supports, placed directly on the build plate. To save resin, you can hollow the columns (don't forget to add the drainage holes).

Sci-fi troopers inspired by the 80's classics!

Currently included are lasguns, flamers, meltas, and plasma guns. There are 2 torso variants; one based on the original cover art by John Blanche (the vests), and one based on the actual models (with armor plates over the chest).

All the 15mm pre-assembled models are not merged, so you should be able to easily separate and customize them.

The separate parts will almost certainly NOT fit together if you print them separately. They are intended to be assembled digitally first.

Scale: The 15mm miniatures are a little more on the "heroic" side, about 16-16.5mm at the eye. The fits with many popular 15mm manufacturers, but if you want more "true scale" you should shrink them to about 95%. I have no idea about the 28mm scaling. I don't really own any 28mm miniatures any more.

Progress: There are currently only retro-style weapons, and open faced helmets. I'm planning on doing bare-heads, fully enclosed masks, and more modern style weapons very soon!

Credits:
ZIOCRU for the original bodies, legs, arms, and heads (heavily modified by me)

Here is another one of the true heroes of a grim and dark science fantasy setting, where no one will be missed. That's right, it's another feisty chaos cultist fighting the good fight. He knows he won't be missed, but then again did anyone even notice him the first place. Grim, like I said. However, contrary to the stories that you've been told, each human life isn't valuable solely for the sacrifice it can ultimately make some far away half-dead God King. With determination, some luck, and the favor of the Dark Gods every human has a small chance of escaping the lot fate has given them. And that includes even lowly and humble citizens of the dying Empire, it even includes mere mortal cultists.

Inspired by the new Votann (return of the squats ;-) i had a reason to finally paint my classic squats in combination with new Votann as one big army.
Being an Epic player with a big Squat army, i also wanted to have a land train for both my squats in 40k and for Necromunda, for that is where squats live.
The Space Dwarf Land Train from taaz was a good basis and from there i made a Land Train 2.0 that i tried to give a post-squat and pre-votann vibe.

I upgraded the train-cars with printable tracks and more details (doors, windows, exhaust pipes, new towbars). Then i added runes to get several different looking train-cars.
Furthermore i made new train-car tops because i wanted a different (lower) height and a more detailed weapon design.

Finally and most importantly i completely redesigned the train engine.
It now also is a playable piece of terrain and has details that fit a model this size in 40k.
The sides are based on the sides from the original from taaz, also as a tribute/thanks, but the rest is redesigned from the ground up.

All STL are tested/printed in 40k scale (0.2mm 15% infill) and printable, most of them supportless.

When building Gore Krusha Mega Walkers, greenskin Meks sometimes opt to build massive klanky klaws as melee weapons instead of the often-seen giant saws.


FOR BEST QUALITY PRINT, PLEASE READ ALL(!) OF BELOW:

This highly detailed Klaw Arm is compatible to my Gore Krusha's Mega Walker
https://cults3d.com/en/3d-model/game/gore-krusha-mega-walker

I REALLY recommend a layer high of 0.050 or lower for all parts to get the quality I intended.
Please see the pics of my print, those are all in FDM (0,05mm layer height)!

I tried to keep the need of tree supports low, but I recommend it to use them on some parts - decide for yourself & make sure to set the tree support z-distance to a multiple of 2 (layer height) for optimal removal (keep in mind: layer height 0.05 to 0.075(!) )


----------------------------------------------------------------------
-------------- EXCEPTIONAL 'fings for this model: --------------------
----------------------------------------------------------------------

---------- MOVABLE PARTS ----------
- Most pivot points are actually functional, pose the arm as you want!
- I have included a functional hydraulics option for the klaw, so it can move once assembled.
 -> You need a well calibrated printer to get this hydraulics working. Print all *FlexHydraulics*.stl with wallcount = e.g. 99 to get a massive print without infill.
 -> For the FlexHydraulics pins you need to cut of ca. 10mm of regular 1,75mm filament. (I did not test this in resin, but I guess you could print them)
 -> As an option to the FlexHydraulics there are two fixed versions. Have a look in the parts.
- Print all PINS with wallcount = e.g. 99 to get a massive print without infill.

---------- CABLES and WIRES ----------

KlawArm_03 Bits come with an option to glue in some wires (or filament).
If you use some 0,75mm² or 0,5mm² electrical wires the arm could still be movable :)

---------- Arm on the LEFT or RIGHT? ----------
You can print all parts normally except the shoulder pauldrons. (because of the flat printing side)
-> You have to mirror both pauldrons if you want the arm on the left side of your model (from your point of view)

---------- ASSEMBLY ----------

If you need instructions - just open all files in 3D Builder or e.g. Meshmixer. There you can look where they need to go.

---------- FOLLOWING: ----------

Shame less beggin' for some coins for caffeine I need doin' stuff like that :-)

Please consider a tip ....this highly detailed model was a work of 80h+ of free time!
If you do so, I HIGHLY APPRECIATE YOUR GENEROSITY :-)

Kind regards,
Tersus

Vest is edited to remove rifle ammo pouches. which would make little sense for machinegunners.

Some of you know I did Jenova a while back. Well I wanted the whole crew but the only one I found was low poly, or the collection listed below which is nice but I wanted a bit more detail. About half of this project is a remix, I did check and am allowed to remix the parts I did use. Huge shoutout to the original sculptors.


For those wanting these but don't have a 3d printer, you can use a print service.

Vincents gun

Tifa: Tifa was basically untouched as the original is amazing and stood in for a quality control standard

Chocobo: I thickend the feathers a bit so they print easier

Cait Sith: I cleaned up the stuffed animal part a little and made new wings for it.

Red XII: Cleaned up and leveled out a bit

The others were pretty much only used as an example for the pose.

Cid
Sephiroth

Aeris (other than rod)
Yuffie

Jenova

The chaos cultist who would go on to become known as Daemonlash was a solitary and taciturn individual. Despite his reserved manner this cultist was a skilled warrior and a gifted leader. One day he challenged the leader of his chaos cult to a fight to see who would lead the cult. He was handily defeated by the current cult leader. A certain amount of shame came with being thus defeated, but a more serious problem came with this development. The existing cult leader now saw this cultist as a potential threat, maybe he would make a challenge again one day and win. Everyone in the cult knew that their cult leader would almost certainly maneuver things so that his most recent challenger was never a threat again. Knowing this, the defeated challenger volunteered to become a living host for a warp daemon. As a barely sane living weapon for the Dark Powers the former cultist was no longer a threat to the cult leader's position, but at least he was alive.

The daemon that possessed the cultist who would become known as Daemonlash had a peculiar way of not making any outward changes to his host's physical body. Only when in combat would the daemon transmute his host's flesh in the form of grotesque fleshy tentacles that suddenly burst from the cultist's chest. These tentacles shot forward with explosive speed to entangle, rend, and strangle his foes. At these times the cultist's head would also transform to a ghastly cackling daemonic visage. And thus was born the daemon-infused mutant cultist know as 'Daemonlash.'

----------------------

I have never really liked space marines, it's much more fun to play the underdogs. Also, when it comes to choosing a faction, I find it more fun to play the bad guys. Translate this into a certain grim future setting and you come up with the ultimate bad guy underdogs... Chaos Cultists.

This is the first of what I plan to be a long series of more Chaos Cultists. I mean c'mon, if you tell someone your genetically modified gene enhanced super soldiers in power armor with the best weapons and training possible won a battle, who cares? That is what they are supposed to do. But you tell someone that your hordes of Chaos Cultists defeated, well, anything, then that is a truly impressive victory.

Aside from the obvious cool factor, why might you want to collect Chaos Cultists? Well, as miniatures go they are tremendously useful and versatile. Obviously they have a place on the brutal battlefields of the grim future (where there is only war). What about the close quarters skirmishes pitting one murderous team against another? Chaos Cultists certainly belong in the shadowed depths of the undercity. And for that matter, they belong on every planet in the confines of the empire and beyond, they are the archenemy after all. Suppose you are playing a modern day miniature adventure where a group of fearless individuals battle cosmic horrors from beyond space and time? You are definitely going to need some cultists for that. I could go on, but I think you get the picture. Chaos Cultists might not be the most effective troops, but they are certainly the coolest.

What included;

- Variation of Kaiju Monsters to print loosely based on your favorite giant monster media - Godzilla, Rampage and Pacific Rim) (*provided by Tony Remiz and Todd Faulls)

- Variation Skyscrapers and Warehouse - stackable aka destructible. (*provided by Ralph Attanasia and Charlie Ross)

- Variation Civilian - Car, Truck and People Crowd (*coming soon)
- Variation Army - Tank, Jeep, Airplane, Helicopter (*coming soon)

Rules for Tokyo Rampage.

What you need to play the game.
Terrain features are the none mobile bits that the monsters destroy on their rampages. They may be mounted on any size of base, but the dimensions of the base must be in multiples of 25mm.
Units are the combatants in the game. The types of unit used in the game are summarised below:
Civilians
Civilians are innocent bystanders. Their main purpose is to run, screaming,from the monsters attacking their city and basically get in the way.
Military
Military units range from squads of soldiers to mecha. They defend cities against the attacks of giant monsters.
Monsters
Monsters are the strange creatures that have come to destroy the city. They are not limited to giant lizards, but may include any creature or machine that is bent on destruction. Monsters can also be part of the city defences. However, they have to be careful what they stand on.
Ideally 1/300th scale figures should be used to represent units. Civilian and Military units should be mounted on 25mm square bases. Monsters may use bases of any size, but the base used will show the area the monster occupies.

Sequence Of Play
Each turn consists of the following phases:
Initiative. All players roll 1d6 to determine the number of Actions they may use this turn. The player with the most actions has the initiative.
Active phase. Each player takes one action in order of initiative. This continues until all actions have been taken.
Passive phase. The reactions of units which have not acted in the Active Phase are determined. This is done by rolling on the appropriate reaction table for the unit.
Once all phases in a turn have been completed, the next turn begins.
Actions
Each Action represents an opportunity to attack or move. Units may move and attack several times in one turn, provided enough actions are spent to allow them to do so. Any units of the same side which are in base-to-base contact, and which remain so for the duration of the Action, may be treated as a single unit for the purposes of spending Actions. Actions may not be saved for use in later turns.

Movement
Each unit has a Move Value (MV) and a Move Type. The MV is the distance (in cm) a unit may move per Action. The Move Type is the type of movement a unit uses and is used to determine the effect of terrain on its movement.
Move Types
There are six Move Types used in Trash Tokyo. These are explained below:

AIR
Air movement is flight. Units with this type of movement may have a minimum MV (shown as Max MV/Min MV). Units with a minimum MV must move this distance or they are assumed to have crashed and been destroyed. Units which do not have a minimum MV are able to hover in place.
See terrain effects.

BURROW
Some monsters (and possibly some vehicles) are capable of tunnelling through solid matter. Burrowing units are not placed on the playing area until they surface.
See terrain effects.

G.E.V.
This represents vehicles which use thrusters, ducted fans or anti-gravity systems in order to hover just above the surface they are crossing.
See terrain effects.

GROUND
Ground movement is assumed to be any form of movement which requires direct contact with the ground. This includes legs, wheels and tracks.
See terrain effects.

SUBMARINE
Submarine movement allows units to move underwater. Submerged units are not placed on the playing area until they surface.
See terrain effects.

WATER
This is the ability to cross bodies of water. Ships use this Move Type.
See terrain effects.

Take-offs And Landings
Units with the AIR Move Type may take off or land as part of their movement. In order to do so, they must declare this before they conduct any movement. They must then spend an Action to move in a straight line at their minimum MV. At the end of the move, the unit is either airborne or on the ground. No other Actions may be taken by the unit during this turn.

Terrain
There are three types of terrain in Trash Tokyo: Good, Bad and Impassable. A unit on Good Terrain suffers no penalty to its movement. A unit on Bad Terrain has its movement halved. Units on Impassable Terrain may not move at all. If a unit's move crosses more than one type of terrain, it counts the whole move as being on the worst terrain.
The following table gives examples of terrain for each Move Type.

Move Types
Move type good bad Impassable

Air No high obstacles High Obstacles (high obstacles are things like sky-scrapers,barrage balloons, mountains, very tall trees) N/A

Burrow Solid Matter Not-so solid matter (eg,beneath cities, buildings,badly faulted rock) Everything else

G.E.V. Roads, water, fields Destroyed buildings,woods, rough ground Buildings

Ground Roads, fields Destroyed buildings, rough ground,woods Water, Buildings

Submarine Underwater Water surface Everything else

Water Water surface N/A Everything else

Buildings
Buildings are items of terrain which can be damaged. A building can be anything from a skyscraper to a pylon, or a bridge to a gas tank. . A building is assigned a Defence Value (DV). This determines how fragile the building is. Once a building is destroyed, the area where it stood is considered to be rubble. Some buildings may have special effects associated with them. For example, electricity pylons may electrocute any monster in contact with them, or gas tanks may explode if damaged. The special effects associated with buildings, if any, should be decided upon before play commences.

COMBAT
Units which are capable of carrying out an attack have an Attack Value (AV), a Range and an Attack Type. The AV represents how much damage the attack is capable of doing. Range is the maximum distance (in cm) the attack may be used to. The Attack Type describes the attack and helps determine its effects. Attack Types The following Attack Types are used in Trash Tokyo. Each attack should have at least one Attack Type from this list.
Chemical
This represents attacks which are based upon noxious gases, corrosive liquids or other, similar substances.
Cold
Cold attacks work by lowering the temperature of the target until it suffers damage.
Electrical
The attack uses an electrical charge in order to do damage.
Heat
These are the opposite of Cold attacks. Heat attacks include flamethrowers and Martian heat-rays.
Impact
Impact attacks use kinetic energy to do damage. Most conventional attacks (ie, guns, claws, etc.) are Impact-based.
Light
The attack uses a burst of high intensity light to disable its target. This is usually a laser beam of some description.
Mental
These are attacks which do not manifest themselves physically. Instead, these attacks are more subtle in their operation. A successful mental attack generally allows one player to control another player's units. The exact effects of a given mental attack should be agreed upon by the players.
Radiation
Radiation attacks cover those weapons which use radioactive energy, strange charged particles or other phenomena beloved by physicists.
Sonic
Any attack which uses powerful sound waves is a sonic attack.
An attack may use more than one Attack Type. However, this only increases the chance that it will get past a monster's defences. An attack with more than one Attack Type only rolls for damage once per attack, not once per Attack Type.
Attacking
In order to use an attack, a unit must pick a visible target that is within the range of its attack.
For a unit to use a weapon with a range of 0cm, it must be in base-to-base contact with its target.
Range (and line of sight) is measured between the centres of units. If the path is not obstructed by intervening scenery then the unit may open fire.

Damage
For each point of AV in an attack, the player rolls lD6. Damage is scored as follows:
D6 Damage
1-3 No damage
4,5 1 point of damage
6 2 points of damage
The amount of damage done is totalled up and then applied.
Applying Damage
If a target unit has Damage Points, it suffers damage equal to the amount of damage inflicted by the attack divided by its DV. If a unit's Damage Points ever reach 0, the unit is destroyed.
If a target unit does not have Damage Points, the amount of damage inflicted by an attack is divided by its DV to give a number. A d6 is rolled and the result compared to that number. If the d6 roll is less than the number calculated, the target is destroyed. Otherwise, it is unaffected.
Units with a DV of 0 are automatically destroyed by an attack.
If a unit is vulnerable to a certain Attack Type, the unit is treated as having a DV of 1 against that attack.
Destroyed units are immediately removed from the table.
If a Monster suffers damage, as well as losing Damage Points, the Monster also loses its next Action.

Reaction Tables
In Trash Tokyo, reaction tables are used to control units (or groups of units) which are not under the direct control of a player. This includes units which have not used any Actions in a turn. Each unit (or group of units) is rolled for once per turn. The reaction table conditions are read from left to right and the first applicable column is used. A D6 is rolled, the modifiers added and the result applied. You are encouraged to experiment with these tables, particularly the Monster Reaction Table. After all, not every monster reacts in the same way, or even to the same things. In fact, some of them may even be intelligent...
Civilian Reaction Table
D6 Monster<10cm Defenders<10cm Monster >10cm
1 W W W
2 R W W
3 R R W
4 R R R
5 S R R
6 S S R
Modifiers to the die roll for this reaction table are as follows:
+1 per attack made on unit
-1 per successful attack made on monster
Military Reaction Table
D6 Monster<10cm Monster >10cm
1 A FA
2 A FA
3 MA A
4 MA A
5 R W
6 S W
Modifiers to the die roll for this reaction table are as follows:
+1 per attack made on unit
-1 per successful attack made on monster
-1 Other units within 5cm
-2 Unit in base-to-base contact with other units
Monster Reaction Table
D6 Unit < 10cm Unit > 10cm
1 FA FA
2 FA FA
3 W FA
4 W FA
5 MA W
6 MA W
Modifiers to the die roll for this reaction table are as follows:
+1 per successful attack made on monster
Results
The entries in the reaction tables have the following results:
A Attack
The unit attacks with all he weapons it can use.
F Advance
The unit moves forward.
FA Charge!
Unit moves forward, firing as it goes.
M Retreat!
The unit moves away using up to half its MV.
MA Fighting retreat
The unit moves away losing half its MV, while attacking.
R Run Away!
The unit moves away as fast as possible.
S Scatter!
Infantry and Civilians are removed from the playing area. Vehicles are considered to be abandoned.
W Wait.
The unit stays where it is and does nothing.

By John Wilson

Scenerios

Revenge Of The Giant Radioactive Dinosaur
Downtown Tokyo is threatened by a Giant Radioactive Dinosaur. The citizens have been evacuated and the Monster Defence Forces have been called in. In the meantime, it is up to the army to keep the creature from destroying the city.
This is the standard Trash Tokyo city-stomp. If you get bored with it, try a three-way fight with two monsters fighting against each other and the military trying to keep the damage to a minimum. Alternatively, have a monster on the side of the defenders. Just make sure he doesn't step on anything important.
Units
MONSTERS
1 x GIANT RADIOACTIVE DINOSAUR
Movement:
MV: 10 (Ground)
MV: 5 (submarine)
MV: 5 (Water)
Defences
DV:10
Damage Points: 25
Attacks:
Eye Beams - AV10 (Heat, Light) Range 20
Radioactive Breath - AV20 (Heat,Radiation) Range 10
Hand to Hand - AV25 (Impact) Range 0
Atomic tests in the Antarctic woke this monster from its frozen slumber of 65 million years. It was the first of the monsters to appear.
In combat it has often proven to be vulnerable to ELECTRICAL attacks.
DEFENDERS
12 x HEAVY INFANTRY
Movement:
MV: 2 (Ground)
Defences
DV:2
Damage Points: 0
Attacks:
Heavy Weapon - AV 5 (Impact) Range 20
Personal Weapons - AV5 (Impact) Range 20
This is a squad of infantry armed with a heavy weapon, such as a bazooka or anti tank gun.
3 x JET FIGHTER
Movement:
MV: 40/10 (Air)
Defences
DV:2
Damage Points: 0
Attacks:
Bomb - AV20 (Impact) Range 0
Cannon - AV5 (Impact) Range 20
Missile - AV10 (Impact) Range 40
Each jet fighter is equipped with 1 bomb which affects everything within 5cm of the impact point and 2 missiles. They are destroyed more often by monster hand to hand attacks than is believed possible.
6 x TANK
Movement:
MV: 10 (Ground)
Defences
DV: 5
Damage Points: 0
Attacks:
Gun - AV10 (Impact) Range 20
This is the standard tank used by defence forces on Earth. Note that it does not have any Damage Points.
TOHO TANK
Movement:
MV: 10 (Ground)
Defences
DV: 10
Damage Points: 5
Attacks:
Techno Cannon - AV20 (any 2 Attack types chosen before play) Range 10
This is the best weapon in the defence forces' arsenal. They fire different beams depending on the monster they are facing.
SETUP
The playing area is 1.5m x 1.5m. Place buildings within the playing area as desired. The Defenders may be placed anywhere within 25cm of one edge of the playing area. The monster is placed within 25cm of the opposite edge.
VICTORY CONDITIONS
The Defenders win if they defeat the Monster.
The Monster wins if it defeats the Defenders or destroys more than 50% of the buildings in the playing area.
SPECIAL RULES
Buildings may have special effects. For example - pylons may do an AV4 (ELECTRICAL) RANGE 0 attack or gas tanks may explode. The exact effects should be decided on before play starts.

From The Depths
Strange earthquakes and tidal waves have been reported in the Pacific Ocean. A Naval Task Force discovers a new island has appeared from the depths of the ocean. As the Task Force steams to investigate this occurrence, a hideous monster rises from the depths to bar their way.
Modifications to this scenario include putting primitive warriors on the island and giving the defenders a landing craft and troups. Maybe there is something on the island they have to retrieve?
Units
MONSTERS
1 x ANCIENT GOD
Movement:
MV: 20 (Air)
MV: 10 (Ground)
MV: 5 (submarine)
MV: 5 (Water)
Defences
DV:20
Damage Points: 20
Attacks:
Breath - AV20 (Chemical) Range 10
Hand to Hand - AV30 (Impact) Range 0
This creature was once worshipped by Primitive Man, but an ancient curse trapped it in its temple beneath the ocean. Angered by this, anyone who wakens it must face its wrath.
DEFENDERS
1 x BATTLECRUISER
Movement:
MV: 10 (Water)
Defences
DV: 10
Damage Points: 40
Attacks:
Cannon - AV20 (Impact) Range 50
Guns - AV20 (Impact) Range 20
Torpedo - AV40 (Impact) Range 100
The Cannon attack represents the big guns on the battlecruiser, whilst the Guns represent the combined attacks of all the smaller weapons. If a target comes within range of both the Cannon and the Guns, both may be used at a cost of 1 Action. The Battlecruiser only caries 2 torpedoes.
2 x FRIGATE
Movement:
MV: 20 (Water)
Defences
DV: 5
Damage Points: 20
Attacks:
Guns - AV20 (Impact) Range 20
This is a smaller, less powerful version of the Battlecruiser.
SETUP
The playing area should be a clear area approximately 1.5m x 1.5m. In the centre of the playing area is a tropical island which should be no bigger than 50cm x 50cm
Place the Battlecruiser and the Frigates on one edge of the playing area. Place the Ancient God halfway between the island and the ships.
VICTORY CONDITIONS
The Defenders win if they manage to destroy the Ancient God.
Anything else is a victory for the Ancient God.

Attack Of The Space Roaches
Aliens have landed on Earth. Twenty four hours ago, a flying saucer landed in the middle of the city. An armed guard was placed around it, but nothing happened. Nothing, that is, until the aliens appeared. As General Killmore said, "I could have coped with little green men, but cockroaches?"
Units
ALIENS
1 x FLYING SAUCER
Movement: MV: 50 (Air)
Defences DV:10 Damage Points: 40
Attacks: Heat Ray - AV20 (Heat) Range 50
The favourite craft of discerning extra-terrestrials everywhere. It is armed with a Heat Ray which projects a beam affecting everything within 1cm of its path.
It is vulnerable to Sonic attacks.
2 x HOVER TANK
Movement: MV: 20 (G.E.V.)
Defences DV:10 Damage Points: 10
Attacks: Laser Cannon - AV20 Heat,
Light Range 20
This is the standard alien tank.
12 x Alien Infantry (Cockroaches)
Movement:
MV: 2 (Ground)
Defences
DV: 3
Damage points: 0
Attacks:
Ray gun - AV10 (Heat, Light, Radiation) Range 10
Intelligent alien cockroaches are here and they want our [insert persons of appropriate gender]!
DEFENDERS
6 x TANK
Movement:
MV: 10 (Ground)
Defences
DV: 5
Damage Points: 0
Attacks:
Gun - AV10 (Impact) Range 20
This is the standard tank used by defence forces on Earth. Note that it does not have any Damage Points.
INFANTRY
Movement:
MV: 2 (Ground)
Defences
DV: 2
Damage points: 0
Attacks:
Personal Weapons - AV5 (Impact) Range 20
This is the standard infantry squad as used by defence forces the world over.
ADDITIONAL UNITS
CIVILIANS
Movement:
MV: 2 (Ground)
Defences
DV: 1
Damage Points: 0
Attacks:
YOU HOPE!
These are the standard panic stricken city inhabitants whose sole purpose appears to be acting as corn plasters for monsters.
SETUP
Use a 1.5m x 1.5m playing area. At the centre of the playing area is a 50cm x 50cm clear area. The remainder of the playing area should have buildings and terrain placed in it.
Place the Flying Saucer in the centre of the clear area. The Defender must place his units around the edge of the clear area.
VICTORY CONDITIONS
The Defenders win if they force the Aliens to leave or destroy the Alien forces.
The Aliens win if they destroy the Defenders.
SPECIAL RULES
The city has not been evacuated. Each building contains a base of civilians. Should a building be attacked but not destroyed, the civilians will leave the building. The civilians should be controlled by the Civilian Reaction Table.Alien units may leave and board the Flying Saucer at a rate of 2 units per Action spent.
For this scenario, the Flying Saucer is effectively grounded. It will only move if it loses more than 50% of its Damage Points. If this occurs, the Flying Saucer will take off 1d6 turns later. Any Alien units on the playing area will attempt to return to the Flying Saucer before it leaves. If the Flying Saucer loses 75% of its Damage Points it will leave immediately.

Commentary :

All of the design backgrounds were based on the Roguetrader (1st Edition) and the 2nd and 3rd Edition designs.

As always, based on the design of the time, I mixed the design sensibilities of the present era.

Personally, I recommend that the size of the shoulder pad is 105-108%, and the size of the head is 95%. (That looks good.)

I got a lot of help from my colleague, LegioXIVguy, in determining the ratio and size. So the overall size is about between New edition Chaos space marines and Primaris marines.

Please enjoy the Retro work.

The All-Purpose Carrier lives up to its name as a rugged and dependable platform that has been adapted to almost every role on & off the battlefield.

This all-in-one package of M'khand-pattern All-Purpose Carrier parts allows you to build your ideal APC-based vehicle to your exact needs. Contains all previously released APC-chassis related files***, both free and paid, adapted to 1:300 scale for mass-scale wargames.

Turrets and middles have 2.5x1.25mm holes for magnets. Compatible with all epic scale M'khand-pattern APC & Lemoine Russel turrets.

To use meshmixer builder, open with meshmixer (a free program from autodesk) and ctrl-click in the object browser the items you wish to have as one piece. Then go to File and Export. Your merged piece is ready for repair and slicing.

Alternatively, individual part stls can be assembled in 3Dbuilder or another program of your choice where they should snap together.

***Non-IFV turrets, Christie suspension sides and artillery cannons for unarmoured hulls not included***

2022-12-30: Added track guards to the builder.

2022-12-30: Added new options for sponson and hull-mounted weapons.

2024-01-23: Added missing armoured artillery mounts and cannons.

2024-08-20: Renamed the parts to be much easier to read. Added new turret parts, new SPG, SPM, and scout tank middles, and wheeled sides (wheels themselves should be printed separately)

2024-09-26: Added hatches for side weapon arrays

Have you ever looked at the beloved Angry Spaceguard sets created by Ziocru, LoggyK, and others, and thought to yourself "Well, yes, these guys are ANGRY, but surely they could be equally angry and ALSO fancy?"

Well worry no more! Now, thanks to myself, the aforementioned creators, and a borrowed horse from Andy Woodhead over on Sketchfab, your angry boys can be the fanciest (yet still angry) men in all of space!

Or, well, EVENTUALLY they will be. Right now, I'm mostly uploading these because I have to put some files SOMEWHERE as backup while I try to get my computer fixed, so here's as good a spot as any. Just, you know, Caveat Emptor because this is still very much a Work-In-Progress set.

V 0.2 update: Added new lower bodies, adjusted torsos, put Aquilas on hats and buttons. Replaced the Andy Woodhead horse with one of the 28mm Horses At Ease by BREXIT.

And many thanks to Ben Antilles for reminding me that I needed to take a second look at those legs.

Note that the heads may be a bit too big right now, if they are, set them to size 0.75.

My take on the standard imperial cruisers for battlefleet gothic.

This design is intentionally very close to the original sculpts, though some creative liberties were taken.

All parts have holes for 1x2 mm round magnets so they can be easily magnetized.

WARNING: This project is still heavily WIP. The tolerances on some of the modular parts are a bit off and they may require some force to assemble. It is currently recommended to just glue the head and ram in place, and only magnetize the weapons. If the scale seems wrong on a part, try scaling it up or down by a factor of 10.

ImperialCruiserComplete.stl represents a Lunar-class cruiser.

Improved versions of all parts, more complete cruisers, a main body variant for battlecruisers and nova cannons are all hopefully coming soon.

The cultist who would go on to be known as 'Talon' was scrawny and puny. He was constantly being bullied by the local thugs and gangers in his poor neighborhood. He joined a chaotic cult in hopes of a better life and to escape the foul treatment of his tormentors. Alas, he found that he had only traded one set of bullying torturers for another, for in the chaotic cult strength and power were prized and weakness reviled. The cultist sought out the legendary Master of Possession, Faustus Daemoncaller who was at that time visiting his world in secret. Daemoncaller was only too happy to perform the dreadful and perverse ritual upon the young seeker.

Once joined with the daemon it learned of his past experience and history. Perhaps it was compassion that made the daemon within him transform his body into a massive and brutishly muscled thing with one oversized arm ending in a savage claw. Or perhaps the daemon sensing the dark emotions of it's host, his rage, hatred, and sense of weakness that the daemon fed upon and transformed the young cultist into a form ideal for enacting bloody revenge on all those who had previously plagued him.

After that the cultist earned the name Talon based on his new form and his keen desire to maliciously destroy any who gained his ire. Not long after the old neighbor where Talon was raised became the site of a series of brutal and savage murders which continued for weeks only to end as suddenly as they had began. The unknown perpetrators, or perpetrator, was never identified or apprehended.

[UPDATE 23-01-16] I was not satisfied with the scale and proportions of my first four mutants. So I have uploaded a new STL in a more 'Heroic Scale.' The original version has been retained in a sub-folder.

An improved pattern of the M'khand Pattern Lemoine Russel Battle Tank, with improved suspension and internal layout offering more crew comfort and higher accuracy when firing on the move. Comes with all turret coxial and sponson weapon options offered at larger scales for maximum customisation.

Completed bodies, turrets and middles have 2.5x1.25mm holes for magnets. Compatible with all epic scale M'khand-pattern Lemoine Russel parts and variants. Comes with a variety of decals and effects.

The zip includes all my parts and meshmixer files. With Meshmixer (free program from Autodesk), simply Shift+Click the pieces you want to use and select export under the FILE dropdown menu. Alternatively, parts can be assembled via 3dBuilder, Blender or another software of your choice. Exported pieces are then ready for repair in netfab/3dbuilder/prusaslicer and slicing.

For best results when printing destroyed turrets, include a closed hatch with the turret, weapon and smoke to prevent a small pocket of unprinted resin.

__For printing for LIMP/AT18, increase scale to 125% when slicing__

2023-12-03: Added new options for side weapons and a builder with all my other lemoine russel variants in it.

2023-12-07: Added adapters to fit the turrets to plastic LIMP hulls. Combine with other wanted parts before scaling up 125%

2023-12-07: Split hull weapon mounts from the hulls. Added new hull weapon options. Removed the old redundant builder file.

2024-01-14: Added coronal-designations of the three patterns of turret as well as both a turret-mounted heat ray and heavy flamethrower.

2024-08-24: Added internal side sponsons.

Provides a version of Woddish's excellent Tiny Bigger Tank Fancy APC and Tiny Bigger Awkward Tank and related things that have been sliced into major parts that are enabled to be quickly swapped and edited for customization by changing visibility of components between different options for support turrets, sponsons weapons, hatches, symbols, and track armour to make Land Raider based vehicles (Phobos, Crusader, Redeemer, Helios, and Prometheus variants currently).

All ships in my Tartarus Fleet to make up a whole fleet of ships that would make a good chaotic gothic style fleet.

There are 9 different ship types

7 classes can be built to your style by swapping out broadsides or turrets.

---------------------------------------------------

- Revenant Class battleship
-------

2 x Prow option
1 x Top
1 x Mid section
1 x lower hull

(about 55ml of resin with supports)

---------------------------------------

- Banshee Class Grand Cruiser.
------

2 x Top Option
2 x Hull Option
- 1 hull section has space for imperial broadsides. I have others on my profile as a free download. 3rd party ones will also fit.
1 x Topper for the tower at the back. A turret or other extra bits will fit there also.

---------------------------------------

 - Strigoi Class Heavy Cruiser.
------

3 x Top Hull Types
2 x Bridges

--------------------------------------

- POSSESSED SHIP- STRIGOI CRUISER
1 x Top Hull

---------------------------------------

- Krekavac Class Cruiser.
------

2 x Hull Types
2 x Bridges

------------------------------------

- Lamia Class Light Cruiser.
-------

1 x Top option
3 x Lower Hull options

-------------------------------------

To Build the ships you get:
1 x Launch bay module. (mirror for the other side)
1 x weapon bay module
1 x Single Turret with weapons module - 3 x turrets to fit
3 x smaller turret option. These will fit the bare slots better.
1x Skull Turret
1 x Cargo Module

Extra bits that apart from the forward bridge will fit into the slots :
1 x Forward Bridge
2 x Mast
1 x Radome

---------------------------------------

 - Umkhovu Class Escort.
------

There are 5 bridge options
- Skull Flat
- Skull Forward face
- Tall Bridge
- Dome Brigde
- Cannon in place of a bridge.

- Dybbuk Class Escort.
-----
- With turret slot at the front.

- Svarog Class Escort.
------

The engine bay for the escorts will need to be printed seperatly and stuck in place afterwards. T2_Rear

=================
READY WITH A HOLE FOR A 2MM FLIGHT STAND THAT IS FAIRLY STANDARD. CAN INSTEAD BE FITTED WITH A 4MM MAGNET IF YOU MAGNETISE YOUR STANDS.
(I do have a free stand download but there are loads to pick from) The clear ones in the photo are for display only. The ones with a brass rod are a free download on my profile

For personal use, Not for resale as a digital file or printed copies
========================
Designer notes:

The Heavy cruiser is slightly larger and broader than the Krekavac Cruiser. The bridges will fit but might look a bit lost on the heavy hull.

You may want to paint before sticking together. The internal hangars can be seen inside after assembly.

The Battleship, Grand & Heavy cruiser comes with an optional cargo module to fit on the lower hull. It bulks the hull out and ships in space need extra cargo! It will accept other broadsides but it might look odd with a weapons one there due to the angle. The cargo module will also fit in the regular broadside slots if you want to make a cargo cruiser. I do have 2 other cargo styles that are sold separately

This is a digital 3D printable model of a Mage. Or a king. It’s up to you. The heads, hands, chests, arms, and legs are completely modular and you can switch them as you progress in your character’s story and equip it with different weapons, spells, and accessories.

**The download contains:**
4x head
4x legs
1x base
3x chest
6x arms
Hands wielding different objects
Accessories such as a cloak and a backpack

All pieces of the model are ready to be 3D printed on an SLA printer. They are prepared for inserting cylindrical magnets.

**Magnets we use:**
Diameter 2 mm
Height 0.90 mm

You might be interested also in **2 Sets of Condition markers for DnD**
Funny Modular: https://cults3d.com/en/3d-model/various/funny-magnetic-condition-markers-for-dnd-figures
Practical rings and bases: https://cults3d.com/en/3d-model/various/practical-condition-markers-for-dnd-figures

**SIZE**
At 100% scale the mage’s dimensions are approximately:
Width: 35 mm
Height: 40 mm
Base diameter: 25mm
Neck diameter: 3.10 mm
Lower body diameter: 6.30 mm

You can scale the model as you wish.

**ASSEMBLY**
The holes in the models are prepared for inserting magnets (2mm diameter, 0.90 mm high)

This model is meant to be post-processed after printing. This means inserting magnets, and painting.
Printing settings will vary greatly depending on your specific printer.

Learn how to cut your own figures and prepare them for magnets in our Youtube tutorial:
https://youtu.be/A6QtOraIAfQ

Do you like the model and don't have a 3D printer? There are lots of people who offer 3D printing services these days. Try searching for someone who offers them in your area.

This model for Dungeons and Dragons tabletop gaming was brought to life by 3Demon. We are a group of modeling and 3d printing enthusiasts based in Prague, Czech Republic.
We’ve been making 3D printable models for more than a decade. We make a lot of cosplay accessories but we also make all sorts of interesting 3D models.
You can join our community or just look at more of our creations here: https://3d-mon.com/links

Quite a bit larger than an Imperial Baneblade, a Kill Grinda Mega Fortress is truly a fearsome idol of the brutish Ork gods:
On massive, krushin' trakks, armed with weapons capable of destroying entire hab blocks with one shot, they rumble onwards, where da fORKtress Kaptains points them to.
Only the most powerful Warbosses have 'nuff teef to pay the bestest meks to build these mega-super-heavy assault vehicles.

An IMPORTANT note for the scale :D
- Quote of an imperial agent during a massive Ork encounter on Fungusius Primus:
"Big Mek Gutgrinda once build this thing at a scale of a Baneblade (~79%).... he was KRUSHED and GRINDED brutally to deff by WAAAGHBOSS Gobba Gitkrusha's 'GORKAfORKress' (100% scale)" ;-)



----------------------------------------------------------------------
------- FOR BEST PRINT QUALITY , PLEASE READ ALL(!) OF BELOW: --------
----------------------------------------------------------------------

I REALLY recommend a layer hight of 0.075 or lower for all parts to get the quality I intended.
Please see the pics, those are all printed in FDM (<=0,075mm)!

All parts are printed without tree supports, some parts don't need supports, but please decide for your self. :)

----------------------------------------------------------------------
---------------- EXCEPTIONAL 'fings for this model: ------------------
----------------------------------------------------------------------

---------- Over all printing recommendation! ----------

Many parts have a "flat surface" -> face those to the build plate. Keep in mind, the z-axies does the detailed job!
Detailed sides / most visible sides should be faced towards the cooling fan.

The supa gattla can fit two 5x3mm magnet to be rotatable. The "KillGindaMegaFortress_SupaGattla_Pin.stl" does a similar job, but not as good, I guess... although I never tested the magnets.

The main gun can be assembled in 3 ways:
- Mega Zzappa
- Nukular Shell (with or without spacer, as you like)
- None of both

I printed the supa gattla ammo without a raft, but if you have problems with adhesion, use a raft.
-> If you have concerns about the sharp corners of the ammo belt in FMD, you have the right feeling, but "in the end it doesn't matter", you will not see this issue after assembly.
-> enable "print thin walls" in cura or equivalent in your slicer.

Arrange the lobbas ("KillGrindaMegaFortress_Lobbas02 - 07 & _LazerMarker) as you like, view all files in e.g. 3D Builder or Meshmixer to see how I designed them. The "Lazer sight"-bit is optional, you can replace it with an additional lobba as you like.

---------- Assembly ----------

All parts have a arritation point, so just "move" them until they snap or feel right.
- If you need instructions: just open all files in 3D Builder or e.g. Meshmixer. There you can look where all parts belong to.


---------- FOLLOWING: ----------

Shame less beggin' for some coins for coffein I need doin' stuff like that :-)

Please consider a tip ....this highly detailed model was a work of 100h+ of free time!
If you do so, I HIGHLY APPRECIATE YOUR GENEROSITY :-)

Kind regards,
Tersus

Want to fire some flesh eatin' short range artillery ammunishun that's not a bug?? Rukka Buggys are your vehicle of choice! Slap it! Expolode it!
"How much bity or 'splodin' flesh balls you want to shoot??" - "Yes."


FOR BEST QUALITY PRINT, PLEASE READ ALL(!) OF BELOW:

To print the Rukka Buggy, you need time or a resin printer ;-)
I REALLY recommend a layer high of 0.075mm or lower for all parts to get the quality I intended.
Please see the pics, those are all printed in FDM (<=0,075mm)!

I highly recommend it to use tree supports (at least on the crew) - make sure to set the tree support z-distance to a multiple of 2 (layer hight) for optimal removal (keep in mind: layer hight 0.05 (crew) or 0.075mm (buggy))

---------- Over all printing recommendation (FDM) ----------

- Many parts have a flat surface -> face those to the build plate. Print slow (25mm/s)
- Detaild sides / most visible sides should be faced towards the cooling fan.
- Crew should be printed with tree supports, rotated 45° back (so the face is up). Support Z-distance should be a multiple of 2 to 3 of the layer hight (0.05 - 0.075mm). PRINT SLOW - Outer wall max 25mm/s. You want dem details gooood!

The most difficult parts (actually not the Gobbo Crew...):
- "RuckaBuggy_Rear_02.stl": you need to be super carefull to remove tree supports (they are needed). My test print broke on the bars while removing them. I was able to glue it back on (tip: smooth cracks with a lighter)
- "RuckaBuggy_Front_04.stl": failed 4 times while removing tree supports, combined with other parts. I needed to print this part as a single part with normal supports.

---------- Assembly ----------

If you need instructions - just open all files in 3D Builder or e.g. Meshmixer. There you can look where they go.
Some parts are press fits (e.g. the wheels) you don't need to glue them, unless you print in resin (not tested).
I recommend to "dry fit" the parts with blu tack or a similar reusable putty.


---------- FOLLOWING: ----------

Shame less beggin' for => "Tossin' a coin to your Tersus...." :D

Please consider a tip ....this highly detailed model was a work of many hours of free time!
If you do so, I HIGHLY APPRECIATE YOUR GENEROSITY :-) :-) :-)

Kind regards,
Tersus

Loads of containers and container handling goodness! Stationary container cranes, walking container cranes, quad container haulers, container skates, container land trains, and more! A variety of container stacks! A confusing plethora of files! These containers and handling equipment make a great container yard terrain setup, or just lots of small vehicles and scatter terrain to give your battlefields some life.

Models include:
The big stationary container crane is presented in several models, with the container 'rack' in different positions. A seperate part is included for a container hanging from cables.

Quad mech 'walking' container cranes in several models. They can also use the hanging container part if you print the version with no rack. (Its another quad industrial mech!)

The container Train is a multi-part model of a tractor and one or more trailers to make up a 'train' that is meant to service the stationary cranes. Empty trailers are included along with those loaded with one or two containers.

Container Stackers are trucks with piston lifts that allow them to drive over single containers, or lift high enough to double-stack. Handy for moving containers but can't stack as high as the big walking cranes.

Container skates are a variation of the mech skates (see the mech repair posting!) either loaded or unloaded; they're an alternative to the trains for moving containers and look best when being loaded/unloaded by the walking cranes.

Container stacks in different configurations and heights, along with a few single containers.

A Buildermech with a container flatbed is also included (See my Buildermech posting for lots of other options - the crane version would also be handy in a container yard. Also, see my modular ships to have something the big cranes can offload!

Modeled in 6mm scale.

Originally designed as an upgrade to a Factory kit, Project Abby has now been sculpted to be its own full frame, armor, weaponry, and escort drones.
Past purchasers of the Project Abby (check the URL) upgrade kit are now rewarded for their early support with a free upgrade.
Thank you very much!

----------------------------

With the mysterious Dark Powers making their once-hidden presence more known, new, sinister mech designs have begun to appear on the battlefields of the Junctionworld inter-reality gate networks.

Notable among these new nightmares is a tailed, tentacled monstrosity labeled by intel operatives at the Mercenary Guild as Project Abby.

These warped, spiked, and twisted armors are malevolent in form and purpose. They have a heat cannon on one arm as their primary ranged weapon, while the melee component of their arsenal is composed of an energized whip weapon system. Crackling with plasma, this cluster of mechanical tentacles can be used to impale, crush, or slice through enemy targets. The Abby features a tail-like appendage that performs the same function, protecting the armored walker from the rear.

Project Abby mechs also seem to be nesting grounds for ScytheBots, verminous robot drones that seem to claim the dreaded hulks as mobile nests. These hive-like bots provide a symbiotic layer of protection for the mech, cutting down infantry that venture too close.

Some time ago I was felt very inspired by the 40K scale imperator titan from Zammerak you can find here in Cults, so I started remixing my own head variant, more close to the titan in the Titandeath cover, a design closer to the original Epic imperator model and featuring a full detailed interior cockpit. I used for the remix the head from the zammerak´s titan and a low poly faceplate model here in cults, apart from hundreds of bits from Cults and Thingiverse for the interior detailing.
The size is calibrated to lore 40K scale titan, of about 95-110 cms. It´s compatible with my Imperator model and Grant´s model but it will need to be rescalated about -25%
In the plans if fits OK but when I´ve printed it needed a lot of sanding in the cap part :-( Version 2 features a simplified cap with better fit.
The interior features complete cockpit with monitors, controls, a holographic display and a hiden room bellow with as little chapel and 2 servitors. Hope you like it :-) Complete crew (2 moderatii and 1 princeps) in the donators rewars folder.

This model is remixed from this models:

- For the base I used zammerak´s titan head, you can fin the complete titan in Cults free Here: https://cults3d.com/en/3d-model/game/titanic-church-delivery-system

The first in a series of remixed noise marines to form a complete noise chaos rock band.
This one is to be the vocalist of the band, so I started with a free, general chaos marine, add the retro-like microphone, a also retro-like sonic blaster and the noise backpack. Plus a lot of tiny chaotic decorations such as the severed head, Slaanesh icons, chaos sword etc.
The idea is a band of noise marines clearly in the show-bussines mood, and with a retro look. After all, chaos warriors must wish to have their own idols, true? and the daemonettes? what kind of photo posters do they have in their lair-rooms? that is.

This model is remixed all from free public models:

- For the main body I choose a classic chaos marine from JimsBeanz here in Cluts3D: https://cults3d.com/en/3d-model/game/chaos-space-warrior-with-chain-axe

10mm minotaur berserkers for warmaster revolution (counts-as ogre kingdoms yhetees). Designed to fit 3 per stand.

Yhetees were a difficult unit for me due to their different statline. I eventually settled on charging unarmored berserker minotaurs* to explain:
1) the extra attack
2) the chase everything rule
3) the 3 hits as opposed to the 4 hits for every other minotaur unit

I think this result conveys point 1 ok-ish, point 2 just fine but point 3 not at all (yhetees have a 5+ save). Still, they should at least be visually distinctive enough for an opponent to tell they're not regular infantry or impalers. Their running pose should hint at their role too.

All in all I'm moderately satisfied with how they turned out. I am definitely open to suggestions though!


* the amount of freely available minotaur stls is also fairly limited, doubly so when you're going for a "savage" themed look.

Basilisks are large, eight-legged reptiles with adults typically weighing around 300 pounds and reaching 11 - 13ft. With the ability to poison or petrify their prey, travelers sometimes found objects that looked like pieces of remarkably lifelike stone carvings of wildlife.
