The Gorkabot is a massive armored mech, built as an effigy of a greenskin god! Armed to da teef da Gorkabot krushes all kind of ememys with it's klaw while shredding infantry with hails of bullets from the DAKKA-Storm gun.


In the Gorkabots belly is space for a few greenskins to pop out, if the time is good for some krumpin'!








FOR BEST QUALITY PRINT, PLEASE READ ALL(!) OF BELOW:





To print the Gorkabot, you need time or a resin printer ;-)


I REALLY recommend a layer high of 0.075 or lower for all parts to get the quality I intended.


Please see the pics, those are all printed in FDM (<=0,075mm)!





I tried to keep the need of tree supports low, but I highly recommend it to use them - make sure to set the tree support z-distance to a multiple of 2 (layer hight) for optimal removal (keep in mind: layer hight 0.05 to 0.075(!) )








----------------------------------------------------------------------


-------- EXCEPTIONAL 'fings for this model: ----------


----------------------------------------------------------------------








---------- COMPATIBILITY ----------





Arms and legs should be compatible to my Mega Bots (not testet)





---------- MAIN BODY ----------





"GorkaBot_Belly.stl" prints without tree support! Just use regular supports.


"GorkaBot_Torso.stl" prints without tree support! Just use regular supports. flip the model slightly to the back (see Cura screenshot)


The doors should be printed without supports with a brim (see Cura screenshot)





---------- LEGS ----------





The legs are unique, there is an individual model for the right / left leg. Those are mirrorable / interchangeable if you want.





---------- ARMS----------





The arms should fit 10x4mm magnets (not tested) but also have a ball joint for more posability...





The "GorkaBot_Klaw_Arm_02.stl" should be printed 45° "floating 1,5mm in the air" see my Cura screenshot - this will give you the best quality result!





---------- Over all printing recommendation! ----------





Many parts have a "flat surface" -> face those to the build plate.


Detaild sides / most visible sides should be faced towards the cooling fan.





---------- Assembly ----------





if you need instructions - just open all files in 3D Builder or e.g. Meshmixer. There you can look where they go








---------- FOLLOWING: ----------





Shame less beggin' for some coins for coffein I need doin' stuff like that :-D ;-)





Please consider a tip ....this highly detailed model was a work of 100h+ of free time!


If you do so, I HIGHLY APPRECIATE YOUR GENEROSITY :-) :-) :-)





Kind regards,


Tersus

Hi all, we have 3 models in this one for BFG Eldar factions

We have
1, Void Dragon Class Grand Cruiser (No icons so pick your eldar faction)
2,The Flame of Asuryan which is Prince Yriel Flag ship, belonging to craft world Iyanden, so this on has the Logo of the Iyanden craft world
3, Shadow Point which is part of the Ulthwe craft world, as this ship is more expensive then the Flame of Asuryan, Ive made it stand out with it having 5 Sails, (This model i would recommend printing in the 3 pieces and orientate almost vertical for the 2 side pods to reduce the number of supports on the sails, but if you think you can print it as 1 piece feel free to try using the complete version

Ive added a SMOOTH SAIL version of all 3 ships, just look at the name description for SMOOTH SAIL at the end for that version

Ive printed these in resin in a old resin printer (no 4k here and still they came out great)

The wings when printing in resin as it is thin will try warping slightly, once you have cured the wings in light, heat the wings with a hair dry to allow you to bend back into shape, I used my table as the flat surface and held the wing there until it had cooled to be back straight again

**Go to the "Thing Files" tab to individually download the files - Thingiverse is giving an odd 404 error when trying to use the "Download all files" buttons**

The perfect restaurant for watching S7 broadcasts or kicking back with the local mercs for a beer. This building is designed to be 3D printed as terrain for 6mm tabletop gaming. The top of the building is large and flat enough to support placing units on top in all hexes for playability. The top of version B has additional supports for two edge hexes for extra stability. It is 1 level tall in most areas, except for the front two hexes where it is 1.5 levels tall, if you're playing a specific mecha tabletop game.

There are eight files. For each of version A and B, one has the building on hexes, another is hexless so that you can print the one that fits your playstyle, and there are two more versions that have the text removed from the front of the building. Using the NoText versions, you can paint custom names on the front, print off logos to attach, or leave it blank.

As always, tipping is appreciated at: paypal.me/rainingfire416

Notable features:
-An in-universe themed restaurant name.
-Fantastic custom logo and details to give it a proper BBQ joint look.
-Detailed design including doors, windows, and a detailed roof with greebles.

The model units are in mm and it is scaled such that the hexes are 33mm from flat-to-flat, which is perfect for modern hex maps using 33mm hexes. You can always resize it if your hexes are slightly smaller/larger.

Please post pictures and leave feedback if you make this yourself! I'd love to see prints and use the feedback to adjust overhangs, detail levels, etc. on this model and future ones as well.

**Go to the "Thing Files" tab to individually download the files - Thingiverse is giving an odd 404 error when trying to use the "Download all files" buttons**

The best "coffee-like" substance, imported from Trell I, is available at this small corner shop! Go check Sarna - it's real. This building is designed to be 3D printed as terrain for 6mm tabletop gaming. The top of the building is large and flat enough to support placing units on top in all hexes for playability. It is 1 level tall if you're playing a specific mecha tabletop game.

There are two versions, A and B. They are essentially mirrors of each other so that the shop doors can open to either corner of an intersection. There are eight files. For each of version A and B, one has the building on hexes, another is hexless so that you can print the one that fits your playstyle, and there are two more versions that have the text removed from the front of the building. Using the NoText versions, you can paint custom names on the front, print off logos to attach, or leave it blank.

As always, tipping is appreciated at: paypal.me/rainingfire416

**Notable features:**
-An in-universe themed restaurant name.
-Cute leaf/bean logo.
-Detailed design including doors, windows, and a detailed roof with greebles.

The model units are in mm and it is scaled such that the hexes are 33mm from flat-to-flat, which is perfect for modern hex maps using 33mm hexes. You can always resize it if your hexes are slightly smaller/larger.

Please post pictures and leave feedback if you make this yourself! I'd love to see prints and use the feedback to adjust overhangs, detail levels, etc. on this model and future ones as well.

The Skrappin' Mega Bot is a stompin' armored Mech capable of moving objects without any efforts using it's powerfull trakktor kannon! Dead 'ard

killy saws tear apart every enemy getting to close. Once the Skrappin' Mega Bot krushed some enemy vehicles, turing those into piles of skrapp, it 

can do some quick n' dirty fixin' jobs on allied vehicles or mechs.


FOR BEST QUALITY PRINT, PLEASE READ ALL(!) OF BELOW:

Beneath my Krumpin' Mega Bot this is one of my most detailed models until now!

To print this monster, you need time or a resin printer ;-)
I REALLY recommend a layer high of 0.075 or lower for all parts to get the quality I intended, while designing this model - please see the pics, those

are printed in FDM (<=0,075mm)!

I tried to keep the need of tree supports low, but I highly recommend it to use them - make sure to set the tree support z-distance to a multiple of 2

(layer hight) for optimal removal (keep in mind: layer hight 0.05 to 0.075(!) )

For a few bitz I added a resin version with "_Resin" in the file name - unlike the FDM versions those don't have a flat bottom. (I have not test printed 

these files, but they should be good to go!)

The Trakktor Kannon can be a variant of an actuall (rattling) Kannon, as it lifts up 'eavy objects and throw them with a high velocity to enemy gitz - 

less explosiv, more smashin' - same damage! ;-)

----------------------------------------------------------------------
---------- EXCEPTIONAL 'fings for this model: ----------
----------------------------------------------------------------------


---------- COMPATIBILITY ----------

Most parts are compatible to my Krumpin' Mega Bot, so you can build your variant as you like :)
https://cults3d.com/en/3d-model/game/krumpin-mega-bot

---------- MAIN BODY ----------

You CAN use two 10x4mm Neodym magnets for the junction "hip <> main hull" to get a rotatable/removable body!
As an alternative to the magnets print the file "ScrappinMegaBot_Hip02.stl"

---------- LEGS ----------

The legs are unique, there is a individual model for the right / left leg. Those are mirrorable / interchangeable if you want.

---------- Over all printing recommendation! ----------

Many parts have a "flat surface" - face those to the build plate.

---------- FOLLOWING: ----------

Shame less beggin' for some coins for coffein I need doin' stuff like that :-D ;-)

Please consider a tip ....this HIGH detailed model was a work of 80h+ of free time!
This model is not a simple remix, all parts of my Krumpin' Mega Bot have been reviewed and altered with new details! :-)
If you do so, I HIGHLY APPRECIATE YOUR GENEROSITY :-) :-):-)

Kind regards,
Tersus




40K, 40K ORKS, EPIC40K, ORKS, WARHAMMER40K, WARHAMMER 40K, WH40K, Dread, Mech

Designed up this dealer button to use in home games or have just as something laying around for any poker fan. It was inspired by a dealer button in Pokerstars VR.

Printing:

Ring - Infil to add weight, supports needed for spade inset. Letter embossing doesn't need it.
Spade - Infil to add weight, no supports
Letters - Print flat, already scaled to fit nicely in the embossing
Star - Infil to add weight.

Full print with 4x4x4 walls/top/bottom and 38% infil came to about 48g in weight.

Glue in lettering and spade. Star may need minor sanding but should push fit into the space tightly and not need anything else to secure it.

I created these greeblies to add some visual interest to tabletop terrain, miniatures and all kinds of kit-bashing projects that need a little more spice. ;-)

There is a curved version of most of the parts fitting to a diameter of about 52mm. You might need to scale these parts up or down according to your needs! (I know - some curved STLs seem to have holes which I could not fix, but in the end they printed just fine without auto-repair.)

The robo legs in the pics will be a separate Thing on my profile as soon as I'm ready to publish them.

The light grey parts om the photos are parts from an early 2000s Games Workshop Leman Russ Battle Tank sprue.

UPDATE: Found there was some geometry present in heads 1 and 2 for each type that may present problems, so I went through and cleaned it out. If you printed these with resin before, should be wary of little pockets of resin within the mouth. New ones do not have these voids.

There are a lot of orcish heads about this website, but I wanted to make my own. I started by putting together some shapes, mostly toruses and squished spheres, in the general form I wanted compared to available orcish heads, and then sculpted the finer details, until I was happy enough to make multiple expressions from it.

I couldn't settle on a specific nose or teeth type, so I decided to use both in extra combos with all the facial expressions I sculpted, resulting in twenty, 20, different head combinations.

I wanted something that could be used for a number of orcish plans I have coming up, something that could work for more warfam figures that I may produce. Panzerfauste, the fantasy ww2 with british orcs, is a game these could be used for.

Have fun with them and be creative all!

I was asked by Tsunami79 to add miniatures for the unofficial Heroquest missions.
The Prophet by maxtobiasweber was a good template to work with.

Dungeon Saga:
https://www.rinnegati.net/dungeon-saga-heroquest/

Update:
Maxtobiasweber has released a new hat pack.
I added a vision without a hat to be able to combine them.
(In the current version they should be reduced to approx. 75% so that they fit)
https://www.thingiverse.com/thing:4284204

Remixed from:
https://www.thingiverse.com/thing:3518994
https://www.thingiverse.com/thing:4047924

---
General information

My miniatures are designed to work out of the box with original 28mm Heroquest miniatures.
I always add a version with Heroquest base and one without a base. The weapons and the base are only combined (if possible).
Personally, I now prefer 32mm miniatures. I usually scale them to 112% -115% directly in the slicer.

I am happy about every shared make, especially the painted ones.
By the way i love espresso, so don't hesitate to leave a tip if you like =D

If you are inexperienced with slicer setting, I recommend this one for Ender Printer: http://www.fatdragongames.com/fdgfiles/?p=4934

Designed up this dealer button to use in home games or have just as something laying around for any poker fan. It was inspired by a dealer button in Pokerstars VR.

Printing:

Ring - Infil to add weight, supports needed for spade inset. Letter embossing doesn't need it.
Spade - Infil to add weight, no supports
Letters - Print flat, already scaled to fit nicely in the embossing
Star - Infil to add weight.

Full print with 4x4x4 walls/top/bottom and 38% infil came to about 48g in weight.

Glue in lettering and spade. Star may need minor sanding but should push fit into the space tightly and not need anything else to secure it.

It's a big quad industrial mech! The Drillermech is a BIG mech (for 6mm anyway), intended to operate as an all terrain mobile drilling platform, able to sink a well just about anywhere you might need it to go. 

The model is a little bit elaborate. The default parts are divided to make printing less of a headache. The original .3mf file is included in case you feel the need to split it up further. (Microsoft 3D builder is a decent part splitter and is free).

This mech is modeled from real drilling platforms, with pipe handling arms, a rather large top drive, iron roughneck, and so forth. The big cylinder in the back is the pipe rack, intended to be reloaded from the back or just swapped for another full cylinder. Just remember - don't shoot the active drilling rig, you have no idea what it's sitting on!

Also included is a 'waterline' model for those rigs deployed in shallow water areas.

A classy Chinese restaurant to add to your city, this building is designed to be 3D printed as terrain for 6mm tabletop gaming. The top of the building is large and flat enough to support placing units on top in all hexes for playability. It is 1 level tall if you're playing a specific mecha tabletop game.

There are four files. One has the building on hexes, another is hexless so that you can print the one that fits your playstyle, and there are two more versions that have the text removed from the front of the building. Using the NoText versions, you can paint custom names on the front, print off logos to attach, or leave it blank.

As always, tipping is appreciated at: paypal.me/rainingfire416

**Notable features:**
-Detailed design including doors, windows, and a detailed roof with greebles.
-Asian-inspired font used for the store name.
-Large yin-yang logo made and placed on the front of the restaurant.

The model units are in mm and it is scaled such that the hexes are 33mm from flat-to-flat, which is perfect for modern hex maps using 33mm hexes. You can always resize it if your hexes are slightly smaller/larger.

Please post pictures and leave feedback if you make this yourself! I'd love to see prints and use the feedback to adjust overhangs, detail levels, etc. on this model and future ones as well.

#Pintando Miniaturas painting handle

This handle was inspired by the project from [NakedFury](https://www.thingiverse.com/nakedfury/designs) handle and uses the same "horns" (https://www.thingiverse.com/thing:4270670/files), so grab them over there and say hi for me :)

The result is a collaboration from the community of the Youtube channel:
[Pintando Miniaturas](https://www.youtube.com/pintandominiaturas)
[@pintandominiaturas](https://www.instagram.com/pintandominiaturas)

##Tips
The "granada" is hollow so you can fill with sand if you want more weight in order reduce the chances of tipping your miniatures or even to help out with hand shakes. The hole at the bottom is 4mm in diameter and 2mm deep, appropriate for a small magnet for the same propose.


#Pintando Miniaturas | Apoio para pintura de miniaturas

Esse apoio foi inspirado pelo desgin do [NakedFury](https://www.thingiverse.com/nakedfury/designs) e usa os mesmos "chifres"(https://www.thingiverse.com/thing:4270670/files), então baixe o arquivo por lá e mande um olá por mim :)

O resultado foi graças a colaboração da comunidade do canal do Youtube:
[Pintando Miniaturas](https://www.youtube.com/pintandominiaturas)
[@pintandominiaturas](https://www.instagram.com/pintandominiaturas)

##Dicas
A granada é oca caso você queira preencher com areia para evitar que ela tombe ou até mesmo para ajudar a mitigar pequenos tremores das mãos. O buraci na parte de baixo tem 4mm de diâmetro e 2mm de profundidade, feito para um pequeno imã com o mesmo propósito

The Krumpin' Mega Bot is a hulking, heavily armored monster! Pistons, welded to powerful close combat weapons, such as the Ripper Klaw deliver enormous hydraulik power to every git or vehicle gettin' to close.
Other than the more commonly Deff Bots and or Kans, Krumpin' Mega Bots are usually armed with high speed rattling weapons of high calibers to kill enemies even before reaching them in close combat! (Or just to make horrible loud noise...)

EDIT: Most Parts are compatible to my Skrappin' Mega Bot
https://cults3d.com/en/3d-model/game/skrappin-mega-bot
Build your Bot as you like! :-)

FOR BEST QUALITY PRINT, PLEASE READ ALL(!) OF BELOW:

This is my ambitious model until now!

To print this monster, you need time or a resin printer ;-)
I REALLY recommend a layer high of 0.075 or better for all parts to get the quality I intended, while designing this model - please see the pics, those are printed in FDM

(<=0,075mm)!

I tried to keep the need of tree supports low, but I highly recommend it to use tree supports - make sure to set the tree support z-distance to a multiple of 2 for optimal removal

(keep in mind: layer hight 0.05 to 0.075(!) )

For the Rippa Klaw I added a resin version with "_Resin" in the file name - unlike the FDM versions those don't have a flat bottom. (I have not test printed these files, but they

should be good to go!)

----------------------------------------------------------------------
---------- EXCEPTIONAL 'fings for this model: ----------
----------------------------------------------------------------------


---------- GUN ARM: ----------

THE RATTLA KANNON MAGAZINE IS ROTATABLE IF DONE AS INTENDED!!

For the axies you simply insert usual filament!
If you don't glue the "MegaBot_RattlerKannon_06.stl" to "...05.stl" the "MegaBot_RattlerKannon_Mag.stl" is interchangeable - who knows what might be released in future...... ;-)
-> If you don't want this or don't have filament, just glue the parts as wanted.


Assembly as followed: (please see also the last two pics/screenshots!

1. Stick (NOT glue, if you want it to be removable) together:
"MegaBot_RattlerKannon_05" & "MegaBot_RattlerKannon_06", OPTIONAL: "MegaBot_RattlerKannon_Barrel.stl"

2. Insert a 1.75mm filament (42mm long - as the answer to all questions, lol) into "MegaBot_RattlerKannon_Mag_Back_Spacer.stl", large side first, followed by

"MegaBot_RattlerKannon_Mag".

2.a) Glue on all parts of "MegaBot_RattlerKannon_Mag_Back.stl", if you want more realistic details (even if Ork xD).
2.a.note: Warning: print "MegaBot_RattlerKannon_Mag_Back.stl" with "brim" 3mm+.
They will, regardless of brim width, fall apart after removing the brim. This is intended so you can glue them bitz more random on the Mag!

3. "Dry fit" (NO glue at first!) all parts

3.a) View the last two pics (Tinkercad screenshots)!

3.b) "MegaBot_RattlerKannon_Trigger.stl" to
 "MegaBot_RattlerKannon_Mag_Back_Spacer.stl"

3.c) I recommend to glue in "MegaBot_RattlerKannon_TriggerPin.stl" to "MegaBot_RattlerKannon_Trigger.stl" first.

3.d) Glue the filament between "MegaBot_RattlerKannon_Trigger.stl" & "MegaBot_RattlerKannon_Mag_Back_Spacer.stl"


---------- MAIN BODY ----------

You CAN use two 10x4mm Neodym magnets for the junction "hip <> main hull" to get a rotatable/removable body!

---------- LEGS ----------

The legs are unique, there is a individual model for right / left leg. Those are mirrorable / interchangeable.

---------- Over all printing recommendation! ----------

Many parts have a "flat surface" - face those to the build plate.


---------- FOLLOWING: ----------

Shame less beggin' for some coins for coffein I need doin' stuff like that :-D ;-)

Please consider a tip ....this HIGH detailed model was a work of 100h+ of free time (~50 RL days)! If you do so, I HIGHLY APPRECIATE YOUR GENEROSITY :-) :-):-)

Kind regards,
Tersus

Demon beasts for warmaster both with and without supports using ADeco's awesome minotaur demon. I fattened its lower legs up a bit to keep them from breaking.

10mm demon army
See my collections for the other units; I have a unit for each of the roles in warmaster revolution and a couple of heroes. Note that this army does not inherently match one of the big four chaos gods by design, as I find them dreadfully boring.

Supports
The supports are auto generated by Prusa. To my surprise none of its horns broke off when removing supports, although you should try to be gentle.

Why?
I just got a 3d printer and was looking to get into warmaster with some friends when I noticed that there is no ready to print demon army yet. Given my 0-level modelling skills I instead decided to use existing models to create the army; this unit is one of the outcomes of this project.

Disclaimer
To be sure: none of these models are actually mine. I am a complete hack blundering his way through blender; all I can do is resize models, fatten segments and add cylinders (you may spot some of my handiwork on other models, or here!).

This is my design remix to properly make the most of those soda or beer can you drink while painting or playing warhammer40k. Give them a new life and make they look really cool in your game table.

This pack includes only the pieces to build the preview:

- 2 bottom supports and rings
- front imperial hatch
- back ventilation grille
- side control panel
- side pipe to the ground
- top ventilation fan
- top human access hatch and the ladder to get there

v2 (2021-04-11):

- Added parts needed to build a vertical container with a 330ml slim can. Only needs 2 beds to print in less than 4 hours.

v2.2 (2021-06-20):

- Added Adeptus Mechanicus symbol to 330ml slim version (also can be used as top part in the regular version). Thanks to @Turtlebot for the suggestion.

Also includes the pre-assembled project files for popular slider softwares. 3 beds for short-printing times and get a tank ready in a single day.

All credit goes to:

- Tijnemanske (for his amazing "soda can terrain" design. Search him in thingiverse)
- SevenUnited (for the control panel)
- PERECil (for the top hatch)
- me (I've made the ladder from scratch ^_^)

I had to go far away from dwarves for some times and I decided to start some models for the High Elf Army. Many models we can find on website are either PLA friendly and ugly or Resin printer made and beautiful.

I worked on a very well known resin model to extract whatever I could use and complete with other stuff. Heads are printed separately and the result is quiet nice. It permits to give some randomness to the unit. Hopefully, High Elf Armies are somehow very strict in their appearance and uniforms (like in the Lord of the Rings in which Elves even move at the same time in a coherent ballet).
Swords need some works with sandpaper or stuff like that for a better shape result as they are very thin.

The whole unit was hard to paint because of the tiny details everywhere but it deserved a clean treatment.

PS: the standard is handmade.

Call it IFV, APC or just mobile cover, this little fellow helps your cannon fodder to get closer to the enemy so they can die faster. Have fun!

Included 3 chasis (standard one, standard one with rear aquila and command one) but only 1 turret.

This is a remix but, again, Thingiverse doesn´t allow me to link them properly, here are the part lists:

Chasis: By Mkhand Forgeworld
Multilaser: https://www.thingiverse.com/thing:3049352
Track guards: https://www.thingiverse.com/thing:3647995
Skull insignia: https://www.thingiverse.com/thing:399182
Aquila: http://www.thingiverse.com/thing:1363920
Radar: https://www.thingiverse.com/thing:3753633

UPDATE 26/10/2020: Test printed. They print fine but I broke one of the lasguns from the array on the clean up process and ended up hating the hollowed part (a pain to clean). I will soon upload new models with tougher lasgun arrays and radar receptor, as well as more pronounced aquilas for the command body (they are barely visible).

UPDATE 28/10/2020: Added second versions for standard and command body, as promised. Also included a second version of the turret, it just has a bigger peg.
If you are upscaling the models, consider using the first ones, they are more accurate.
Test printed at 0.04 and 0.02, both went great.

This is a Curtiss-Wright J2 Fury from the game Crimson Skies. **This version is bigger than game pieces and has a little more detail, the idea is to print it to be used as desktop token just for Crimson Skies fans**

**Remember you can leave a tip for the zeppelin crew here: [Beer for the crew](https://www.paypal.com/paypalme/toposolitario)**

Creating Crimson Skies planes for 3D printing is something that no-one has done previously. And it is a shame as the planes are pretty iconic and after many years from it discreet publishing, FASA's Crimson Skies still has a lot of fans who play or are willing to play from time to time.

I started this for testing the VR modelling tool Gravity Sketch, and I found that work flow is so quick that a new plane can be created from zero in almost an hour. First I made the Fury (the one I like most), and the results for it and the Peacemaker were so good that I finally am willing to complete the full series (basic box plus the Balmoral).

In the end... I'll have a good bunch of pieces just to frankenbuild almost any flying perversion just by dragging and dropping! XD

It is not designed to be printer friendly, but it is coming out perfect with resin printers and pretty good in FDM (I suggest to print them vertically with supports growing from the tail).

*Honk if you're a Crimson Skies fan!!*

In the 31st century, this originally Canadian business has rebranded to be even more popular! This building is designed to be 3D printed as terrain for 6mm tabletop gaming. The top of the building is large and flat enough to support placing units on top for playability. It is 2 levels tall on the higher levels and 1 level tall on the lower levels if you're playing a specific mecha tabletop game.

This is a two part print. Part 1 of the building can be used standalone as any large commercial building if you print the version without text and a logo. Part 2 is an automotive center add-on that can be placed on either side of the main building to make it larger, as seen in the photos above.

There are six files. Two have the building sections on hexes, two are hexless so that you can print the ones that fits your playstyle, and there are two more versions of Part 1 that have the text removed from the front of the building. Using the NoText versions, you can populate your tabletop with custom commercial/big-box stores by painting names on the front or printing off logos to attach.

As always, tipping is appreciated at: paypal.me/rainingfire416

Notable features:
-Based off of a very popular Canadian business, using a similar font and building design style.
-Detailed design including large front windows, two main entrances, garage doors, windows, and bollards to protect the building from bad drivers.

The model units are in mm and it is scaled such that the hexes are 33mm from flat-to-flat, which is perfect for modern hex maps using 33mm hexes. You can always resize it if your hexes are slightly smaller/larger.

Please post pictures and leave feedback if you make this yourself! I'd love to see prints and use the feedback to adjust overhangs, detail levels, etc. on this model and future ones as well.

This is the Ravenscroft Coyote from the game Crimson Skies.

**Remember you can leave a tip for the zeppelin crew here: [Beer for the crew](https://www.paypal.com/paypalme/toposolitario)**

Creating Crimson Skies planes for 3D printing is something that no-one has done previously. And it is a shame as the planes are pretty iconic and after many years from it discreet publishing, FASA's Crimson Skies still has a lot of fans who play or are willing to play from time to time.

I started this for testing the VR modelling tool Gravity Sketch, and I found that work flow is so quick that a new plane can be created from zero in almost an hour. First I made the Fury (the one I like most), and the results for it and the Peacemaker were so good that I finally am willing to complete the full series (basic box plus the Balmoral).

In the end... I'll have a good bunch of pieces just to frankenbuild almost any flying perversion just by dragging and dropping! XD

It is not designed to be printer friendly, but it is coming out perfect with resin printers and pretty good in FDM (I suggest to print them vertically with supports growing from the tail).

*Honk if you're a Crimson Skies fan!!*

First I made the Fury (the one I like most), and the results for it and the Peacemaker were so good that I finally am willing to complete the full series (basic box plus the Balmoral).

In the end... I'll have a good bunch of pieces just to frankenbuild almost any flying perversion just by dragging and dropping! XD

It is not designed to be printer friendly, but it is coming out perfect with resin printers and pretty good in FDM (I suggest to print them vertically with supports growing from the tail).

Honk if you're a Crimson Skies fan!!

An airport/spaceport control tower designed to be 3D printed as terrain for 6mm tabletop gaming. The top of the building is large and flat enough to support units placed on top for playability. The top is 5 levels tall and the bottom is 1 level tall if you're playing a specific mecha tabletop game.

There are two files. One each of the building both with and without hexes so that you can print the one that fits your playstyle.

As always, tipping is appreciated at: paypal.me/rainingfire416

Notable features:
-This building goes perfectly with the other military buildings I've designed.
-Detailed design with doors, many windows, and a balcony for viewing base operations.

The model units are in mm and it is scaled such that the hexes are 33mm from flat-to-flat, which is perfect for modern hex maps using 33mm hexes. You can always resize it if your hexes are slightly smaller/larger.

Please post pictures and leave feedback if you make this yourself! I'd love to see prints and use the feedback to adjust overhangs, detail levels, etc. on this model and future ones as well.

This is a re-mix of Smight's lovely Vectored thrust VTOL (https://www.thingiverse.com/thing:4639577). I've added a peg hole to fit my hex flight stand (https://www.thingiverse.com/thing:4766450) as well as included a version of the engines with exhaust that won't need the flight peg. With the exhaust version, you'll need to print it twice with one copy mirrored and print the main body of the VTOL from the original design.

Please see the instructions at https://www.thingiverse.com/thing:4766450 for how I recommend printing the stand.

I had great success printing the aircraft itself on my Ender 3 by angling it up 45 degrees, which greatly reduced layer lines and gave it a clean underside.

8
9

Microfleet Gothic is my terminology for half-scale BFG fleets and gaming. Game-play is conducted on a half-size board, with ranges and movement halved; minis, bases and markers are half-scale as compared to the original models (based primarily on the scale of the original STL files).

All ship models have an insert that accepts a 5x1mm magnet, as do all of the bases in this Thing. 20mm bases have been provided should the 15mm bases be too unstable for your cruiser minis (just be generous to your opponent with Nova Cannon coverage and blast marker contact if you're using 20mm cruiser bases).

The three 3-ship escort bases are convenient, and don't change much in the way of game-play; it's up to the players whether or not to use them.

No markers for orders dice or ordnance are provided; the orders dice can be found elsewhere on Thingi, as can ordnance (though I just use differently-colored 12mm dice to represent these, as they're about the right size for fighter/bombers/boarding craft, and for missiles if using the BFG XR options for torpedoes.

Fleets for the game can be found by searching with the Microfleet tag, or checking my Designs page.

This elite unit is made with experienced warriors, often the tallest and the strongest of their kind to be able to swing huge hammers into the battlefield. They wear large armors, which add to their impressive presence among a dwarven army.

To make them, I had in mind the fact that I hate the GW models showing dwarves holding hammer above their head in a strange movement which should end in the neck of the unit's front rank. I wanted to make a more worthy unit with noble and right standing, cold blooded elite fighters and not a warband with wild drunk smelly dudes.

Each model is made of four parts: body, feet on the base, hammer head and shield. The leader is the only one who has his own "feeted" base. Each body is on the same basis but with head turned and decorated differently (nude, circlet, helmet). You can add more personality to the group by turning hammer's heads on various angles. Be careful with that tip and check that your model can stack on the second rank of the unit before gluing the hammer.
I also made a standard which can take the place of a hammer's head.

Note that the models on the picture have 110% the size of the downloadable ones. I resized them after having printed my whole unit so that I'm stuck with those a little bit too tall dwarves. Yours will be better.

Always waiting to spring up on their enemy, this restaurant chain seems to spread all across the sphere. This building is designed to be 3D printed as terrain for 6mm tabletop gaming. The top of the building is large and flat enough to support a unit placed on top for the hex locations. It is 1 level tall if you're playing a specific mecha tabletop game.

There are four files. One has the building on hexes, another is hexless so that you can print the one that fits your playstyle, and there are two more versions that have the text removed from the front of the building. The versions with text may only look good when printed in resin, so if you print with FDM you may prefer to print the NoText files. In that case, you can paint a name on the front, print off a logo to attach, or leave it blank.

Notable features:
-Building design is based on a version of the real-world equivalent restaurant. The angled entrances in particular.
-Detailed design including doors, windows, a drive through, and a detailed roof with greebles.
-The NoText versions work perfectly well as any generic commercial building. Feel free to be creative and print off logos to decorate your city!

The model units are in mm and it is scaled such that the hexes are 33mm from flat-to-flat, which is perfect for modern hex maps using 33mm hexes. You can always resize it if your hexes are slightly smaller/larger.

Please post pictures and leave feedback if you make this yourself! I'd love to see prints and use the feedback to adjust overhangs, detail levels, etc. on this model and future ones as well.

This is a 6mm residential building for use with 6mm - 1/285 war games, such as Battletech and Epic 40k. It's designed to fix neatly within Battletech standard 33mm hexes like those found on the more recent maps at least.

I've tried to reduce the requirement for supports and on my print I can turn them off altogether on my Ender 3.

This is actually a sample from a much larger collection over here: https://cults3d.com/en/3d-model/game/residential-buildings-for-6mm-1-285-scale-gaming. That collection currently includes over 160 buildings in four different styles and I'll continue to expand it in the future. 

 A free sample of the other style can be found here: https://www.thingiverse.com/thing:4688152.

I sell the complete collection to help justify the amount of time I spend doing this, but I think I have enough free models to game with.

Edit May 2021: I've uploaded a version of this model that is more resin friendly as I've removed all the internal geometry.

Hail, Fellow Scions!

The standard Thermal Cannon that comes from the factory is nice, but I wanted a little bit more.

This matches my alternate carapace gun from my other designs.

I magnetize my Knights at the elbow. There's is a socket there for whatever method you prefer. There are two parts...

1-The Main Gun. I print in a vertical orientation. It takes time, but the barrels don't have droop or supports on them.
2.The Optional Gunshield. This is notched to allow the cannon's sensors to view past it, but still provides a bit of cover.

The gunshield slips over the two barrels of the cannon, and should be glued. Some fitting may be required, depending on your printer.

Make sure you send in pics of your Makes!

Instead of tips, please check out my science fiction series on Amazon. Read the preview chapters, and if you like it, download the ebook.

Armored mech warfare in the arenas and streets of a place called Junctionworld!
https://www.amazon.com/Defiance-Junctionworld-Book-Bear-Ross-ebook/dp/B07XKW213J

Thanks,
JBR

This is a sample of a collection of many gothic sci-fi buildings, for 6mm / 1:285 gaming - primarily Battletech and Epic 40k. I'm selling the full set on [cults3d here](https://cults3d.com/en/3d-model/game/gothic-style-buildings-for-6mm-1-285-scale-gaming) to help justify to my significant other the time I spend working on these :)

The buildings are combinations of tower blocks that equate to level 1, 2 and 3 for when used within Battletech. There are two types of roof, flat and peeked as well as some other embellishments which means all up there are 290 different buildings in the cults3d set, although they're all different combinations of tower blocks.

For Battletech, they are designed to fit entirely within the "standard" Battletech map hexes of 33mm flat edge to flat edge as is used in the current boxed sets. The flat roof versions are also designed to allow Mech models to be placed on them.

The models are designed to be mostly supportless on an FDM printer and have printed fine on my Ender 3.

Edit:: I've repaired the files.

"Each crackle of their rifles, was a death sentence to their enemies. Their old rifles had been replaced for this mission, and the soldiers had been eager to try out the fresh forge-crafted laser rifles. The normal magazines had been exchanged for a power cable, hooked up to the proto-fusion capacitators on their back; standard issue for their regiment; allowing them a much higher rate of fire, and fewer reloads than normal"

3 different variants of snipers intended for 28mm wargaming, in line with the rest of the Hostile Environment Guardsmen I've made, and also includes a standalone sniper rifle. Due to popular requests, I made sure that the cables were much thicker and wider this time, to make them easier for printing and painting.
This is also one of the few times I'll be using legs (by ZioCru, go check out his stuff), as I intend for the models I make to be used as conversion pieces, and not wholly printed models.

Enjoy!

This is a reupload as the original wasn't showing up under my designs, and I also wanted to add another version, with the sword in a resting position and a bionic arm.

"He looked over the horizon, he'd grown accustomed to the ash wastes of Teidon Prime, just like he had with the endless swamps of Delta-64-91. He'd been on countless worlds, each a different home, with different families. Families he'd soon depart with, as he once again would be the only one out of the warzone. He gave a fake smile to the corporal next to him, who smiled back unknowingly that the sergeant had done the same to last 3 men and women assigned to him. "another warzone corporal, another battle to win. Remember your training, and I'll make sure you'll be back home with your family in a couple of months". He donned his mask and yelled orders for the charge, already having said goodbye to those around him"

This is a single model, meant to represent either a veteran sergeant or higher ranking officer of the Hostile Environment Guardsmen.
He's armed with a powered sword, plasma pistol and improved armour against shrapnell.

Remixed from the following parts:
Heroic scale heads for wargaming miniatures 28mm. By Brexit: https://www.thingiverse.com/thing:3217411

https://www.thingiverse.com/thing:4693247

Angry Spaceguard Legs; Angry Spaceguard Arms clean. By ZioCru:
https://www.thingiverse.com/thing:4582571
https://www.thingiverse.com/thing:4580213

Special Thanks to ZioCru for feedback during the creation process

A cute little Japanese restaurant for anywhere in the universe, this building is designed to be 3D printed as terrain for 6mm tabletop gaming. The top of the building is large and flat enough to support a unit placed on top for all 4 hex locations. It is 1 level tall if you're playing a specific mecha tabletop game.

There are four files. One has the building on hexes, another is hexless so that you can print the one that fits your playstyle, and there are two more versions that have the text removed from the front of the building. The versions with text may only look good when printed in resin, so if you print with FDM you may prefer to print the NoText files. In that case, you can paint a name on the front, print off a logo to attach, or leave it blank.

Notable features:
-Nice little window and door designs that evoke a Japanese feel.
-Detailed design including doors, windows, a ladder to the roof, and a detailed roof with greebles.

The model units are in mm and it is scaled such that the hexes are 33mm from flat-to-flat, which is perfect for modern hex maps using 33mm hexes. You can always resize it if your hexes are slightly smaller/larger.

Please post pictures and leave feedback if you make this yourself! I'd love to see prints and use the feedback to adjust overhangs, detail levels, etc. on this model and future ones as well.

Triple F Burger! The most popular fast food joint in the Federated area! This building is designed to be 3D printed as terrain for 6mm tabletop gaming. The top of the building is large and flat enough to support a unit placed on top for all 4 hex locations. It is 1 level tall if you're playing a specific mecha tabletop game.

There are eight files. Four versions of the building - on and off hexes both with and without text. Two large F statues as decorations - one on a hex and one without a hex. And two large "triple F" billboards - one on a hex and one without a hex.

The building versions with text may only look good when printed in resin, so if you print with FDM you may prefer to print the NoText files. In that case, you can paint a name on the front, print off a logo to attach, or leave it blank.

Notable features:
-Detailed design including doors, windows, drive-through window with bollards, a ladder to the roof, and a detailed roof with greebles.
-The F statue is on a small pedestal with 3 flower boxes and benches. These would look best if you flock it nicely or add miniature flowers or shrubs.
-The large F statue is 2 levels tall but will not support a unit. It is meant as a decoration. It will require a little support to print nicely.
-The billboard is also 2 levels tall and may support a unit if you are careful, but it is also meant as a decoration. It will require a little support to print nicely.

The model units are in mm and it is scaled such that the hexes are 33mm from flat-to-flat, which is perfect for modern hex maps using 33mm hexes. You can always resize it if your hexes are slightly smaller/larger.

Please post pictures and leave feedback if you make this yourself! I'd love to see prints and use the feedback to adjust overhangs, detail levels, etc. on this model and future ones as well.

In the distant future, humanity has learnt that hexagonal buildings are superior!

They're hexagonal residential buildings, for 6mm / 1:285 gaming - primarily Battletech but also Epic 40k and other games at that scale.

The buildings are combinations of hexagonal towers that equate to level 1, 2 and 3 within Battletech. I've set level 1 at about 25mm which allows small mechs to still see over them and level 2 at about 55mm which blocks visibility of even the largest mechs I've tested. Each level after that goes up 30mm.

They're designed to fit within the "standard" Battletech map hexes of 33mm flat edge to flat edge as is used in the current boxed sets. They also have a roof designed to allow Mech models to be placed on them.

The models are designed to be mostly supportless on an FDM printer and have printed fine on my Ender 3.

The two models shown are earlier test prints and the final models as uploaded include a couple of more details. I'll be replacing the images once I paint up one of the updated versions.

This is an original work.

JBR

These 15 player character models are collected from various free posts we've made over the years, and come with character record sheets for our [CRUX roleplaying system, which is available as a free download from our own site](http://www.illgottengames.net/cruxuniversalroleplaying), as well as rules for [Pocket-Tactics](http://www.illgottengames.net/pocket-tactics) (our 3d pint-and-play strategy board game) and [Open-Tactics](http://www.illgottengames.net/opentactics) (our open-source, miniatures-agnostic wargaming rules).

All models are supplied without bases and print 100% support free. Daring Delvers are scaled for standard miniature gaming (30mm scale), and 15mm versions are included as well! Blank bases are included for both scales and, if you want a quick tutorial on adding them before printing, [check out this video](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=HGCwjUJVZ-0).

For those of you thinking about [supporting us on Patreon](https://www.patreon.com/illgottengames?fan_landing=true), our patrons get special weekly model releases, access to new storefront releases and our entire back catalog, plus licensing options to sell printed versions of our designs.

This collection of previously released models has been re-scaled and tidied up and will be featured in one of the two starter sets for our current Kickstarter campaign: [Pocket-Tactics Series 2: Coils of Chaos](https://www.kickstarter.com/projects/292543184/pocket-tactics-series-2-coils-of-chaos)

*Hailing from the Bloodlands to the barren north, the Dreth are hulking, cyclopean marauders descended from the demons that once haunted this desert realm.*

All models are supplied without bases and print 100% support free in FDM (with minimal supports required when printing in resin), are scaled for standard miniature gaming (30mm scale), and 15mm scale versions are included as well!

This set includes 6 miniatures (Half-Dreth Raider, Dreth Hurler, Dreth Marauder, Dreth Champion, Dreth Warlock, and Dreth Warlord) plus a wasteland base for either scale. Stat cards for our [OpenTactics](http://www.illgottengames.net/opentactics) free (and open source) wargaming system are also included as a PDF.

For those of you thinking about [supporting us on Patreon](https://www.patreon.com/illgottengames?fan_landing=true), our patrons get special weekly model releases, access to new storefront releases and our entire back catalog, plus licensing options to sell printed versions of our designs.

***See below Re: scale and statues***

Suitable in size (huge) and armament (basically none) to be a Universe-Class Mass Conveyor for the classic tabletop wargame Battlefleet Gothic, and also for games of Rogue Trader. You'll need to dig out your own statues to add, I recommend the following:

https://www.thingiverse.com/thing:2718906

https://www.thingiverse.com/thing:3413744

https://www.thingiverse.com/thing:3669457

https://www.thingiverse.com/thing:153037

You'll either need to smush them together or tweak them separately and glue them the old-fashioned way. There's two slots either side of the prow, one on the prow upper face behind the large antenna, and one near the stern on the large flat platform. See the render for some examples.

With regards to scale, the BFG scaling is logarithmic so smaller vessels are oversized and larger ones are undersized. This keeps model sizes managable. This model is ~130 mm long, however for a more "correct" size it should be around 200 mm (1.5x).

I am not affiliated with GW in any way! Please don't reupload this on Shapeways and the like for commercial use (though you're welcome to upload them to get them printed that way for yourself).

Some connector bitz to use drinking straws as pipes in your scratchbuild wargaming terrain.

For a long time now I avoided using drinking straws in my wargaming scenery builds because i simply didn't like the bending part. It always squished and looked arkward.
Today i came up with this rather simple but effective solution. 3D printed connectors!

The drinking straws I had had a inner diameter of 6.6mm.

If your drinking straws have a different diameter just calculate the needed scaling using the excel sheet i added or by hand [("your diameter" x 100) / 6,6]

There is a version of each connector with and without the part that goes into the drinking straw to secure it.

To replace the mis-scaled original Mantic Basilean Men-at-Arms arms.

I had 80 of the original MAA Basileans with the terribly oversized gorilla arms. I put these together to replace the sword and shield arm and they scale well and look pretty good. When I got these originally I was so disappointed that I shelved the entire army years ago without assembling anything. Now, I can get excited about this great army again!

I also created a spear version with longer shields.

I wanted to use the original Mantic shields, but it was so much work removing the original arm, so I thought these shields would fit the Basileans nicely. Not recommended for FDM printing. I printed on mt Elegoo Mars with using only light supports (Auto) and was able to get quite a few sets on the build plate.

The shield is from cncmodels4you (3946113), but for some reason Thingiverse is not letting me add another remix source - will try to again to add later on.

Rigged version of an ork made by VidovicArts. I used this to create all my ork models so far.

There are a some hidden parts in the file and lots of poses in the pose library of the rig. My workflow with this is as follows:

-Add objects like torsi an weapons to the file an pot them to the right place at the body
-hide all parts you don't need for your boi
-make copy of the rig, the body and all parts you added
-parent all objects to the rig (as objects to specific bones)
-choose a pose from the pose library or create a new one.
-apply all modifiers to the parts
-unparent all objects while keeping their transformation
-boolean unite all objects
-use windows 3D builder to repair any problems in the mesh
-print

Hi, made this a year ago but forgot to upload.
Have not cleaned them but they are support free and most have integrated bed supports.
I made the bottom 1mm of mine to have no top or bottom layers and made it a grid pattern on the infills so that it looks like a mesh.
I have not rotated them into the right orientation, you will have to do something yourself when it is FREE! ;)

They are prepared for Ø3x2mm magnets så that they snapp great together.
I used one orientation of them on the left side and the opposite on the right side of all connection surfaces.

They are optimized for storage so that you can stack them ontop of each other.

The grid pattern on the floors are almost 1" (24,5mm)

Do not mind getting a tip for 100h+ of work ;)

Have fun and enjoy!

A library building designed to be 3D printed as terrain for 6mm tabletop gaming. The top of the building is large and flat enough to support a unit placed on top for all 23 hex locations. It is 6 levels tall if you're playing a specific mecha tabletop game.

There are two files. One has the building on hexes and the other is hexless so that you can print the one that fits your playstyle. Further, there is a second variation of this building, uploaded as “Library 1A” here: https://www.thingiverse.com/thing:4598463

The difference between the two buildings is that 1A is the "original" version, and for 1B the faces that extend from the side of the upper part of the building do not extend as far. If you do not print at a high enough resolution then the bottom part of those faces may sag slightly on 1A. This is not an issue if you print at a high resolution, and can clean up well if you do experience sagging, but you may choose to use 1B to speed up the print time by lowering the resolution, or because your printer resolution cannot go high enough to print those extra faces without issue. 1B makes the building design less prominent, but it means that if you print the building at a low resolution then those parts won't sag at the bottom.

Notable features:
-Detailed design including doors, windows, loading docks, steps to an exterior walkway around the building, and a detailed roof area with greebles such as ducting.
-Visually interesting exterior design.
-The second floor has a curved wall supporting the larger floors on the upper part of the building. This means that the building should print without any supports, and conveniently it is also how the real life building is designed.
-This building is closely based on a real life building. It is designed as a library, but you could use it as an office building or something else if you're creative.
-This building is fairly large and would provide a great addition to your urban terrain.

The model units are in mm and it is scaled such that the hexes are 33mm from flat-to-flat, which is perfect for modern hex maps using 33mm hexes. You can always resize it if your hexes are slightly smaller/larger.

Please post pictures and leave feedback if you make this yourself! I'd love to see prints and use the feedback to adjust overhangs, detail levels, etc. on this model and future ones as well.

A mixed use building designed to be 3D printed as terrain for 6mm tabletop gaming. The top of the building is large and flat enough to support a unit placed on top for all 7 hex locations. It is 2 levels tall if you're playing a specific mecha tabletop game.

There are two files. One has the building on hexes and the other is hexless so that you can print the one that fits your playstyle. Further, there is a second variation of this building, uploaded as “Mixed Use Building 2A” here: https://www.thingiverse.com/thing:4598418

The difference between the two buildings is that 2B has simplified windows and slightly different placement of the windows around the building. This provides you with different versions of the same building that you can use to vary the look of your terrain.

Notable features:
-Detailed design including doors, windows, and a detailed roof area with greebles such as ducting.
-This building is designed as a mixed use building, meaning that the ground floor could be commercial retail space while the upper floors are used as apartments. Of course, you can use the building as whatever you'd like, and you could even use it as a manufacturing facility, storage facility, or something else if you're creative.

The model units are in mm and it is scaled such that the hexes are 33mm from flat-to-flat, which is perfect for modern hex maps using 33mm hexes. You can always resize it if your hexes are slightly smaller/larger.

Assortment of bases for Epic 40k.

Please note that infantry bases are 40x10 mm or 45x15 mm instead of the traditional 40x12!
Also included 20x20 mm, 25x25 mm and 35x25 mm bases.

All bases are 2mm hight and beveled, holes in the infantry bases are 6 mm wide and 1 mm deep (shallow versions 0.5 mm deep, perfect for BaseDepartment models!)

Update 2020/09/16: Added 45x15 bases and standarized the file names.

Update 2021/01/15: Reuploaded all the files with a raised surface, so they can be printed flat on the bed and removed "easily". No need for supports and much improved precision.

UPDATE 2021/01/19: Added 57! decorated options for the 40x10 shallow bases, with an assortment of rocks and soldier corpses. Sources for these details are:
Rocky Bases - 25mm and 50mm Bases by GoonMasterGames https://www.thingiverse.com/thing:4132343

I start from the excelent work of AxoloteGaming and onebitpixel.
Take a look and support them, they are great!
I'll be glad if I can work on something with them someday.

I've got a lot of fun remixing them while learning remixing. I spent more than 300h on them. I could not stop trying new things, And I've only done half what I wanted to. Once I got more free time I'll add more content. Post me what you want to see in the next set.

I made them to be printed as cheap as possible 0.8/1.2 shell 3 or 5% infill.

The minis are only here for scale purpose.

The Dewback made by DaylightInventor, re-sized for 1:18 in 3 different sizes, i.e. adult, female and child, and hollowed for FDM printer. In case you need it for SLA - just add holes and it should be fine. The wall thickness is 2.5 mm for all 3 sizes, should be ok for most FDM printers, might be too thick for SLA, but the model is anyway too big for most SLA printers.

Files are huge. this time really huge ... so here you have the original file in stl and the rest is in zip archives.

In case you decide to re-size for smaller scale, please check that wall thickness is not too small for your printer.

If you like my contribution please hit that Like button. All credits please to the author not to me ( I do not collect tips anyway ) !

Enjoy ;)

I recently started to learn to use Zbrush and this opened a lot of options for me. I decided my first freerun project should be something for wargaming and thus I created this set of heads. They are inspired by Warhammer Tau obviously but I wanted to give them my own curbes. They could be used with my Gue'Ron'Vesa kits to create a interesting mix of ideas and perhaps a new auxiliary aliens that are capable of adapting to the recovered/reverse engineered astartes technology?

They should be printed so that their height is 6-7 mm. My Prusa Slicer says it means the scale should be around 298 but it's best if you guys check it before you decide to print them in larger quantities.

Update: I changed them to be 2mm high, the bottom is now 0,4mm high and the outer walls still 0,8.
They're now perfect to print with a 0,4mm nozzle and 0,2mm layer height.
I added all the earlier 1,5mm versions to a zip file, they still work perfectly fine.

Annoyed by having to fill the little gaps on hole bases for infantry models or by adding to much mass on top when adding more creative base designs?
Look no further! These bases have huge holes instead of small ones, so you can just fill the entire top of the base with Green Stuff/Milliput/Tamiya-Putty or whatever you like!

They're probably best printed with FDM but they should also work with SLA printers, I only tested them with FDM so far.

!MAKE SURE TO LET THEM COOL OFF INSTEAD OF PULLING THEM OFF THE BUILDPLATE WHILE THEY'RE STILL WARM OR THEY WILL END UP BEING BENT!

I used pretty old dried up Green Stuff for the example picture, so please excuse that it looks terrible.

If you want any other size just post a coment and I'll make it for you.

I want to say thanks to all my followers as have pretty much have reached the 500 mark(3 away) You guys are the reason I keep at this and love seeing the positive feedback.

Sorry its been a while since my last upload. I took a break from modeling for a bit, and this has brought me back into it. My next upload will be small and soon. It will be a bits/parts pack for the common Space Communist greebles that will make remixing and modeling a little easier for beginners. Then after that its back to a big release of a complete Retributor Marine and weapons from the Astartes Youtube series done in pretty high poly.

To escort the Grail Reliquary, we needed some fanatic pilgrims. I wanted them to look like religious cultists, with some serious gesture and some stuff for in-battle devotions. I had in mind the picture of fat friars and fighter-monks in dresses and I wanted to be able to customize each minis but with a unique body basis.

The body I did has a very neutral standing which allows many custom stuff like a staff, a standard, a scroll, a sword, a club and of course, a shield. You can use any heads of my bretonnian set on it (the archers' hooded one, the errants' hairless one or even any of you own). For the picture, I did many pilgrims using legit heads, printed heads and even a greenstuff made head). The stuff used to custom is mainly handmade with toothpicks, greenstuff or comes from legit kits.

A body takes 1h15 to be printed.

You'll find the reliquary there:
https://www.thingiverse.com/thing:4520462

Here's a fully remixed fleet for the Mechanical Spaceships - full credit to Italianmoose for creating such an amazing set of models.

Why a remix? I've cleaned up the files a fair bit and added some nice extras to make them more practical for the tabletop.

All options are magnetized - 2x1mm holes for Prow and Weapons Battery choices. Each option has been designed to be WYSIWYG - torpedo tubes, matching lance/weapons batteries from the rulebook to make any combination.

All Hulls are magnetized for 4x2mm flight stands which I've also included - this is perfect for keeping them stable without any issues, tried and tested!

Each hull has an "Embossed" set of prows and hulls. This is so you can choose to have logos or not.

"The Nova Cannons are underslung?!" Yes. I struggled to get them to fit correctly in a way I was happy with. Included are Stock prows and separate Nova Cannon files if you want to add them on yourself, and in the future I may add them as additional files.

[UPDATE 12/9/20] Added Armored Prow Pack (LC rules allow an upgraded prow at the cost of mobility, why not roll them out for all options! Once again significantly modified from Italianmoose base files for Imperial Battleships.)

Light, duelist troops for your noble army of tiny imperial humans. These are 10mm scale and should be printed with 0.025mm layer height, with supports, on a resin printer. I am including the individual models, but also groups of five, and groups of five with pre-added supports for printing. I didn't put these figures into strips, because they're supposed to be loose units, with five models per 40x20mm base.

A pre-Fall Elfdar luxury cruiser. What I imagine the Elfdar would have used when they just wanted to enjoy the feeling of sailing - the Sunjammer. About as pretty and as detailed as I can manage.

So, why something off-the-wall like this? My mother has been fighting cancer for the past few years and it has now become inoperable. When she was younger she used to sail in little boats called Lasers, which were tiny, fragile, fast things. Her boat was called Tiny Dancer (like the Elton John song). Hence when I decided I'd do something to remember her by, I decided on a very fast Eldar ship.

Could I ask as many of you as possible to print one out, so that all over the world there would be some memory of her? Can I also ask that no-one sticks a gun on this, it would just feel wrong.

If you would like to donate, she's said she'd wants to support Macmillan, who have been really lovely helping her out:
https://www.justgiving.com/macmillan

The usual shtick, I am not affiliated with GW in any way! I know it's a bit cheeky to do this but it means a lot to me. Please don't reupload this on Shapeways and the like for commercial use (though you're welcome to upload them to get them printed that way for yourself).

Here is a collection of pieces I have designed as accessories for playing the Blitzkreig Commander (BKC) series of wargames rules. They are designed for 10/12mm scale, but can easily be shrunk/enlarged to suit 6mm or 15mm scale.

There are;-
- 180' arc of fire template (Tanks etc)
- 90' arc of fire template (SPGs etc)
- Artillery Template (200mm diameter)
- 3 types of bases to suit infantry sections, support weapons & field guns - these are bevelled edged (like FoW bases) with a recessed to allow for basing material hiding figure bases and have a hole to take a 7mm dice to indicate hits.
- Simple Dug-In markers to match the above
- Smoke screen piece to mark where smoke has been fired
- Burning tank markers to indicate destroyed AFVs
- Mortar/Artillery burst markers to indicate where fire has landed
- 'S' counters to mark units who have been supressed
- 'O' counters to mark units that have taken opportunity fire.

All have been printed on a Creality Ender 5 Pro using PLA at 210'c and bed temperature of 60'c. I tend to add a brim just for security, but probably not really needed.

If you can think of anything else we need to play BKC let me know! Enjoy!!

Hey folks! Just 3 parts for you to place in your miniatures to customize your characters. Extra thick to increase compatibility. Heavily based in historic milanese armor (high waist large shoulder piece, few folds)
My process to adapt them (blender 2.8+):
1- Load your miniature and the armor parts
2- Place them more or less in position
3- Get the best fit you can simply scaling it (if some parts of the mini stick out, don't worry, get the overall placement)
4 - Try sculpting down (elastic deform brush in blender works wonders!) the parts sticking out in the original mini.
5- Use the sculpting elastic deform to give the final touches.

It normally takes less than 5 min for even somewhat complex models!

Hope you enjoy it!

Description :

1
2
3
4
5

My take on the Epic Necron War Engine. The canoptek machine holds a C'tan in eternal punishment, keeping its core ripped open and perpetually wounded, searching for sustenance. Ghastly claws extend down from its exposed torso, grasping at any organisms it can find to pull into its chest and absorb their essence. Punishment for the C'tan and living alike, the Abattoir serves the Silent King well.

It should fit on 2 prints. Not a super easy model to print and not intended for any larger scale. I have no intentions of separating it further.

Please enjoy!

Designed on Blender and after a lot of issues as never used any kind of design software before, these printed first time without any support on my Anycubic Photon. This is my first ever design and have had a 3d printer for about 2 weeks now.

These fit to the Grot Tank design by AgentSmith99. Only used this design for measuring where the holes need to be. Cogs, Gears and Sprockets Group 1 by EpicNameFail are perfect for adding hubs to wheels, etc.

Please note that track section may be a little tight to fit initially. i thought better tight than too loose.

Now added a single track section. These are best joined up before printing if you need small lengths of track.

Dragon attack? Gnoll raiding party? A group of overpowered murderhobos causing a ruckus?
Whatever the reason, here are some fleeing peasants to add drama to your town scene!
Available in coif+hat and bowl cut, and in both regular and burninated!

This mini is scaled to 28mm, floor to eyeline! If you want it bigger or smaller, feel free to scale it as you please! No base is included, but it is sized to fit on a 1 inch / 25.4mm diameter base. If you would like a 32mm version, scale up to 114.1%.

This was requested by a Patron of mine, so many thanks are given to them for supporting me!

[If you liked this model and want to show your thanks, you can buy me a coffee!](https://ko-fi.com/clayrade)

[And follow me on Instagram!](https://www.instagram.com/clay.rade/)

The Scroggan Ambush Truck is a common improvised low-tech design found on many back-water planets that typically lack their own dedicated FightMech force or other standing professional militaries. The Scroggan Ambush Truck typically mounts 2x SRM-6s and is designed for a single-shot surprise attack, initiated at close range.

The improvised nature of this method of attack often means that the SRM fire-system is burned out during the initiation, which makes it uncommon for the Scroggan to be able to sustain multiple attacks from the same platform.

To build a Scroggan, a single-salvo SRM pod is usually grafted to whatever cargo moving truck is available locally and then positioned on likely FightMech approaches.

The Scroggan Ambush Truck ambush method was originally used on Thingerse III (in the Deep Periphery) in Jun 3020. In this minor action, a well-equipped force of invading FightMech Pirates was temporarily halted in their advance through the planet's urban capital by several Scroggans. Antonius Scroggan, an officer cadet wash-out from the nearby Taurian Constellation who had settled on the planet, organized several small ambushes that delayed the pirates by at least several days.

Scroggan subsequently blew himself up while wiring in some SRM pods incorrectly, and the Pirates soon claimed Thingerse III - despite the harassing inconvenience imposed by a few remaining trucks and minor damage sustained to several ankle actuators.

In tongue-in-cheek homage to Scroggan, the Pirates afterward referred to this method of singe-shot, low-blow, but largely ineffective ambush as the 'Scroggan Cheap-Shot.'

From behind a dense copse of trees, a large shape trundles forth. It sniffs and bends down, broad nose pushing through the detritus of the forest floor, searching for something. Its dense, earthy fur is entwined with a dense mat of hyphae, and you're not entirely sure where it begins and ends, all seemingly connected to the odd collection of mushrooms fruiting over its body. It looks up, chewing absentmindedly on something, stopping suddenly as it notices your party. It eyes you warily, snorting loudly in your direction, before bolting back into the forest's depths, a dense cloud of spores swirling behind it.


This is what happens when hungry hogs start rooting around for fae-touched truffles over a few generations. Alternatively: Porkabello. Porcine Porcini?

This is a 28mm scale miniature, suitable for tabletop roleplaying games such as Dungeons and Dragons or Pathfinder. No base is supplied, but is scaled to fit on a medium sized base (25.4mm / 1 inch diameter).

Day 68: It's Sir Scalesby, your friendly, low-poly scaling dummy!

I thought it was time to update the scaling model I use (sorry, [Sgt.](https://www.thingiverse.com/thing:1465372), but you had your time). This guy can be uploaded into whatever slicing program you're using (or 3d Builder, Blender, whatever) and placed beside a model for the ol' eyeball test if you're adjusting the scale before printing or releasing a design.

People tend to get hung up on scale issues, and there's a lot of misinformation out there. You'll notice that the bigger companies don't tend to list a scale for their models (and often won't engage inquiries about scale). Some random thoughts on scale-

*Most things aren't 28mm.* I know that a lot of models claim to be, and people toss that scale around because it's what they've heard/know, but these days it's pretty uncommon. The majority of miniatures you'll find (3d printed or otherwise) are pretty firmly in the 30 to 32mm range. 

*"Heroic Scale" isn't a scale.* It's a style. It just means that the head and hands are a little larger than they should be. This conveys a slightly cartoonish look that works well with smaller things (making them easily identifiable).

*25mm bases aren't an indication of scale.* This is just the diameter of the base (about .5mm short of an inch), and it's the most commonly used base dimensions for human-ish models in scales ranging from 25mm to 34mm (especially when using laser cut bases, which are pretty popular). In lots of games, an inch is meant to equate to 5 feet. This really depends on scale of the model though, and if you're looking to design terrain based on those numerics, chances are you'll be disappointed with the result.

*Scale isn't determined by the top of the head.* It should be. It really should. But, thanks to some hoary old rules, it's based on the eyeline of a regular tall-ish person. You've got all those accurate model scales, like 1/72 and the like, and we probably should be using those, but... this is what we've got.

*Don't worry about it too much!* If it passes the initial eyeball test, just go with it, especially when you're playing. I generally use models ranging from 28mm to 32mm together, and it's just fine. But, if you are a stickler for these kinds of things, it's lucky that we live in an age where you can scale models easily before you print (and I hope this model helps in your endeavor).

For those of you thinking about [supporting us on Patreon](https://www.patreon.com/illgottengames?fan_landing=true), our patrons get special weekly model releases, access to new storefront releases and our entire back catalog, plus licensing options to sell printed versions of our designs.

Hello this is my first proper upload of anything here!

Been needing Epic Scale Plaguereapers from the Chaos God of Decay for a while, and after converting a few, I got into 3D printing, so this was my first major project. I did use a lot of parts from other builds, so there's a list at the bottom for that. I certainly did not build these things from scratch, I just stuck things together and mutated them, so I can take no credit for the finished designs.

Not all of these are perfect, like I say this is my first real go at designing things. Some will be better printed out as resin, and some in finer detail than what I could manage on my humble Monoprice printer. But they should certainly do the trick on the battlefield.

You'll see some of these have the main cannons attached as one piece, where there are separate cannons to chose from for others. Please feel free to fiddle and adjust these how you see fit.

Rigged version of an ork made by VidovicArts. I used this to create all my ork models so far.

There are a some hidden parts in the file and lots of poses in the pose library of the rig. My workflow with this is as follows:

-Add objects like torsi an weapons to the file an pot them to the right place at the body
-hide all parts you don't need for your boi
-make copy of the rig, the body and all parts you added
-parent all objects to the rig (as objects to specific bones)
-choose a pose from the pose library or create a new one.
-apply all modifiers to the parts
-unparent all objects while keeping their transformation
-boolean unite all objects
-use windows 3D builder to repair any problems in the mesh
-print

This is the shingle texture roller that I demonstrated on the Craft Logic YouTube channel. This is a technique I am experimenting with for making good looking shingles much more quickly than cutting and gluing individual pieces. This is still a work in progress. I have printed a very similar roller successfully but have since made changes and this version has not be printed. The first version was printed on my Ender 3 without any issues and without supports. The changes I made are fairly minimal so I expect this will print just fine as well. These are my versions of the Nova and Gladius Frigates from that no longer available tabletop game of epic space battles in the Gothic Sector. These were made from scratch using base primitives.

Hey Guys,

here are my flight stands for BFG.
I like it when the flight bases are adapted to the size of the ships they are carrying.
While this may not be in line with the rules, it shouldn't play too much of a role.
Escort stand (25mm diam.) have only one deepening for a mini dice to represent the initiative.
(LD value of the ship = 6 + dice value)
light cruiser stands (30mm diam.) have two slots. (1 dice for structure points, second one for LD)
Battle-/Heavy-/Cruisers (35mm diam.)
(2 dices for SP, 1 for LD)
Grand Cruisers (40mm diam.)
(2 dices for SP, 1 for LD)
Battleships (60mm diam.)
(2 dices for SP, 1 for LD)
Ships like Planet Killer will get a customized one later.

I hope you like my creation.
Have fun.

Here are two skink (the reptile itself) inspired miniatures suitable for tabletop roleplaying games. Best printed in resin for fine detail and delicate parts, but feel free to give FDM printing a shot, although I can't guarantee the best results.

[If you liked this model and want to show your thanks, you can buy me a coffee!](https://ko-fi.com/clayrade)

[And follow me on Instagram!](https://www.instagram.com/clay.rade/)


Three files exist for each model: one that is just the figure, one that is just the base, and one where the figure and base have been joined. I personally find printing the base and figure separately and gluing them together is the best for support addition/removal, but that's just me!
