Thingiverse is broken and I cannot add any current links to the remixes, as soon as it's fixed I will add all the information in. Sorry for the inconvenience. 

NOTE: Every part except the backpacks and helmets should be printed at about 85% scale. Do a test print beforehand to make sure that they are scaled correctly to a primaris. They shouldn't excede 40mm in height.

Inspired by the great art of Mo Mukhtar https://www.artstation.com/artwork/RYxAbO

I decided to give it a go and design a 3d printable model kit to host your very own Asta'Vesa soldiers. 

This time I am working only on my own idea with creating a Apothecary equivalent for the Asta'Vesa. These are one of the most important people involved in running an Astarted Force and I cannot imagine Tau Managing to sustain any astartes force without the Apothecaries maintiaining their medical needs. 

Ladies and Gentleman: meat the Apothecary.

They aren't as close to the fanart as I'd like but then again, they are designed to retain their character when being printed as a 28 milimiter scale models so I needed to exagerate some features and smooth out some details and I used some preexisting model sculpts and heavily modified them.

As always, please don't use this kit commercially. This is a gift from me to the community.
However if you would like to tip me, my tip link is https://paypal.me/elmutanto
But this is totally optional and the files are free to download and use non-commercially.

Hope you guys will like this. It was a blast to work on them.

Ulf Mausschnauze was a rat catcher of great renown. As his eyesight deteriorated significantly after years spent in the sewers, he hired his personal lantern bearer, Jim. However, Jim's light was a clear sign for the rats to hide, Ulf became less effective and Jim was fired. Don't worry, Jim was soon hired as a town guard on night shifts.

Suitable for 28mm tabletop games.
Created so that it does not need any supports and prints well on a cheap FDM 3d printer like the Ender 3.
There are variants with square and round bases.

**NOTE** The hireling lantern bearer/town guard seen in the photo <a href="https://www.patreon.com/posts/34888610">available on my Patreon</a>.

Please enjoy!

Remix of various Knight parts with some custom CAD parts to flesh it out, bare hulls to allow for Armour swaps. Pre-Scaled to print at 1:1.

I added struts to some of the overhangs that were difficult to add supports to so you can string them off those (particularly the on the legs)

Note when adding the rear hip cables glue the middle first then when that is set use a hairdryer to heat up the resin and bend the ends into place (use a toothpick or the tip of your scalpel to add the superglue).

The carapace is fairly tight of a fit around the exhausts. I used a needle file to bevel the lower part of the hole and glued it on before painting.

Also included the following:
- Remix of "Quest bot Magaera upgrade AT" by TrueGrits617 - I split up the files into individual parts plus reversed the layout of the carapace and added some grab handles to make it more accurate to the 40k version
- Included some files with supports already added mine printed fine on the Photon with these where they are.

Added 14/08/19 -
- Hekaton Claw Arm with both the Styrix and Mahaera Claw Tips.


Added 15/08/219 -
Styrix Pattern Head, well a fair approximation, in High Poly model.


Serious Note: This was a personal project, to test to see how far I could push the detail on my Photon. it would have been far easier for me to just buy the plastic kits and remix just the armour and weapons lol

So sexy, So sleek, So very deadly. This here is my remix of BloodyLeechs' Grimdark Chrono Trigger Bits. After I had printed it and assembled it, I just, really didnt like it. It just didnt look right. So I gave it a little attention. I removed the tank on the back and in its place put a Reactor with logo. I got the reactor part from AntomanElven and his Back reactor extension bit. I then put a port hole for the new shoulder stubber and mount, which I aquired from https://www.patreon.com/themakerscult. Then I added a logo to the skirt plate which I also got from AntomanElven. I then replaced the head with one from SebTheis' Dominion Crusader head pack. I included 2 head poses. After that I replaced the arms with well, cooler arms which I got from https://www.patreon.com/ghamak. Lastly I replaced the legs. Oh God I hated those legs. So I took the legs from one of my favorite robots of all time, ED209 and welded them on. Now, she's a thing of beauty.

As soon as I have some more time I am going to work on a fist variant. In the mean time I hope you enjoy.

This is simply a collection of things mostly from other people that I used to upgrade an old Eldar Wraithlord to Seer status.

I repaired the elements from jimjimjimmyjim's wraithseer to make them more easily printable as they caused issues with my slicer.

It is all non-scaled and you need to fit it to your needs in your splicer (Cura worked pretty good for that purpose e.g. to inlay the rune into base and Shield)
- Spear is too large (lenght advis 130-140 mm)
- The Base is to high and to small (advise: diameter 65mm - height 8 mm)
- The Shield (longest length 25-30 mm)
- The gun is also too large (overall length should ideally be around 65mm --> scaling the canon trippel to a height of 25-30mm worked for me)
- rune and back is up to your liking.

Unsatisfied with my earlier set of loincloths, I got drunk and set to work. This is the product of my labor. These are flippable, resizeable, to cover loins or do whatever you want with. should work wonderfully for salamanders but also for any other chapters that feature scaled greebly things. I am working on scaled drapes for shoulder pads next so watch out for those. I've printed a couple and the detail is very nice at 0.08 layer height on a stock nozzle, with clearly printed scales and hammers. Print vertically with a small raft (3-5mm is great) for added stability. Printing horizontally works too but scales will be rounder/messier.

Note: can't speak for you resin bois but for FDM printers the smaller studs WILL NOT PRINT. Thus, I hastily added the three larger studs that do.

General information

My miniatures are designed to work out of the box with original 28mm Heroquest miniatures.
I always add a version with Heroquest base and one without a base. The weapons and the base are only combined (if possible).
Personally, I now prefer 32mm miniatures. I usually scale them to 112% -115% directly in the slicer.

Hello! these "high" poly models have been designed for those who are learning, or want to start learning 3D modelling and make their very own miniatures. Its a place holder, or a very basic tool i provide to already start tweaking around, making poses, facial expresions, simple stuff as you keep learning from tutorials in the internet.

They have been designed with heroic proportions: thick hand and foot, bigger head, a medium volume muscle mass (so you can add more muscle/fat or remove volume easily to make a skinny character).

The MALE human has 6 heads tall. The head is 5mm in heigth, and he is 30mm tall (28mm to eyes).

For reference, each square of the GRID is 1x1mm.

I provide a 30x30mm grid and 3 images explaining basic stuff needed to know how and why do certain things regarding importing-exporting files in zBrush. Similar process is needed for other modelling softwares but i only use zBrush.

:::::::::::::

WORKFLOW

If you already know a bit how to use zbrush, now, you have to:

Duplicate the subtool (body in this case) select one of them (hide the original) to make Zremesh, all times neceasry to have aprox 3-5k polys.

Then subdivide about 4 times.

Then activate the original hidden model while still having selected the one you zremeshed (which now is looking smooth and with lot less of details) and select PROJECT.

SO, the details on the original model, will project into the remeshed+subdivided model polys,and woila! now you have the model with multiple levels ofpolys, from 5k to about 1millon.

Now you have a model to POSE in the low poly level and when you are happy, you apply DYNAMESH and start sculpting! (after finishing sculpting you will have to decimate the model, in average a foot miniature like human/elve/orc is around 100K polys)

HEre is an example of how to pose a low poly model:

youtube.com/watch?v=s6THhnv0m6g&fbclid=IwAR18aXLSvvSM9S9y-CkW3kSOtdEgZgrbM_mFq15ockUKAV9Hi6M1iJcRLCE

Cya!

Erramir Orlans.

Death comes in many forms. For this death, it's a ball. Also includes 2 genetic gathering and sampling assistants for free.

For a Devilfish, it's the wrong shape, wrong size, wrong weapon options, and can't technically carry any Kroot, but it's lovely just the same. This was supposed to be a simple joke project that got out of hand. The level of detail isn't the same all over but it's taken up too much of my time and I just need to move on. 

* Comes with open and closed version of the side and back hatches.
* It can either be assembled using 1.75mm filament as alignment pins or 10x2mm magnets.
* Magnets allow for easy breakdown to swap open/closed hatches or easier travel.
* Sides can be printed mirrored for more variety.


You will need heads to complete these models. I recommend purchasing the official box sets for those. Hopefully this will tell THEM that we want more options to add them to our armies. Hello fellow printers!
================
This set of ruins is designed to be assembled in the most easy but still most versatile way. Just print a few wall sections and several copies of the pillars and the rubble. Then glue the parts together with pillars at the corners. With the rubble parts as footings you don't even need to create a base for your walls.


Printing
--------------------
- This print is designed for resin printing but don't hesitate to try it with your FDM printer and post the results!
- The full set you see on the pictures took me about 600ml of resin.
- Since I could not manage to get the parts perfectly plane on the underside you should **lower the STL file about 0.2mm below the print plate**
- No supports or rafts should be needed when these parts are printed upright in resin.


Tips for the building process
--------------------
- Use sandpaper to flatten some parts if necessary.
- Cut some single bricks from Styrofoam to add them to your bases and cover any flaws.
- Mirror your parts for more variety!
- put together two rubble parts to create a whole standalone pile
- consider putting some parts together beforehand in you slicer

This is a proxy representing a Rogue Trader Brigantine from the out-of-print board game Battlefleet Gothic, from Games Workshop.

It contains some elements from other authors. I've used the imperial cruiser from Italianmoose as an inspiration to get the general look, so it blends with the rest of the imperial fleet (although I've given it a more sports-like look), but I've also taken some parts directly from the original model. The statues of the hull are from Harrowtale, but sadly on a FMD printer you will only get the basic shape. The bridge is adapted from Tezca, because I think is very cool and I think it really fits in.
The hull should be printed with supports.

There is also a battery bay from Italianmoose, which is what's intended to go in the hull slots, but if you wish to use a different loadout,the following two links have compatible weapons:
https://www.thingiverse.com/thing:3077193
https://www.thingiverse.com/thing:3489166

The assembled model is there for reference, not for actual printing.

The Warp, the final final frontier. This is the battleground of the Crusaders. Their eternal mission to explore strange new worlds, seek out foul xenos, to boldly go where no marine has gone before... and then kill them.

Lost Crusaders continue on the incredible mission laid before them by the Emperor of Mankind before he went off to sit upon his porcelain throne never to be seen again. Their mission is endless, their resources strained, and lacking all the fun new toys the later generations get. For this proud few band of brothers failure is not an option, at least not one they are willing to entertain.

Using the awesome Macharius tank designed by Mkhand_Industries I put together this custom closed turret (Armageddon) Omega variant. This tank is scaled for Epic 40k however if you would like to print it for use in normal Warhammer 40k simply up scale it by 498.75%. The tank is currently one piece which is how I typically prefer to print on my Ender 3.


Macharius Omega Lore:

The Macharius Omega is a variant of the Macharius Heavy Tank used by the Imperial Guard. The Macharius Omega differs from the standard Macharius tank and its other variants due to its unique main weapon. The Macharius Omega is a war-machine built with a single purpose, the battlefield deployment of the Omega Pattern Plasma Blastgun.

This weapon is a variant of the common Ryza Pattern Plasma Blastgun commonly deployed on the Stormblade super-heavy tank. The Omega Pattern is smaller and lighter than the Ryza Pattern, as it uses a compact generator and smaller force crucible allowing it to be mounted on smaller armoured hulls, such as the Macharius. The downside of this version of the Plasma Blastgun is that it is less stable and generates considerably more heat than the Ryza Pattern, but fortunately it is also much easier to manufacture.

The warships of Chaos will often be a mixture of ship classes, with whole sections of ship swapped out according to the whims of their masters. The wrecked hulks of Imperial ships are particularly prized as being durable and standardized enough to make such modifications relatively straightforward.

Consists of a more true-to-inspiration weapons bay, a new side wing & command deck and a prow & its turrets taken from Dockmaster's Abyssal ships and scaled down. All parts are fully compatible with Imperial Light Cruisers, and barring the wing & command deck can go with Astartes Cruisers. Required weapons options & engines can be found in Imperial Light Cruisers or Astartes Cruisers.

Ideal for games of Battlefleet Gothic, representing orbital support in Epic: Armageddon, and for conquering other, lesser, space games.

I have supplied a model with and without (sans) warpstone bits, so the ship can be used as something less specific than a Skaven vehicle.





A few mistakes were made in the late 90's that ended the presence of a couple of races in the Warhammer 40k universe. I made this ship for myself, to fill in one of those vacancies.


Fluff:

The Hrud (or Skaven) Warren Ship is the Hrudii battleship and their primary center of habitation and culture. The Warren Ships are similar to Eldar Craftworlds in that they serve as permanent homes, though are far smaller and vastly more numerous. Their technology, which is nearly as advanced as the Eldar, is powered by rare Warpstone that only the Hrud have found in great quantities.

Along with the various other Hrudii ship classes, the Warren Ship inhabits pockets in between the Immaterium and our own dimension into which they have "tunneled", using Warpstone to power their extradimensional drives. This gives the Hrud nearly unequaled latitude of travel in the galaxy, and insulates them from the predations of warp entities that would otherwise be greatly attracted to the concentrations of Warpstone that they use.


Millennia of relatively undisturbed advancement and inter-warren trading has created a civilization of royal city-states, ruled ostensibly as oligarchies. A city-state of this fashion, called a Clan House, will consist of many Warren Ships and hundreds of other warships and auxiliary craft, (though it stands to reason that greater craft, perhaps rivaling Eldar Craftworlds in size, exist in these realms).


Given their empire's existence below the surface of the material galaxy, it's no wonder that they have only accidentally and improperly been codified by Imperial Magos Biologis adepts. However, the Hrud do need material supplies, which necessitates plying the darker regions of the material galaxy for food and ore. These "forages" sometimes bring them into conflict with the various sentient races of the galaxy, not least of which are the Squats.

We at Ill Gotten Games are big fans of the [Vintage RPG Podcast](https://www.stitcher.com/podcast/unwinnable-3/the-vintage-rpg-podcast), and after designing a model for Hambone [the hammer-wielding ranger, Johan](https://www.thingiverse.com/thing:3483772)), I made one for Stu as well. This is Greel, an opportunistic (but deep down, gold-hearted) ex-mercenary company leader/current warlock with a magic ring that can turn him into a tree at the first sight of danger. The model prints without support.

If you haven't checked it out, Hambone and Stu (Horvath, from [unwinnable.com](https://unwinnable.com/)) do a weekly podcast where they discuss tabletop games, and do deep dives into RPGs old and new. This all branches off of Stu's excellent [Instagram feed](https://www.instagram.com/vintagerpg/?hl=en), which is always an insightful read if you're into the history and current state of tabletop roleplaying games. We're proud to be [supporting them on Patreon](https://www.patreon.com/vintagerpg/overview), and you should really check out what they're doing/throw them some bones if you like it as much as we do.

The U.L.C. (Urzan Liberty Corps), is our new range that will serve as a proxy guard/sci-fi trooper army (whichever rules set you use, though we'll be designing our own as well). This guy requires support material (though not all of the models will).

CONTEST ALERT!!

We'll be launching a full range of U.L.C. (Urzan Liberty Corps) models soon, and we're doing a painting contest (using this ground pounder in firing pose). All you have to do to enter is download, print, and paint this little fella and post a make here on Thingiverse. We'll be choosing one entry here, and three from our Patreon supporters (posting their entries to our Patreon community page). All winners will receive the printable files early and for free, as they're designed, and before we run the Kickstarter/post them for sale to our [online storefront](http://www.illgottengames.net/products). The grand prize (chosen from Patreon submissions), will also get to request a custom urzan character model. The deadline is 4/30/19, and we'll announce the winners on 5/1/19.

For those of you thinking about supporting us on [Patreon](https://www.patreon.com/illgottengames), our patrons get special access to our store releases as they come out (not to mention license options to sell printed versions of our designs).

Enjoy!

Even within the dogmatic and zealous organisation, that is the Cult of Machines, few can hope to match the fanatism of these monks, who are going so far as to invite the frightening might of the kinetic force into their very own bodies until their skin cracks and their eyes boil in their sockets under the electrical inferno. But the rewards for the faithful far outweigh such petty losses as sight and sense of touch, as they are able to stride into the apocalyptic battlefields of the future almost naked, untouchable by deadly projectiles and shrapnels, for the kinetic force shields their own from the attacks of the unenlightened in a shroud of lightning. If this proves popular, I will work on some other Dinosaurs and Prehistoric Creatures,as well as accessories and variants of this model if requested. I could possibly do things like battle wounds, dino-rider armor, a wall mountable bust, a jungle base. So Please post your makes, hit like, and provide feedback on what you would like to see in the comments.

Ankylosaurus (meaning “fused lizard”) is a genus of thyreophoran dinosaur. Fossils of Ankylosaurus have been found in geologic formations dating to the very end of the Cretaceous Period, between about 68–66 million years ago, in western North America, making it among the last of the non-avian dinosaurs. It was named by Barnum Brown in 1908, and the only species classified in the genus is A. magniventris. A handful of specimens have been excavated to date, but a complete skeleton has not been discovered. Though other members of Ankylosauria are represented by more extensive fossil material, Ankylosaurus is often considered the archetypal member of its group.

The front part of the jaws were covered in a beak, with rows of small, leaf-shaped teeth further behind it. It was covered in armor plates, or osteoderms, with bony half-rings covering the neck, and had a large club on the end of its tail. Bones in the skull and other parts of the body were fused, increasing their strength, and this feature is the source of the genus name.

Compared with modern land animals the adult Ankylosaurus was very large. Some scientists have estimated a length of 11 meters (36 ft).[1] Another reconstruction suggests a much smaller size, at 6.25 m (20.5 ft) long, up to 1.5 m (5 ft) wide and about 1.7 m (5.5 ft) high at the hip.[2] Ankylosaurus may have weighed over 6,000 kilograms (13,000 lb), making it one of the heaviest armored dinosaurs yet discovered. The body shape was low-slung and quite wide. It was quadrupedal, with the hind limbs longer than the forelimbs. Although its feet are still unknown, comparisons with other ankylosaurids suggest Ankylosaurus probably had five toes on each foot. The skull was low and triangular in shape, wider than it was long. The largest known skull measures 64.5 centimeters (25 in) long and 74.5 cm (29 in) wide.[4] Their teeth were weaker than ceratopsid and hadrosaurid dinosaurs of the time, so they probably chewed very little.

If this proves popular, I will work on some other Dinosaurs and Prehistoric Creatures,as well as accessories and variants of this model if requested. I could possibly do things like battle wounds, dino-rider armor, a wall mountable bust, a jungle base. So Please post your makes, hit like, and provide feedback on what you would like to see in the comments.

Parasaurolophus was a hadrosaurid, part of a diverse family of Cretaceous dinosaurs known for their range of bizarre head adornments. This genus is known for its large, elaborate cranial crest, which at its largest forms a long curved tube projecting upwards and back from the skull. Charonosaurus from China, which may have been its closest relative, had a similar skull and potentially a similar crest. Visual recognition of both species and sex, acoustic resonance, and thermoregulation have been proposed as functional explanations for the crest. It is one of the rarer hadrosaurids, known from only a handful of good specimens.

As always I will promote and REWARD the first person to post a quality make (must enable tips on your profile for reward). A quality make is a successful, complete, hopefully decent looking print of at least 80% scale. This doesn't necessarily need painted but extra bonus if it is.

WIP

A collection of bases for playing popular older "6mm" games with modern "8mm" miniatures.

Filename format is BaseSize_CutoutSize_CutoutType_Variation, so "40x20_5x8mm_Inf2_Arrow" is a 40mm by 20mm base with five 8mm by 0.5mm sockets, which are round for Infantry, placed in an arrow formation. Cavalry have ovoid cutouts, and I'm doing several sizes of circular cutouts for infantry so that bigger models don't have to attach by balancing on a dinky wee 6mm integral base.

All the bases are 1.2mm thick with a 65 degree bevelled edge, as I wanted them low-profile and printable on an Ender 3(which likes .4 multiples for layer heights). I've included bases of the same thickness for "8mm" Titanic Robots which are accurately curved should you wish to use those models in both systems.

More will be added over time.

A Thunderhawk Ordinance proxy for Battlefleet Gothic.

A game buddy asked for some prints and I couldn't find a suitable model.

As per 2nd pic...
- The scale is based on the Imperial Attack Craft Models by Mkhand_Industries
https://www.thingiverse.com/thing:2626812
- The shape is heavily borrowed from a similar model on $h@p#w@y$.

While i very much like Mkhand's models (and have printed a number for my Imperial fleet) i've found that the wings are very delicate on my filament printer... as such the thunderhawk wings are all a little chunkier (minimum 0.5mm).

Has now been netfabb'd.

Have test printed. works but it's like tiny tiny (as per last pic).
Re pic: the small ones are what the file produces. the big one is 250% scale just to test that stuff was there and printing.
Re other pic: (not finished) paint just to add some colour.
The teeny-tiny ones do look ok once they're on stands. And there's a fair amount of tricky support cleanup. enjoy.

Note: For my marine fleet i've printed these at 133%. just to get a bit more 'detail' and less blobbular. these are the yellowish ones. note that for sticking them to the bases i just use some chopped filament, was easier than printing the bases with stands as they were coming out horrible.

I revisit the city of Ulvheim. This time we leave to craftsmen quarters and come to the powerfull nobles and rich merchants. Ulvheim B is a modular set of pieces that can be used to make relative intact as well as ruin buildings. You can print as many as you like and make something really gigantic.

I have tried to make a manual in with the images. Please comment if you have opinions on this.

The flat pieces use the shorter peg. Walls use the regular peg. For best stability, glue the tapered end of the peg into the hole from the bottom of each piece.

Noticed the backpack was wrong on SebTheis's Nuka Girl and the heels were weird so after starting remixing her with a new backpack I got a bit carried away and replaced her legs with shapelier ones, redid a hand, remade the collar from scratch, replaced her face, redid the suit sockets, and the buckles and tried to give her a few more curves and sharper clothes, though damn difficult in meshmixer. I've also scaled her feet slightly bigger so that it has a better chance of being printable.

The Factorio locomotive made into a keychain! each piece is ~33mm long with the holes in the center being 2mm across

I used 7 strand steel beading wire. to thread through the pieces then leaving a little under the length of the last wagon extra to loop back into opposite holes. I jammed a piece of copper wire in to keep it from pulling back out and put a nice gob of super glue on the back to keep it from pulling out.

The length is basically as long as you want it to be.

I added the Raw models without holes for those making minis (the bottom isnt totally flat)

The smallest of the 4 Gargant types the mekboy fits on the standard gw 40mm base or old monster base.

I did have some trouble printing this model on my ender 3. i found some of the bits too small and cleanup to be a pain. So i have included simplified versions of the parts that gave me the most trouble. mainly the large arm, (with or without pistons) the buzz saw (wide for PLA printers) and the grabber claw 2 or 3 fingers.
The arms can be flipped so you can swap the chain saw and guns as you like. i have made the arms quit long compaired to the origional as i never liked the stubby little arms of the metal model.
Also you can flip the big weapon mount if you want the big arm on the right side, or print one each shoulder and have a 4 armed gargant

I have made my own versions of the other gargants that are avaiable here:

The stamps are 2 inches by 2 inches, and will tile pretty well. There are slight lines around the stamped texture due to variations in pressure. I think I might do rollers next time to fix this. In the photo I stretched the circle cobbles stamp to 2.5 inches to make Wyloch style 1.25" grid.

To use, press firmly into foam with your hand and maybe a heavy flat bottomed object if you have trouble applying enough force manually.

This is inspired by the original Kev Adams 1990's era gargant with the rounded belly and arm and shoulder weapons.

some of the notable changes I made to the original design was the placement of the feed, rather than underneath they are to either side of the body, Another change was how I mounted the Buzz saw, I wanted it to look like it had a greater range of movement the 3d change was to the belly gun mount the original left huge holes in the belly that could be seen through during games, so I have added a big mantlet that I think gives the gargant a more solid look.

Also a minor tweak i widened the balcony on the back so now you can add infantry models there, but if you intend to do this do it before gluing the top body to the mid body.
With the modificatiosn its a little wider than the old model, and best mounted on a games workshop 80mm or reaper miniatures 75mm base. I have included a simple printable base id you don't have either of these sizes to hand

theoreticly you could scale this up for Titanicus, you would need to print at about 150%, priniting full size for 40k may be 2 difficult unless you cut up the hull parts or happen to have a huge print bed


You can add extra weapons from this selection here, Please mesage me if i have forgotten a weapon, i think i added all of them.
https://www.thingiverse.com/thing:3196923

Also please visit my facebook group
https://www.facebook.com/Redstarkits/

Description :

 1

 5
 6
 7
 8
 9
10

12
13
14
15

This is my punt at creating a high quality cobblestone textured rolling pin for making larger areas or roads for your scenic (28mm) terrain.

The image is of my test-print (cut down using meshmixer). The actual model is 6 inches wide. One turn should theoretically give you a 6"x6" textured area.

It is based on a seamless (in both x & y directions) texture, so if you line it up correctly (put a mark on the side of the roller) it should produce a seamless pattern on your surface.

If you don't have a suitable paint roller handle, try using a screwdriver for the axis.

For foam you need quite high pressure to get a good pattern. Another standard medium is air-dry polymer clay on MDF or plastic card. Let the clay dry for 10mins then use the roller. Use an old toothbrush to keep it clean.

I print at 0.1mm to get best texture results, but your call!

Good luck and show off your results!

PS Any tips for beer are welcomed now I'm retired!

After the fall of the Council, the Great Hunt was unleashed against anyone who seemed fit for the arcane. During these dark times, the Assassins emerged as a force of balance. "Assassination" was the term by which the vulgar referred to an unresolved crime; an Assassin was that individual capable of committing a crime and never be discovered. Little by little, their presence was becoming more frequent during the Great Hunt: people who tortured children during the night appeared dead in the morning; judges who condemned the innocent were found hanged and with horrible marks on their bodies.

In her quest for balance, the Assassin searchs within the Dark Wizard's domains looking for the means to restore Magic to it's rightfull place... and becoming a more lethal weapon against all who opose the arcane.

06/11/18 EDIT: Added the 22mm version, which is the proper scale for the game.

Simple add-on parts to modify any diecast car for any postapocalyptic racing game. Scales well with ~1:64 original Matchbox scale. Primarly designed for Gaslands but can be used for any other games as well.

Updates
---------
* **12.7.18:** Started to split this thing into multiple new things with a theme (armour, fuel tanks, etc.) for easier maintenance...
* **23.5.18:** Some very simple straight rams added (PS: forgot some that are not on the photo...).
* **22.5.18:** Motor Prototype added, prints in 3 parts to avoid overhangs (no support needed). Parts will be interchangeable in the future to allow customization and different builds.
* **17.5.18:** Some simple exhaust pipes added...
* **10.5.18:** Barrel and gas can set added. Barrels are very, very thin (1 0.4mm layer) to be able to dent them after printing with a little bit of heat...


Additional elements will be added in a timely manner...
Splitting into separate theme-based things (barrels, rams, armour, motors, etc.) was requested but this will take a little bit of time in reorganization.

[KICKSTARTER ALERT!](https://www.kickstarter.com/projects/292543184/scatterblocks)

We're currently running a Kickstarter campaign for the [extended range of our ScatterBlocks](https://www.kickstarter.com/projects/292543184/scatterblocks) (quick-assembling miniature terrain), so drop on by and drop us a pledge if you want the full range. For those of you supporting us (or thinking about supporting us) on [Patreon](https://www.patreon.com/illgottengames), all the rewards will go to our backers there as well (as we do with all our crowdfunding campaigns).

These OBJ models were designed for use in [Sculptris](http://pixologic.com/sculptris/) to give you a head-start creating gnomish characters. If you import them into [Sculptris](http://pixologic.com/sculptris/), their parts should remain separate and you can immediately begin sculpting and posing them any way you like.

If you make anything with these, let me know and post a link here in the comments section (and certainly post a remix when you have something printable). I'd love to see what you come up with!

You can find an expanding collection of compatible parts [here](https://www.thingiverse.com/dutchmogul/collections/desktop-hero-parts).

We've set up a [Patreon page](https://www.patreon.com/illgottengames) for anyone who's interested in helping to fund us so we can keep making free and open sourced games like Pocket-Tactics, Wayfarer Tactics. and others, not to mention the growing catalog of gaming miniatures that you can use for whatever you want! (Psst... we take requests and commissions...)

Enjoy!

A battleship, Light and regular cruisers, all with a demonic twist. Great for Battlefleet Gothic or other space miniatures games. These will take a bit of modeling work to clean up. Weapons inserts will fit, but may need a little filing along the sides (as they are very snug).

Fun trick, try using a flame (like from a BBQ lighter) to quickly pass over the stringy PLA filament strands strands to clear them. Just don't hold it in one place for too long otherwise you'll get melting... or possibly burning.

1/3/'18 a little update, I've improved the launch bay's slightly as I found the originals looked a little too small for the frame. I've also increased the size on the battleship by 7.5%, just to make it slightly more imposing.

A re-design of the original miniature produced by Games Workshop for their 6mm scale table top wargame, Epic 40,000 (and precessors/successors). They have since abandoned all support for Epic, so I modeled this in Autodesk Inventor for any avid wargamers who don't want to use proxies or pay through the nose for OOP official models off Ebay.

I haven't tried printing this model in an FDM printer so I can't recommend settings or methods of optimization.

Epic has been re-released as a titans-only game called Adeptus Titanicus. It is nominally 8mm scale instead of 6mm, so I suggest that anyone wanting to print this for AT scenery or to play 8mm Epic should upscale it by 125%.

These STL files are designed to equip my [Sculptris Dummies](https://www.thingiverse.com/thing:1972042). You won't be able to import these files into Sculptris, though once you get your character posed, you can align these parts in any model staging platform (MakerBot Deskto, Blender, Meshmixer, or 3D Builder are all good choices). All of these parts are also available in Andrew Stockton's awesome [Desktop Hero](https://www.kickstarter.com/projects/263291121/desktophero-free-3d-printable-character-maker) project as well (which is quite a bit easier than adjusting all the parts by hand). All of these weapons have been scaled to 28mm/Heroic scale, so they should be ready for any kind of miniature conversion if you want to print them separately.

If you make anything with these (including through Desktop Hero), let me know and post a link here in the comments section (and certainly post a remix when you have something printable). I'd love to see what you come up with!

You can find an expanding collection of compatible parts [here](https://www.thingiverse.com/dutchmogul/collections/desktop-hero-parts).

We've set up a [Patreon page](https://www.patreon.com/illgottengames) for anyone who's interested in helping to fund us so we can keep making free and open sourced games like Pocket-Tactics, Wayfarer Tactics. and others, not to mention the growing catalog of gaming miniatures that you can use for whatever you want! Enjoy!

Onece I thought: can I make a model using so simple reference as a few pixel graphics images? I've liked the game Dune 2 - The Building of a Dynasty made by Westwood Studios in it's time and always liked it's mentat/building menu units' images. I think they were a very good designed things. So I thought it would be a nice challenge to complete :)

It took a lot of time to make a model actually, since I didn't attend to it too much. I didn't like the way how the front and the back of the tank's body looked like, but overally the model looks nice anyway. I also thought maybe to make textures for the model and finally remake an original Dune 2 "slide", but got a bit lazy to do so.

But the case I was lazy was that I wanted actually to print this model and paint it. I don't have much experience in painting tanks, since I'm too far away from stand modeling, but, anyway, I just wanted to make a good try. You can see the actual photos of the result and decide it for yourself.

By the way, I've tried to find a lead Dune 2 designer - Aaron E Powell - to show the tank. It ought to be an interesting salute after 20 years, but, alas, didn't manage to find him - found three of his sites with (C)2014 stated there and with no reply for theese sites' local message system.

Hope people who still remember that nice old game will like the fact it is now possible to look it in real 3D and even being able to print it :)

Also there is an article (though in Russian) how I've made this tank. It includes more WIP images, just in case someone would be interested:
http://3dtoday.ru/blogs/harh/tank-of-dunes-or-sand-stone-axe/

-------------------------------------------------RULES-------------------------------------------------------
For a standard 50 point build you'll want to build using a combination of units and spell cards. For a starting build, consider the following: Guild Initiate x1, Guild Apprentice x1, Guild Mage x1, Guild Guard x1, Grand Librarian x1 (totaling 32 points + 18 points worth of spell cards, Stonework tile x4, Water tile x2. The Fortress, Ruins, or Township features are good tactical/thematic choices for this build.

Inverted-color images of the rules cards are available [here](http://i.imgur.com/Du3YYXf.png), [here](http://i.imgur.com/S9i78Sg.png), [here](http://i.imgur.com/IMIMQly.png), and [here](http://i.imgur.com/QJlHoJQ.png) if you want something a little less ink-intensive.

SETTING UP

To begin, each player builds a force by selecting a number of units that total 50 points or less. For a larger game, you and your opponent could agree on a higher point total.

Next, each player chooses 6 tiles and all of the tiles are dropped into a bag and shuffled. Then, players agree (randomly, if you choose) on a “central feature” tile and then each choose a feature for themselves. (features are the 3-dimensional tiles such as Forest, Highlands, Villages, et cetera). Draw a single tile from the bag and place the central feature into that tile. Rolling off to see who goes first, players take turns drawing tiles from the bag and placing them adjacent to one another in whatever configuration they wish. Once all of the tiles have been placed, each player (in turn order decided by the roll-off) places their chosen feature so that it is both as many tiles away from the center and from one another as possible.

Once the map has been generated, players place up to three units of their choice (as many as they can fit) either in or adjacent to their chosen feature using the rolled-off turn order. You may only ever have a single unit occupy a tile or feature. Once this is finished, game play begins starting with the last player to place their units.

PLAYING THE GAME

Each turn, a player may either move one of their units, use one of their units to assault an enemy unit, or deploy a new unit onto the map.

MOVING: When activating a unit to move, they may do so into any unoccupied tile adjacent to them. If an allied unit is in an adjacent tile, the moving unit may “hop” over that unit to get to an open tile adjacent to their ally. A unit may only hop a single ally per move. Some features (Forests, Highlands, Villages, et cetera) have special movement considerations that will be listed on their rules card. Spaces that do not contain a tile may not be moved into.

SWIFT UNITS: Units with this symbol on their rules card may perform a number of bonus moves equal to the numeric value listed to the side when they are activated to move.

FLYING UNITS: Units with this symbol on their rules card may perform a number of bonus moves equal to the numeric value listed to the side when they are activated to move and may hop over enemy units as though they were allies when doing so.

ASSAULTS: When activating a unit to assault an adjacent enemy, each player tests their units Offense (OFF) by rolling their red dice and defense (DEF) by rolling their blue dice. A unit will have between zero and three of each kind of dice as shown on their rules cards. The assault occurs in three phases:

Roll Phase- All dice are rolled simultaneously.

Bump Phase- Some units have “bumps,” a numeric value with a + listed under either their OFF or DEF dice. Starting with the player initiating the assault, each player may take turns using a single bump. Each bump may adjust a single die result (either OFF or DEF) up by its value (though a single die may not go higher than 6). Some units may have multiple bump values listed under their dice or granted by special abilities or terrain effects.

Re-Roll Phase- Starting with the player initiating the assault, each player takes turns using any re-rolls they are afforded, either by special abilities or terrain/unit placement. Each re-roll allows the player to re-roll one of their die results (OFF or DEF). A unit that has adjacent allies is benefiting from “support” and gains one re-roll per ally. A unit also gains a single re-roll when occupying their “favored terrain” (a terrain tile or feature that is shown on their rules card).

Tally Phase- Each player checks their OFF results and checks them against the opponent's DEF results. Starting with the highest OFF die, compare it to the highest enemy DEF die. If the results are a tie, move on to the next highest. If a single OFF die can't be matched or beat by value from the enemy's DEF, that enemy is “defeated” and is removed from the map and placed in the victorious player's captures (a space to the side of the map on that player's side). If the OFF cannot beat the enemy DEF values, that unit is safe. Note that, because all dice are rolled at once, it is possible for both units to defeat one another simultaneously.

RANGED ATTACKS: Units with this symbol on their rules card may make assaults against units that are an extra number of tiles away equal to the numeric value listed to the side. Count through the closest route to get to the target before making a ranged assault. Features and enemy units block line of sight (except when a Flying unit is targeted or is making the assault) and empty spaces (spaces without a tile) always block line of sight. If a unit being assaulted is not capable of meeting the range requirements to the attacker, they may not roll their OFF dice for that assault.

DEPLOYMENT: In place of activating one of your units already on the map, you may choose a unit from your reserves (any of the units you didn't put on the map at the start of the game that haven't been captured by enemies) and place them adjacent to any feature on the map that you control (provided the space is unoccupied). If no such tile exists, you may not deploy a unit until one opens up.

Any player may, in place of performing a regular move action, move a piece into an occupied feature tile to return that unit to reserves. Similarly, a unit that is occupying a feature may move into that feature to return to reserves, though you then cede control of the feature by doing so.

TYPES

Listed directly beneath a unit's name are a number of “types” (Human, Elf, Robot, et cetera). These types have no effect on their own, though are referenced by certain abilities and terrain effects that may either be beneficial or detrimental to the unit.

HAZARDS

Some terrain tiles and features contain hazards. These are special effects that occur when a unit is moved into that tile. Units that are deployed into a tile with hazard effects ignore them, as do units that have that tile type as their favored terrain.

WATER: A unit moving into a Water tile must succeed at a DV 5 DEF test or be defeated immediately after doing so.

If a feature is placed in a terrain tile, the tile counts as that feature rather than the terrain type, and therefore negates any hazard effects native to the terrain type.

VICTORY CONDITIONS

A player achieves victory as soon as their opponent (or opponents) cannot activate or deploy any units. Alternately, victory is secured the moment any single player controls all features on the map.

USING SPELL CARDS

When using spell cards in your force, each card selected is subtracted from your force point total. For example, if your are including the Fireball spell (which costs 2 points as indicated at the bottom of the card) in a standard 50-point force, it takes up 2 of those 50 points. You may use any number of spell cards in your force build provided you can afford their point cost and may use duplicates of the same spell if you like.

At the start of the game, shuffle all of your spell cards into a deck, then draw up to five of them. At the start of each turn, you may draw back up to five if you have less than five cards in your hand. You may not have more than five cards in your hand at any time.

Any unit with the Mage type may use spell cards, following the instructions when doing so. After a spell card has been used, place it in a discard pile designated to the side of the deck. Discarded cards may not be used again (except with the use of special abilities like the 'Grand Grimoire' ability possessed by the Archmage).

It's Sgt. Scalesby, and he's here to help you scale your models for miniature gaming!

This isn't a model for printing, per se, but something you can upload into your staging program (I use MakerBot Desktop for this stuff) to help you make sure your characters, tanks, giant robots, et cetera are at the right size for the scale of game for which you're printing them. Scalesby here represents a tall (6') human, with the scale value coming up to his eye line (an archaic rule in scaling for wargames due to confusion brought on by tall hats... yeah). Anyway, definitely use a give-or-take approach, especially if your models are taller or shorter than the mark. Hope this is helpful!

Stroganoff made some beautiful Leman Russ models in 6mm for games like Epic. That's great and all, but a 10 Russ company has 9 Main Battle Tanks, and one Vanquisher in NetEA. And then there's the Demolishers you can attach in 3s. What's a gamer to do?

Make them!

Here you will find some variant turrets for Leman Russ chassis tanks. Demolisher, Vanquisher, Punisher, Conqueror, Executioner, Eradicator, Exterminator (come on GeeDubs, those names are just confusing) The Exterminator could double as an Annihilator.

There are two Punisher turrets. A 6 barrel and a 4 barrel. The 4 prints cleaner, but the 6 did not feel as flimsy to me. So your milage may vary there. Could have been my post-processing.

These have been printed on an SLA printer. Some of these items are not going to print well on an FDM printer. The Punisher and Exterminator come to mind. I might edit the Eradicator a little as it has little supports on the side which might be too thin/separated from the main barrel. It won't really affect printing, but might not form well in the process.

I wasn't intending on doing a follow up piece to my previous sculpt, but got inspired by beardly goodness.

Character sculpt at relatively low, medium and high and highest poly counts.

File will need support material, but the top half of the model has been successfully printed on an UP printer, needing relatively low amount of supports. Should work great on a resin/SLA printer. Hoping to do a full test print soon, will see if a manually modelled support structure is needed for the hair. Was just too keen to make the file public and see what the community does with it. :)

Edit: Confirmed printable on FDM! Thanks ichibey!

Edit 2: Uploaded second option for all detail levels with a single shell, mostly to fix issues with the eyes. Thanks 3DWP! Zip file contains all detail levels.

Sculpted in Zbrush, preview renders in Blender, final check and stl file saved from Netfabb.

Approximate poly counts
Low = 137,000 tris
Med = 372,000 tris
High = 965,000 tris
Highest = 2,804,000 tris
